10.name: PAGE_MODE
10.helpText:
Select the page mode for this page.

#LOV_VALUES#

Note that options Modal and Non-Modal Dialog will only be available for selection where the current application theme contains a default Dialog Page Template.

lovValues.helpText: The page is presented as a normal Oracle APEX application page.

The page is presented as a modal dialog.
A modal dialog is an overlay window positioned within the viewport, which remains active and focused until the end user dismisses (closes) it. The underlying page is grayed out and the end user is prevented from interacting with the rest of the page until the dialog is closed.

The page is presented as a non-modal dialog.
A non-modal dialog is an overlay window positioned within the viewport, where the end user can interact with the dialog, and content on the page that launched the dialog. A non-modal dialog can be used when the requested information is not essential to continue, work can continue elsewhere while the window is still open.

1003.name: DATABASE_OPERATION
1003.helpText:
Assign a Database Operation to this HTTP operation. The database operation is important for Oracle APEX components to work with the REST Data Source. An Oracle APEX component is assigned a REST Data Source (and not an operation), thus it looks up the HTTP operation based on the required database operation.

  • Visualization components like report, charts, CSS calendar and others, will always use the HTTP operation assigned to the Fetch Rows database operation. APEX_EXEC.OPEN_WEB_SOURCE_QUERY will also use the Fetch Rows database operation.
  • When a Form component inserts, updates or deletes rows, it will use the operations assigned to the Insert Row, Update Row or Delete Row, respectively. In PL/SQL, APEX_EXEC.OPEN_WEB_SOURCE_DML_CONTEXT is the equivalent to a form.
  • The Fetch Single Row database operation is used by the Form component when lost update detection or the allowed operations check is performed. The form then uses this operation to re-fetch the row from the REST service before doing the actual DML operation.
  • Operations which are not mapped to a database operation, will not be used by Oracle APEX components. Use the APEX_EXEC.EXECUTE_WEB_SOURCE PL/SQL procedure to execute these from a PL/SQL context.


For instance, the report or chart components of Oracle APEX require a collection of rows. When working with a REST Data Source, Oracle APEX will look up the Fetch rows database operation and execute the assigned HTTP operation at runtime. A Form will look for Insert Row, Update Row or Delete Row database operations.

Each database operation can be assigned only once within a REST Data Source. This abstraction of the Oracle APEX component from the actual HTTP operation allows to create a new operation with different behavior and assign that to the database operation. All components will then transparently use the new HTTP operation.

There is no restriction on which HTTP operation (GET, POST, PUT, DELETE) can be mapped to which database operation. A POST HTTP operation can be mapped to the Fetch Rows database operation. However, for clarity and maintainability, it is recommended to design REST APIs to use GET for fetch operations and to use POST, PUT, DELETE to change data.

101.name: FIELD_TEMPLATE
101.helpText:
Select a label template to define the appearance and layout of this item label.

Label templates are defined in the application theme. When an item is created, the template is automatically set to the default item template defined in the current theme.

Many themes contain label templates for displaying required, optional, and hidden labels.
Universal Theme provides the following label templates:

Hidden
Use this when the label should not be displayed on screen. Note that Assistive Technology will still be able to read the label. Hidden is ignored for Checkbox items because a label must be shown after the checkbox.
Optional
Use this for form items that are optional. The label will be displayed to the side of the item.
Optional - Above
Use this for form items that are optional. The label will be displayed above the item.
Optional - Floating
Use this for form items that are optional. The label will be displayed inside of the input item, and will automatically shrink once the input field has a value.
Required
This label template displays a red asterisk next to the label, and is used for form items where user input is required. The label will be displayed to the side of the item.
Required - Above
This label template displays a red asterisk next to the label, and is used for form items where user input is required. The label will be displayed above the item. Item templates enable you to define the user interface attributes as part of a theme and share that definition among many page items.
Required - Floating
This label template displays a red asterisk next to the label, and is used for form items where user input is required. The label will be displayed inside of the input item, and will automatically shrink once the input field has a value. Item templates enable you to define the user interface attributes as part of a theme and share that definition among many page items.
See Also: Universal Theme Sample Application

1013.name: HTTP_METHOD
1013.helpText:
HTTP Operation or Method (GET, POST, PUT, DELETE) to be executed on the REST Web Service. The combination of URL pattern and HTTP Operation identifies the operation within a REST Data Source. A REST Data Source may contain the same URL pattern for different HTTP operations and different URL patterns for the same HTTP operation.

Following is a brief explanation of HTTP methods and their usage in REST services. Note this this is all convention - REST services should adhere to this, but real implementations can be different. Always check the documentation of the REST service you plan to access on which methods can be called and how they work.

lovValues.helpText: Fetch data from the REST service. GET is supposed to be idempotent; it's invocation does not change anything at the server side. For this reason, GET requests can be typically be cached or called multiple times. GET requests do also not have a request body in normal cases.

Typically used to create a new resource on the server. However, in practice, POST requests can do all sort of things. POST requests typically
require a request body to be sent.

Typically used to replace a new resource on the server. A request body is typically required. Note that you need to pass all attributes to the server - missing attributes are likely to be written as null or empty values.
Typically used to remove a resource on the server. A request body is typically not required.

Typically used to change a new resource on the server. Not all REST services provide PATCH endpoints. A request body, containing information on which attribute to change to which value, is required. PATCH thus allows to do partial updates on a server resource. Note that there is no standard on how the request body for a PATCH endpoint should look like - check the documentation of your REST service before invoking it.

1035.name: POST_PROC_WHERE
1035.examples:
Only include those employees which have a manager or have a job of salesman.
    ( MGR is not null or JOB = 'SALESMAN' )
1035.helpText: Enter a valid SQL where condition, used to limit the records retrieved.

1036.name: POST_PROC_ORDER_BY
1036.examples:
To show the newest hires first and those which have not been hired yet last. If the date is equal, sort them by department number.
    HIREDATE DESC NULLS LAST, DEPTNO
1036.helpText:
Enter one or more comma separated column names, including directives, to define the order in which records are retrieved.

Directives include:

  • ASC - Return column in ascending order
  • DESC - Return column in descending order
  • NULLS FIRST - Return column with no value before those with values
  • NULLS LAST - Return column with values before those with no value

1041.name: POST_PROC_SQL_QUERY
1041.examples:
Select the EMPNO, ENAME and SAL columns and filter out all rows with a SAL less then 3000.
    select EMPNO, ENAME, SAL
      from #APEX$SOURCE_DATA#
     where SAL < 3000
1041.helpText: Enter a SQL Query to transform the data retrieved from the REST Data Source. Select from the pseudo-table #APEX$SOURCE_DATA# and specify columns available in the data profile. Subquery factoring using the SQL WITH clause is not supported here.

1042.name: USE_EXTERNAL_EXPR
1042.helpText: Whether to use external Filtering or Order By expressions, which are directly passed to the REST service.

1043.name: EXTERNAL_FILTER_EXPR
1043.examples:
For an ORDS REST Service, retrieve all records with the "sal" attribute less than 3000.
{"sal": {"$lt": 3000}}
For an Oracle Cloud Applications (Saas) REST Service, retrieve all records with the "sal" attribute less than 3000.
sal < 3000
1043.helpText: Provide a filter expression to be passed to the external REST service. The expression will be passed to the remote server as-is. The syntax depends on the type of the REST Data Source. For example, Oracle REST Data Services (ORDS) expects JSON syntax while Oracle Cloud Applications (SaaS) expects a SQL-like where clause predicate using filterable attribute names.

1044.name: EXTERNAL_ORDER_BY_EXPR
1044.examples:
For an ORDS REST Service, order by the "job" attribute ascending, then by "ename", descending.
    {"job": "asc", "ename": "desc"}
For an Oracle Cloud Applications (SaaS) REST Service, order by the "job" attribute ascending, then by "ename", descending.
    job:asc,ename:desc
1044.helpText: Provide an order by expression involving one or more columns to be passed to the external REST service. The expression will be passed to the remote server as-is. The syntax depends on the type of the REST Data Source. For example, Oracle REST Data Services (ORDS) expects JSON syntax while Oracle Cloud Applications (SaaS) expects a comma-separated list of attribute names with optional direction indicator.

lovValues.helpText: The labels will display on the slices of the chart, based on the selected Label column mapping. For example, Bugs.
The labels will display as values between 0% and 100%, based on the selected Value column mapping. The value is a percentage of the total values represented on the chart. For example, 15%.
The labels will display as numeric values, based on the selected Value column mapping.
The labels will display the label and value information in the following format: label - value. For example, Bugs - 18.
The labels will display the label and percentage information in the following format: label - percentage. For example, Bugs - 15%.
The labels will display the label, value and percentage information in the following format: label - percentage ( value ). For example, Bugs - 15% ( 18 ).
The labels will display as numeric values, based on the selected Value column mapping. For example, 15% ( 18 ).

lovValues.helpText: The column will not stretch and always just use the width specified. This is useful for columns with short content like Yes/No or Numbers.
The column will always stretch, irrespective of the Stretch Report Setting set by the End User.

1048.name: JET_FILL_GAPS
1048.helpText: Specify whether gaps in your multi-series chart data should be automatically filled. This setting does not apply to single series charts or the following chart types: Bubble, Donut, Funnel, Gantt, Pie, Pyramid, Scatter, and Stock. When set to On, data densification logic introduced in Oracle APEX 5.1.3 will be applied to the chart data. When set to Off, gaps in data will not be filled and may result in inaccurate chart rendering. The default is On.

1050.name: JET_GAUGE_INNER_RADIUS
1050.helpText: Specify the inner radius of a Status Meter gauge chart with circular orientation, defined by the distance from the center of the gauge to the innermost edge of the indicator and plot area. Valid values are a percent or ratio from 0 to 1.

1051.name: JET_GAUGE_START_ANGLE
1051.helpText: Enter the start angle in degrees for the Status Meter Gauge chart with circular orientation. Positive values indicate clockwise start angle. Negative values indicate counterclockwise start angle. You may draw your circular gauge at any angle you want and change its shape according to the chosen angle. The shape of your gauge depends on 2 settings: Start Angle and Angle Extent.

1052.name: JET_GAUGE_ANGLE_EXTENT
1052.helpText: Enter the angle extent in degrees for the Status Meter Gauge chart with circular orientation. The Angle Extent is an actual angle of the circular orientation. Positive values indicate clockwise angle. Negative values indicate counterclockwise angle. You may draw your circular gauge at any angle you want and change its shape according to the chosen angle. The shape of your gauge depends on 2 settings: Start Angle and Angle Extent.

1053.name: JET_GAUGE_PLOT_AREA_COLOR
1053.examples:
Examples of major HTML color codes include -
  •   Black   #000000 RGB(0,0,0)
  •   Red   #FF0000 RGB(255,0,0)
  •   Yellow   #FFFF00 RGB(255,255,0)
  •   Lime   #00FF00 RGB(0,255,0)
  •   Green   #008000 RGB(0,128,0)
  •   Aqua   #00FFFF RGB(0,255,255)
  •   Blue   #0000FF RGB(0,255,255)
  •   Navy   #000080 RGB(0,0,128)
  •   White   #FFFFFF RGB(255,255,255)
1053.helpText:
Enter the color to be displayed for the plot area of a Status Meter Gauge chart. You can utilize &COLUMN_VALUE. substitutions. This color only applies when threshold colors have not been defined for the chart.

The color is specified using hexadecimal (hex) notation, RGB color codes, or HTML color names. Hex notation is defined as #xxyyzz (a # followed by 3 double digit hex numbers), where xx, yy, and zz represent the two character hex values for red, green and blue respectively. RGB codes are defined as RGB(xxx,xxx,xxx), where xxx is a number between 0 and 255 each representing the single 8-bit byte value for red, green, and blue respectively.

Search the internet for 'HTML Color Codes' to find the equivalent hex code or RGB code for the color you wish to utilize.

1083.name: ENABLE_FLASHBACK
1083.helpText:
Specify whether end users can utilize flashback queries for this Interactive Grid.

Flashback queries utilize the Oracle Flashback Technology and Database Point-in-Time Recovery to view data as it existed at a previous point in time. Users can only query this data, but can not rewind any data changes. How far back in time they can successfully perform a flashback query is determined by when the redo log files were last switched within the Oracle database, as this technology utilizes the RMAN backup.

1099.name: FC_COLLAPSIBLE

11.name: PAGE_TEMPLATE
11.helpText:
Select a page template to define the appearance and layout of this page.

Page templates are defined in the application theme. When a page is created, the template is automatically set to Theme Default which will render the page using the default page template defined in the current theme. Making a selection here overrides the default page template.

Many themes contain page templates with specific purposes, such as for displaying content with side columns, login page, dialog pages, and so forth.
Universal Theme provides the following page templates:

Standard
The default page template. Ideal for home pages, dashboards, large reports, and other layouts where maximum screen real-estate is desired.
Left Side Column
Provides a slot on the left side where search and filter regions can be placed.
Right Side Column
Provides a collapsible slot on the right side where action-oriented controls such as buttons or lists can be displayed.
Left and Right Side Columns
Provides both the left-side column and collapsible right-side column that is well suited for very complex pages.
Login
Used exclusively for the application login page.
Marquee
Provides a collapsible right side column and a title-bar area which contains primary information. This page template is well suited for displaying a single record which has several related reports or data. Marquee is commonly used for displaying Master-Detail relationships where a single master record is first selected from a report.
Minimal (No Navigation)
Useful for very simple pages, disclaimers, single page applications, or where navigation is not necessary.
See Also: Universal Theme Sample Application

Changes to this property may not be seen right away because the set of charts the user has shown is persisted in the browser session. To see the effect of changes to this property reset the report using the link Reset Regions cache control option such as with the wizard generated Reset button.

118.name: NULL_RETURN_VALUE
118.helpText: Enter the value to be returned if the NULL value is selected in this list of values. If you do not provide a value, the item value is left as null when the NULL option is selected from this list.

1180.name: CARD_ACTION_TYPE
1180.helpText:
Select the type of action to add to the card component.

Note: You can define multiple actions of the same type. However, only button actions are rendered multiple times. For all other action types, the first TRUE display condition gets rendered, and the rest are ignored.

Display conditions can be defined based on the column values if execution condition is set to check for each row.

lovValues.helpText: Adds button to the card.
Adds link to the full card. Usually, one of this action type should be defined.
Adds link to the card title. Usually, one of this action type should be defined.
Adds link to the card subtitle. Usually, one of this action type should be defined.
Adds link to the card media. Usually, one of this action type should be defined.

1181.name: CARD_ACTION_POSITION
1181.helpText: Determines where the button is positioned on the card.

1182.name: ACTION_LINK_TARGET_TYPE
1182.helpText: Select the action to be performed when the specified action type is clicked.

lovValues.d: Redirect to Page in this Application
lovValues.helpText: Redirect to a page in the current application, with optional additional attributes for resetting pagination, setting the request value, clearing cache and setting item values, on the target page.

lovValues.d: Redirect to Page in a different Application
lovValues.helpText:
Redirect to a page in a different application, with optional additional attributes for resetting pagination, setting the request value, clearing cache and setting item values, on the target page.

Note: Redirecting to a page in different application relies on deep linking being enabled in the target application. To enable deep linking, go to the application's Security attributes and enable Deep Linking.
Redirect to the target URL you specify.

1183.name: CARDS_PER_PAGE
1183.helpText: Enter the number of cards to display per page.

1185.name: BUTTON_DISPLAY_TYPE
1185.helpText: Select a button display type to define the appearance of this button.

lovValues.helpText: Displays the button label only.
Displays an icon only.
Displays an icon next to the button label.

1186.name: CARD_ICON_CSS_CLASSES_REQUIRED
1186.helpText:
Enter the classes for the icon you want to add to the component. You may add multiple classes by separating them with spaces.

If your theme uses Font APEX then review the Universal Theme Sample Application to view available icons and modifiers.

1187.name: CARD_PK_COLUMN1
1187.helpText: Select the first primary key column from the region source. If the primary key of this table has more than two columns, you must select the ROWID column. If the region is set to display scroll pagination, the primary key is used to avoid displaying duplicate rows. If the region displays an image from a BLOB column, the primary key is used to get the image.

1188.name: CARD_PK_COLUMN2
1188.helpText: Only select the second primary key column if the primary key for your region source has two columns. If you select ROWID for the first primary key column, you should not populate this column. If the region is set to display scroll pagination, the second primary key is used to avoid displaying duplicate rows. If the region displays an image from a BLOB column, the second primary key is used to get the image.

1189.name: CARD_PK_COLUMN1_REQUIRED
1189.helpText: Select the first primary key column from the region source. If the primary key of this table has more than two columns, you must select the ROWID column. If the region is set to display scroll pagination, the primary key is used to avoid displaying duplicate rows. If the region displays an image from a BLOB column, the primary key is used to get the image.

119.name: CASCADING_LOV_PARENT_ITEMS
119.helpText:
Enter page or application items that trigger the refresh of this list of values. For multiple items, separate each item name with a comma. You can type in the name or pick from the list of available items. If you pick from the list, and there is already text entered, then a comma is placed at the end of the existing text, followed by the item name returned from the list.

This list of values is refreshed whenever the value of any of the specified items are changed on this page.

You should use the page item(s) specified in this attribute within the where clause of this list of values SQL Query to restrict the values returned.

For example, if you have page items for Car Make and Model, you could specify Car Make as the Cascading LOV Parent Item within the List of Values definition for Model, and use Car Make within the where clause for that list of values. Then whenever Car Make is changed, the LOV for Model is refreshed, and the list only displays values for the currently selected Car Make.

1190.name: CARD_PK_COLUMN2_REQUIRED
1190.helpText: Only select the second primary key column if the primary key for your region source has two columns. If you select ROWID for the first primary key column, you should not populate this column. If the region is set to display scroll pagination, the second primary key is used to avoid displaying duplicate rows. If the region displays an image from a BLOB column, the second primary key is used to get the image.

12.name: STANDARD_TAB_SET
12.helpText: Select a standard tab set used for this page. A standard tab set is associated with a specific page number. You can use standard tabs to link users to a specific page.

120.name: LOV_PAGE_ITEMS_TO_SUBMIT
120.helpText:
Enter column, page or application items to set into session state when the value of any of the specified Cascading LOV Parent Item(s) change on this page. For multiple items, separate each item name with a comma. You can type in the name or pick from the list of available items. If you pick from the list and there is already text entered, then a comma is placed at the end of the existing text, followed by the item name returned from the list.

You should use the page item(s) specified in this attribute within the where clause of this list of values SQL Query to restrict the values returned.

Note: The page items defined in Cascading LOV Parent Item(s) are automatically transmitted and do not need to be entered into this attribute.

121.name: CASCADING_LOV_PARENT_REQUIRED
121.helpText:
Specify under what conditions this list of values is refreshed.

If set to On the refresh call to get new values performs only when all Cascading LOV Parent Item(s) are not null. If one item is null, it is assumed that the LOV Query does not return any rows. In such cases, the select list entries are simply cleared in the browser, without doing a refresh.

If set to Off, the refresh is always performed. This option is only used if you specifically handle nullable Cascading LOV Parent Item(s) in the where clause of this list of values SQL Query. If nullable page items are not properly handled, unnecessary refresh calls are executed that never return any rows.

1219.name: FC_DISPLAY_AS
1219.helpText: Specify whether the facet will be displayed inline or in a filter dialog.

lovValues.helpText: Displays the facet inline in the facet region.
Displays the facet in a filter dialog.

122.name: LOV_SQL
122.examples:
Display department name, set department number
select dname  as d,
       deptno as r
  from dept
 order by 1
122.helpText:
Enter the SQL query definition to populate this list of values. Generally list of value queries are of the form:

select [displayValue],
       [returnValue]
  from ...
 where ...
 order by ...

Each column selected must have a unique name or alias. Oracle recommends using an alias on any column that includes an SQL expression.

1221.name: MULTI_VALUE_TYPE
1221.helpText: Determines whether the Source Column contains multiple values, and how these are encoded.

lovValues.helpText:
Column contains values as a delimited list.

APEX,SQL,PL/SQL

Use the APEX_STRING.SPLIT function for processing, as in the following example:

select column_value from apex_string.split ( :ITEM_NAME, ',' );

The Source column contains a JSON array of scalar values. Oracle APEX will raise error messages if the column contains invalid JSON syntax.

["APEX", "SQL", "PL/SQL"]

Use the JSON_TABLE SQL function for processing, as in the following example:

select
    element
from
    json_table ( :ITEM_NAME, '$[*]'
        columns
            element varchar2 path '$'
    );

1222.name: MULTI_VALUE_SEPARATOR
1222.examples:
Normal characters:
,
:
Control Characters:
Tab (ASCII: 9) 
\t
Linefeed (ASCII: 10) 
\n
Other Characters:
Use a Unicode encoding value of the form '\xxxx' where 'xxxx' is the hexadecimal value of a character in UCS-2 encoding format.
Start of Heading (ASCII: 1) 
\0001
"@"-Symbol (ASCII: 64) 
\0040
1222.helpText: Identifies the character which separates values from each other. Note that the " (double-quote) and \ (backslash) characters are not supported as a Value Separator, also not in the \xxxx format.

1223.name: MULTI_VALUE_TRIM_SPACE
1223.helpText:
Whether to trim leading and trailing whitespace from individual values after splitting.

APEX:SQL:Spatial :Oracle Text: Data Warehouse
APEX :SQL:Data Warehouse
Trim Whitespace disabled leads to the following individual values counted:
"APEX":            1
"APEX ":           1
"SQL":             2
"Spatial":         1
"Oracle Text":     1
"Data Warehouse":  1
" Data Warehouse": 1
Trim Whitespace enabled leads to the following individual values counted:
"APEX":            2
"SQL":             2
"Spatial":         1
"Oracle Text":     1
"Data Warehouse":  2

Note that trimming whitespace can significantly impact query performance. For larger data sets, consider data cleansing instead.

1224.name: FC_MULTI_VALUE_COMBINATION
1224.helpText: Specify how to combine individual values when filtering.

lovValues.helpText: Values will be combined using "OR"; thus the result will be the union set of individual values.
Values will be combined using "AND"; thus the result will be the intersection of all individual values.

1226.name: SUGGESTIONS_TYPE
1226.helpText:
Select how suggestions are determined for this filter.

Note: The values provided are still checked against the visible entries of the List of Values and will only be used if there is a match. If a value is not found it will be skipped and the next one is checked.

lovValues.helpText: Picks the first visible entry from the List of Values.
Comma delimited list of values.
Values are returned from the SQL Query entered.

1227.name: SUGGESTIONS_STATIC_VALUES
1227.helpText:
Enter a comma delimited list of static values used as the source for the suggestions.

Note: The order in which the values are specified is used to determine the order they should get displayed.

1228.name: SUGGESTIONS_SQL_QUERY
1228.helpText:
Enter the SQL Query used as the source for the suggestions.

Note: The order in which the values are returned is used to determine the order they should get displayed.

123.name: ELEMENT_FIELD_ALIGNMENT
123.helpText: Select the alignment of the item within the HTML table cell that surrounds it.

1230.name: SHOW_SUGGESTIONS_LABEL
1230.helpText: Specify whether to show the label of the filter or only the value in the Suggestion Chip. Hide the label if the suggested value is self-explaining, for example, an order status.

1231.name: DEPENDING_ON_SFILTER
1231.helpText: Select the associated Filter which should be checked to decide if the current Filter should be displayed.

1232.name: DEPENDING_ON_SFILTER_GRP_ITEM
1232.helpText: Select the associated checkbox which should be checked to decide if the current checkbox should be displayed.

1233.name: SFILTER_GROUP
1233.helpText: Select the filter group to which this checkbox is associated.

1234.name: CASCADING_LOV_PARENT_FILTER
1234.helpText: Select a Filter that triggers the refresh of this list of values.

1235.name: SHOW_CURRENT_FACET_LABEL
1235.helpText: Specify whether to display the facet label next to its selected value(s) in the list of current facets. Hide the label if the selected value is self-explaining, for example, an order status.

1238.name: SOURCE_QUERY_ORDER_BY_TYPE
1238.helpText: Select how this component is sorted.

lovValues.helpText: Based on the ORDER BY clause entered into Order By Clause.
Based on the value held in session state for the Item selected.

1239.name: SOURCE_QUERY_ORDER_BY_ITEM
1239.examples:
To show the newest hires first and those which have not been hired yet last. If the date is equal, sort them by department number.
HIREDATE DESC NULLS LAST, DEPTNO
1239.helpText:
Enter multiple Order By Clauses that can be picked by end-users. Each can contain one or more comma-separated column names, including directives, to define the order in which records are retrieved.

Directives include:

  • ASC - Return column in ascending order
  • DESC - Return column in descending order
  • NULLS FIRST - Return column with no value before those with values
  • NULLS LAST - Return column with values before those with no value

124.name: ELEMENT_WIDTH
124.helpText: Enter the width of the form element to be used to display this item.

1241.name: POST_PROC_ORDER_BY_TYPE
1241.helpText: Select how this component is sorted.

lovValues.helpText: Based on the ORDER BY clause entered into Order By Clause.
Based on the value held in session state for the Item selected.

1242.name: POST_PROC_ORDER_BY_ITEM
1242.examples:
To show the newest hires first and those which have not been hired yet last. If the date is equal, sort them by department number.
HIREDATE DESC NULLS LAST, DEPTNO
1242.helpText:
Enter multiple Order By Clauses that can be picked by end-users. Each can contain one or more comma-separated column names, including directives, to define the order in which records are retrieved.

Directives include:

  • ASC - Return column in ascending order
  • DESC - Return column in descending order
  • NULLS FIRST - Return column with no value before those with values
  • NULLS LAST - Return column with values before those with no value

1243.name: POST_PROC_ORDER_BY_ITEM2
1243.examples:
To show the newest hires first and those which have not been hired yet last. If the date is equal, sort them by department number.
HIREDATE DESC NULLS LAST, DEPTNO
1243.helpText:
Enter multiple Order By Clauses that can be picked by end-users. Each can contain one or more comma-separated column names, including directives, to define the order in which records are retrieved.

Directives include:

  • ASC - Return column in ascending order
  • DESC - Return column in descending order
  • NULLS FIRST - Return column with no value before those with values
  • NULLS LAST - Return column with values before those with no value

1244.name: EXTERNAL_ORDER_BY_TYPE
1244.helpText: Select how this component is sorted.

lovValues.helpText: Based on the REST service order by expression entered into External Order By.
Based on the value held in session state for the Item selected.

1245.name: EXTERNAL_ORDER_BY_ITEM
1245.examples:
For an ORDS REST Service, order by the "job" attribute ascending, then by "ename", descending.
{"job": "asc", "ename": "desc"}
For an Oracle Cloud Applications (SaaS) REST Service, order by the "job" attribute ascending, then by "ename", descending.
job:asc,ename:desc
1245.helpText: Provide an order by expression involving one or more columns to be passed to the external REST service. The expression will be passed to the remote server as-is. The syntax depends on the type of the REST Data Source. For example, Oracle REST Data Services (ORDS) expects JSON syntax while Oracle Cloud Applications (SaaS) expects a comma-separated list of attribute names with optional direction indicator.

1246.name: SOURCE_QUERY_STATIC_ORDER_BY
1246.examples:
To show the newest hires first and those which have not been hired yet last. If the date is equal, sort them by department number.
    HIREDATE DESC NULLS LAST, DEPTNO
1246.helpText:
Enter one or more comma separated column names, including directives, to define the order in which records are retrieved.

Directives include:

  • ASC - Return column in ascending order
  • DESC - Return column in descending order
  • NULLS FIRST - Return column with no value before those with values
  • NULLS LAST - Return column with values before those with no value

1247.name: EXTERNAL_STATIC_ORDER_BY_EXPR
1247.examples:
For an ORDS REST Service, order by the "job" attribute ascending, then by "ename", descending.
    {"job": "asc", "ename": "desc"}
For an Oracle Cloud Applications (SaaS) REST Service, order by the "job" attribute ascending, then by "ename", descending.
    job:asc,ename:desc
1247.helpText: Provide an order by expression involving one or more columns to be passed to the external REST service. The expression will be passed to the remote server as-is. The syntax depends on the type of the REST Data Source. For example, Oracle REST Data Services (ORDS) expects JSON syntax while Oracle Cloud Applications (SaaS) expects a comma-separated list of attribute names with optional direction indicator.

125.name: ELEMENT_MAX_CHARACTERS
125.helpText: Enter the maximum number of characters users can type into this item.

126.name: ELEMENT_HEIGHT
126.helpText: Enter the height (approximate number of rows) for textareas, shuttles, multi select lists, and any plug-in Item types that support the Has Height Attribute attribute.

127.name: ELEMENT_VALUE_PLACEHOLDER
127.helpText:
Enter hint text displayed in this item when no value for that item is entered. Once any text is entered into the item, the hint is removed.

This placeholder attribute specifies a short hint that can be used to describe the expected value of a page item. Such hints are useful for providing a sample value, or an example of the expected format, or instructions such as: Search on title, description, and tag. For accessibility reasons, this attribute should not be used as an alternative to a well defined, meaningful label.

Attention: This is a HTML5 feature and only works in modern browsers! Older browsers do not display the text entered into this attribute.

128.name: ADVANCED_CSS_CLASSES
128.examples:
Add the CSS classes articlenumber and highlight to the HTML tag of the component
articlenumber highlight
128.helpText: Enter additional space delimited CSS classes to be included in the component.

129.name: CUSTOM_ATTRIBUTES
129.helpText:
Enter additional space delimited attributes to be included in the item tag.
For the HTML CLASS attribute, Oracle recommends using the dedicated CSS Classes attribute.

13.name: TITLE
13.helpText: Enter the page title. The page title is displayed in the title bar of the browser window.

130.name: ELEMENT_OPTION_HTML_ATTRIBUTES
130.helpText: Enter additional space-delimited attributes for the HTML table cell used to display each individual option in a radio group or set of check boxes.

131.name: ELEMENT_PRE_TEXT
131.helpText:
Enter additional attributes displayed before the HTML table cell that displays each individual option in a radio group or set of check boxes. You can include HTML, JavaScript, and shortcuts.

You can reference the following substitution strings:

#CURRENT_FORM_ELEMENT#
Obtains the name of the HTML form element that this page item is associated with.
#CURRENT_ITEM_NAME#
Obtains the name of the current page item.

132.name: ELEMENT_POST_TEXT
132.helpText:
Enter additional attributes displayed after the HTML table cell that displays each individual option in a radio group or set of check boxes. You can include HTML, JavaScript, and shortcuts.

You can reference the following substitution strings:

#CURRENT_FORM_ELEMENT#
Obtains the name of the HTML form element that this page item is associated with.
#CURRENT_ITEM_NAME#
Obtains the name of the current page item.

133.name: SOURCE_USED
133.helpText:
Select which value takes precedence, the value from session state or the item source value.

For items with the source type Database Column, select Always, replacing any existing value in session state unless you do not want the associated row fetch operation to populate the item if the page branches back to itself. For other source types you must decide, based on how the page is used, whether the previously sourced value is displayed, or if the source type is applied anew for each page view.

lovValues.d: Always, replacing any existing value in session state
Only when current value in session state is null

134.name: SOURCE_TYPE
134.helpText:
Select the source type the value of this item is based on.

Note: If Source: Used is set to Only when current value in session state is null, the source will not be utilized if a value has been set into session state for this item.

lovValues.helpText: Set to the text entered into Static Value.
Set to the column value entered in Database Column, that is retrieved from a built-in fetch row process.
Set to the value held in session state for the Item selected.
Set to the first value returned from the SQL Query entered.

Set to multiple values returned from the SQL Query. The format of what is returned is determined by the current item's Multiple Values setting. If Multiple Values is set to Delimited Values, the value will be a single concatenated list separated by the defined Separator. If Multiple Values is set to JSON Array, the value will be a JSON Array of the values. If Multiple Values is set to No or the item does not support multiple values, then the value is a single concatenated list separated by a colon.
Set to the value that results from executing the Expression entered.
Set to the value returned from the Function Body entered.
Set to the value of the Preference entered.
Set to null as no value specified.

135.name: SOURCE_STATIC_VALUE
135.helpText: Enter the static value used as the source for this item value.

136.name: SOURCE_QUERY
136.helpText: Enter the SQL Query used as the source for this item value. If more than one row is returned then the value of the first row is used.

137.name: SOURCE_QUERY_COLON
137.helpText: Enter the SQL Query that returns one or more rows to be used as the source for this item value. If the result contains multiple rows, then the format of what is returned is determined by the current item's Multiple Values setting. If Multiple Values is set to Delimited Values, the value will be a single concatenated list separated by the defined Separator. If Multiple Values is set to JSON Array, the value will be a JSON Array of the values. If Multiple Values is set to No or the column does not support multiple values, then the value is a single concatenated list separated by a colon.

138.name: SOURCE_ITEM
138.helpText:
Enter the page or application item used as the source for this item value.
You can type in the name or pick from the list of available items.

14.name: CURSOR_FOCUS
14.helpText: Specify whether the cursor is focused when first entering the page.

lovValues.helpText: The cursor focus is placed on the first field on the page using JavaScript, generated by the Oracle APEX engine.

The cursor is not focused and no JavaScript is generated.
Select this option if the generated JavaScript conflicts with custom JavaScript.

140.name: TASK_VALUE_TYPE
140.helpText: Select how this parameter is populated.

lovValues.helpText: Set to the text entered into Static Value.
Set to the value held in session state for the Item selected.
Set to the first value returned from the SQL Query entered.
Set to the value that results from executing the Expression entered.
Set to the value returned from the Function Body entered.
Set to the value of the Preference entered.
Set to null as no value specified.

1402.name: FC_ACTIONS_FILTER
1402.helpText: Specify whether the action Filter is displayed on the facet context menu to allow the user to toggle the client-side filtering On and Off, the user setting will be saved in session storage. The action will be disabled if the number of facet values is less than the value of Maximum Displayed Entries.

141.name: SOURCE_DB_COLUMN
141.helpText:
Enter the case sensitive database column name used as the source for this item value.

This column must exist in the table specified within the built-in fetch row process defined on this page. An error is raised, and the page is not loaded, if the database column name does not exist in the referenced table. Similarly, if there is no built-in fetch row process defined and there is an item with a source type of Database Column, then an error is raised, and the page is not loaded when trying to render the page.

142.name: SOURCE_PREFERENCE
142.helpText: Enter the User Preference to be used as the source for this item value.

143.name: POST_CALCULATION_COMPUTATION
143.helpText:
Enter a PL/SQL expression to refine the value of the item.

For example, if this item is named P1_X, you could use post calculation expressions such as UPPER(:P1_X), INITCAP(:P2_Y), MIN(:P1_X, :P2_Y - 200), NVL(:P1_X, :P2_Y), or a function call such as my_func(:P1_X) to set the final value of the item. Note that these examples demonstrate that the expressions can reference the current item, or they may reference any other item in session state.

144.name: MAINTAIN_SESSION_STATE
144.helpText: Select how session state is maintained.

lovValues.helpText: Do not save state in the database. State is only available when processing the current request. When AJAX requests need to use an item, make sure to pass the item name via "Page Items To Submit".
Maintain for each session by storing the value in the database, to access it across requests.
Maintain for a user by storing the value in the database, to access it across sessions.

145.name: DEFAULT_VALUE_TYPE
145.helpText: Select a default value type for this item.

lovValues.helpText: Set to the value entered in Static value.
Set to the value returned from the session state for the Item selected.
Set to the first value returned from the SQL Query entered.

Set to multiple values returned from the SQL Query. The format of what is returned is determined by the current item's Multiple Values setting. If Multiple Values is set to Delimited Values, the value will be a single concatenated list separated by the defined Separator. If Multiple Values is set to JSON Array, the value will be a JSON Array of the values. If Multiple Values is set to No or the item does not support multiple values, then the value is a single concatenated list separated by a colon.
Set to the value returned from the Expression entered.
Set to the value returned from the Function Body entered.

Set to the value returned from the Sequence entered. This is a "special" default type: It is executed as part of the Form Region DML process and not during page load. Use this type for auto-generated primary key values, when Return Primary Key(s) after Insert cannot be used, for instance, when working with views and INSTEAD OF triggers or with database links. The sequence name is case-sensitive.

146.name: DEFAULT_VALUE_STATIC_TEXT
146.helpText: Specify a default value for this item. The default value is used when the item's value is not derived from session state and when the source value is null.

1467.name: PARTICIPANT_VALUE_TYPE
1467.helpText: Select how this participant is populated.

149.name: SHOW_QUICK_PICKS
149.helpText:
Specify whether quick picks display for this page item. Quick picks enable users to select predefined values with just one click, rather than typing in text or selecting from a list of available options.

You should specify quick picks when there is a relatively small, discrete set of common input values. There is a maximum of ten quick picks that can be defined for an item. Such user aids are especially useful when defined for an item that has a lengthy select list of available values.

15.name: JS_FILE_URLS
15.examples:
Standard file reference
/myjs/main.js
Standard file reference which loads the minified file main.min.js from /myjs/minified/ for regular page views and main.js from /myjs/ in debug mode or when running the application from App Builder.
/myjs/#MIN_DIRECTORY#main#MIN#.js
Use this syntax if the library is also used from a RequireJS require call. The define name must match what is used in the requirejs.config paths and the value must be the global symbol exposed by the library. Only applies when using RequireJS. This avoids RequireJS loading that library a second time.
[define hammerjs=Hammer]/myjs/hammer.js
Use this syntax if the file has a dependency on RequireJS. This will automatically load RequireJS before this file.
[require requirejs]/myjs/main.js
Use this syntax if the file has a dependency on Oracle JET. This will automatically load RequireJS and the Oracle JET RequireJS configuration before this file.
[require jet]/myjs/main.js
Use this syntax if the file is a JavaScript ES Module. It will add type="module" to the script tag.
[module]/myjs/main.js
Use this syntax if the file should be loaded asynchronously. It will add attribute async to the script tag.
[async]/myjs/main.js
Use this syntax if the file should only be executed after the document was been parsed. It will add attribute defer to the script tag. Note that modules are deferred by default.
[defer]/myjs/main.js
Multiple File URL directives can be provided but must be comma separated.
[module, async]/myjs/main.js
File reference using a query string in the URL referencing the application version, such that when the application is upgraded (and the version is incremented), the browser is instructed to always load the new file and ignore any previously cached files.
/myjs/main.js?version=#APP_VERSION#
15.helpText:
Enter JavaScript file URLs for code loaded on this page. Each URL must be written on a new line. If you provide a minified version of your file you can use the substitution string #MIN# to include .min or #MIN_DIRECTORY# to include minified/ in your file URL for a regular page view and an empty string if the page is viewed in debug mode or when running the application from App Builder. You also have access to the substitution string #APP_VERSION# if you want to include the application's version in the file URL.

JavaScript file URLs you enter here replaces the #PAGE_JAVASCRIPT# substitution string in the page template.

Each file URL can be prefixed with a pair of brackets ([...]) containing one or more of the following directives. See the examples for details.

  • module
  • defer
  • async
  • define
  • require requirejs
  • require jet

Note: You do not need to include opening or closing script tags. Just specify the URL.

1529.name: MAP_REGION_STATUS_ITEM
1529.helpText:
If a page item is chosen, the map region will always maintain the current map bounding box, in GeoJSON format, as the value of this item. This is useful to connect the map to another APEX component (for instance, a classic or interactive report): the contents of the bounding box item can be used by the other component to perform a spatial query and to display only data visible on the map.

Example content of the Bounding Box Item after some map movement or zoom level change:

{
  "type": "Polygon",
  "coordinates": [[
                    [-5.499,46.380],
                    [ 8.187,46.380],
                    [ 8.187,49.550],
                    [-5.499,49.550],
                    [-5.499,46.380]]]
}

Using a Refresh Dynamic Action, the map can be connected to a report region. The report region can apply a spatial filter to show only results which are also visible on the map.

Example report query:

select [column1],
       [column2],
       ...
  from ...
 where sdo_anyinteract(
           [geometry-column],
           sdo_util.from_geojson( :[item-name-of-bounding-box-item] )
       ) = 'TRUE'
   and ...

1531.name: MAP_HAS_SPATIAL_INDEX
1531.helpText:
Enable this switch, if the underlying table has a spatial index and the map widget should use it when fetching rows from the database. In this case, the widget will only fetch rows for the current map window from the database. This provides a performance benefit when the data source contains a large amount of rows.

A spatial index can be created on an SDO_GEOMETRY column in SQL Workshop.

Note that a Spatial Index will not be used in the following situations:

  • More than one layer references the Region Source as their data source.
  • The map window is too large; that is the case when it spans more than half of the world.

1670.name: LANDMARK_TYPE
1670.helpText:
There are 8 different landmark types available to use. 7 of the 8 have specific meanings and will be suitable under certain circumstances (eg "search" for a region containing search functionality, "navigation" for a region containing navigation functionality). The final type is "region", which is suitable in the case where no specific landmark is appropriate, but where you still want to include the region as a landmark on the page.

For more information on landmarks, see Page Structure - Landmarks.

lovValues.helpText:
A banner landmark identifies application-oriented content at the beginning of each page within your APEX application. Within APEX, this will usually be everything contained within the top bar, for example application logo, name and navigation bar controls, (but this could vary depending on your application, the theme you are using, or the template).

Pages will usually only have one banner landmark, and the most common pattern for APEX pages will be for this banner landmark to come from the page template, meaning defining page regions as banner regions in APEX will likely be rare.

A complementary landmark is a supporting section of a page, designed to be complementary to the main content at a similar level in the DOM hierarchy, but remains meaningful when separated from the main content.

A contentinfo landmark is a way to identify common information at the bottom of each page of an application, typically called the "footer" of the page.

Pages will usually only have one contentinfo landmark, and the most common pattern for APEX pages will be for this contentinfo landmark to come from the page template, meaning defining page regions as contentinfo regions in APEX will likely be rare.

A form landmark identifies a region that contains a collection of elements (usually page items and buttons) that, as a whole, combine to create a form when no other named landmark is appropriate (e.g. main or search).

A main landmark identifies the primary content of the page.

Each page should have one main landmark, and the most common pattern for APEX pages will be for this main landmark to come from the page template, meaning usually there will be no need to define individual regions as main landmarks.
Navigation landmarks provide a way to identify groups (e.g. lists) of links that are intended to be used for application or page content navigation.

A region landmark is a perceivable section containing content that is relevant to a specific purpose and sufficiently important that users will likely want to be able to navigate to the section easily and to have it listed in a summary of the page. This is probably the most common landmark type for APEX regions.

The region landmark can be used to identify content that the other named landmarks do not appropriately describe.
A search landmark contains a collection of elements (usually page items and buttons) that, as a whole, combine to create search functionality to content in the application.

1671.name: LANDMARK_LABEL
1671.helpText:
Define a custom label for the landmark. Note: If no label is defined, the region title will be used as the landmark label. For more information on landmarks, see Page Structure - Landmarks.

It is important to provide good labels that truly improve user experience. Good labels are defined as follows:

  • Unique on a page, and not too long (preferably 3 words or less).
  • Accurately describe the purpose of the contents of the region, for example 'Edit Employee', or 'Useful Links'.
  • Do not use the landmark role in the label, for example the label for a navigation landmark for an application should just be 'Application', rather than 'Application Navigation', to avoid screen readers announcing 'navigation' twice.

2004.name: STATE
2004.helpText:
The state of the workflow version.

A workflow version when first created is always in the In Development state.

Once the developer is satisfied with modelling a version, they can click on Activate to move the version to the Active state.

Only one version of a workflow can be active at one time. Only one version of a workflow can be in development at one time.

If the developer activates a version and a different version of the workflow is already active, then the currently active version will be silently deactivated before moving the version to Active state.

Inactive versions cannot be used to start new workflow instances. They can only be deleted or duplicated.

When a Workflow Version is in Active state, only selected properties can be edited.

  • Activities and connections cannot be created, duplicated, or deleted.
  • Variables cannot be created, duplicated, or deleted for the version.
  • Activity Variables can be added to and deleted from the activities in the version.
  • The Type cannot be changed for activities. But the Source type and value can be changed for the version and its activities.
  • The conditions for the connections of Switch activities can be changed.
  • Workflow Participants can be added. But existing participants cannot be deleted.

When a Workflow Version is in Inactive state, none of its properties, activities, and variables can be edited.

2006.name: FROM_WORKFLOW_ACTIVITY

2007.name: TO_WORKFLOW_ACTIVITY

lovValues.helpText:
The default connection between two activities.

Every workflow activity must have one incoming and one outgoing normal connection.

The only exceptions are activities of type Workflow Start, Workflow Switch and Workflow End.

  • The Workflow Start activity cannot have any incoming connection.
  • The Workflow End activity cannot have any outgoing connection.
  • The Workflow Switch activity has conditional connections also known as branches.
  • The connection type for a branch depends on the Type of the Switch activity. It cannot be selected from here.

Every activity can have one or more error connections for handling of errors.

Every error connection must include the following properties.

  • Condition Value - This is the SQL Error Code with which the activity error is compared.
  • Condition Operator - This is operator used for the comparison.
  • Sequence - For multiple error connections, this property defines the order of comparison.

Available only if the From activity has the Due On Type attribute defined.

Not available for the Wait Activity because it already has its own timeout property.
