2025.name: WF_SOURCE_QUERY_OWNER
2025.helpText: Select the schema that owns the table.

2026.name: WF_SOURCE_QUERY_TABLE
2026.helpText:
Enter the case-sensitive table or view name. You can type in the name or pick from the list.
        The column names of the table can be used as bind variables and substitution strings to evaluate variables, participants and conditions during the execution of the activities.

2027.name: WF_SOURCE_SQL_QUERY
2027.examples:
select empno,
       ename,
       job,
       sal
  from emp
 where deptno = :DEPT_NUMBER
2027.helpText:
Enter a SQL query to read additional data.

The column-names of the query can be used as bind variables and substitution strings to evaluate variables, participants and conditions during the execution of the activities.

The result of the query should contain only one row.

If the query returns no result or more than one row then the workflow fails during execution.

21.name: HEADER_TEXT
21.helpText: Enter text or HTML you want to appear immediately following the page header and before the body content.

213.name: EXCLUDE_TITLE_FROM_TRANSLATION
213.helpText: Specify whether you want to exclude this title from translation. This attribute has no effect, except when translating the application into another language.

214.name: REGION_HTML_CODE
214.helpText: Enter the region source or content, depending on the Region Type selected.

215.name: SOURCE_PAGE_ITEMS_TO_SUBMIT
215.helpText:
Enter page or application items to be set into session state when the region is refreshed by a partial page refresh. For multiple items, separate each item name with a comma. You can type in the name or pick from the list of available items. If you pick from the list and there is already text entered, then a comma is placed at the end of the existing text, followed by the item name returned from the list.

The region can be refreshed with partial page refresh either during pagination, if Enable Partial Page Refresh is set to On), or with the Refresh action within a Dynamic Action.

These page items can then be used in the where condition of the Region Source SQL Query to restrict the query result.

216.name: SCHEMA_OVERRIDE_ITEM
216.helpText: Enter the page or application item to be used as the overriding parsing schema.  This is for internal applications only.

217.name: REGION_TEMPLATE
217.helpText:
Select a region template to define the appearance and layout of this region.

Region templates are defined in the application theme. When a region is created, the template is automatically set to the default region template defined in the current theme.

Many themes contain region templates for displaying reports, forms, alerts, buttons, collapsible (hide / show) content, login forms, and so forth.
Universal Theme provides the following region templates:

Alert
Blank with Attributes
Blank with Attributes (No Grid)
Buttons Container
Cards Container
Carousel Container
Collapsible
Content Block
Hero
Image
Inline Dialog
Inline Drawer
Inline Popup
Interactive Report
Login
Standard
Tabs Container
Title Bar
Wizard Container
See Also: Universal Theme Sample Application

218.name: ITEM_DISPLAY_POSITION
218.helpText: Select if the region components (sub regions, items, buttons) display above or below the main region content.

219.name: REGION_DISPLAY_SELECTOR
219.helpText:
Specify On if you want this region included in the Region Display Selector. This attribute is only utilized if a region type of Region Display Selector is defined and viewable on the page.

When a user clicks on a region name, included in the Region Display Selector, only the selected region shows and all other listed regions are hidden. The first entry within the Region Display Selector is Show All, which enables the user to show all of the available regions rather than only the previously selected region.

If a region is not displayable, based on the region conditions, then it is not included in the lists of regions within the Region Display Selector.

22.name: BODY_HEADER
22.helpText: Enter text or HTML you want to appear before regions that display on the running page. Text you enter here appears before the page template #BODY# substitution string.

220.name: REGION_IMAGE
220.helpText: Enter a reference to an image that displays in the upper left of the region. There is no control over the table tag used to display this image.

221.name: IMAGE_TAG_ATTRIBUTES
221.helpText: Enter custom region image attributes to be included in the image HTML. This can be used for attributes such as height or width.

222.name: CACHE_MODE
222.helpText: Select how the Oracle APEX engine can cache HTML text on the server side. If caching can be used, it emits the cached result instead of computing it again. This cuts down on expensive computation time on the server. This feature is unrelated to the browser's caching capabilities.

lovValues.helpText: Content is not cached and computed for each request.
Content is cached and utilized by all users.
Content is cached specifically for each user.
Content is cached specifically for each session.

223.name: CUSTOMIZABLE
223.helpText: Select whether display attributes in this region can be customized by the user.

lovValues.d: Customizable and Not Shown By Default

224.name: CUSTOMIZED_OPTION_NAME
224.helpText:
Enter the label for the link that displays under this region, which provides access to the region customization page.
This label only displays for regions that are customizable.

225.name: REGION_FUNCTION_RETURNING_SQL
225.prompt: PL/SQL Function Body returning SQL Query
225.helpText: Enter a PL/SQL Function that returns a SQL query that is used as the basis for this region.

226.name: BRANCH_TYPE
226.helpText:
Select the type of page branch to perform.

Redirect branches
Oracle APEX returns the new page or URL to the browser, which performs a new request before showing the resultant page. The major advantage is that the end users can refresh the page without losing context, as the browser address contains the full page URL. The disadvantage is that the browser performs an additional request to show the page.
Show Only branches
Oracle APEX immediately renders the new page as part of the current page processing, without performing another request. This has the advantage that the browser does not have to perform an additional request. The major disadvantage is that the browser address will be wwv_flow.accept. If the end users refreshes the page the browser will ask to resend the data, as the browser address is not a full page URL.

Oracle recommends that you select one of the redirect branch types to provide a better end user experience.

227.name: BRANCH_POINT
227.helpText: Select at what point in page rendering or processing this branch is executed.

lovValues.helpText: Rendering: Branches before the page renders.
Processing: Branches after submitting the page and before computation, validations and processes are executed.
Processing: Branches before validations performed.
Processing: Branches before processing performed.
Processing: Branches after processing performed.

228.name: TARGET
228.helpText: Click the Target to invoke a modal dialog. You can enter the target that is called when this branch is invoked.

229.name: BRANCH_PAGE_NUMBER
229.helpText: Enter the page to which this branch is redirected.

23.name: FOOTER_TEXT
23.helpText: Enter text or HTML that appears before the page template footer.

230.name: BRANCH_ITEM
230.helpText:
Enter the page or application item containing a page number or URL to redirect to.
This item can be set by the calling page, or by a process when the page first loads.
Specifying an item provides an easy way to dynamically set the branch for pages that are called from many other pages.

232.name: BRANCH_PLSQL
232.helpText: Enter the PL/SQL code executed by the branch. This PL/SQL procedure is responsible for invoking the necessary URL.

233.name: SAVE_STATE_BEFORE_BRANCH
233.helpText: Specify whether values in session state are saved to the database before the branch executes. It is important to set this attribute to On if you are navigating to a different application that needs to access the session state values from this application.

234.name: WHEN_BUTTON_PRESSED
234.helpText: If you want this page processing component to execute only when the specified button is clicked, select a button from the list. You can incorporate this button condition with other conditions to further refine when this page processing component executes.

235.name: VALUE_FORMAT_MASK
235.helpText: Format mask to be used to convert the value into a NUMBER, DATE and TIMESTAMP and back into a VARCHAR2. If no format mask has been specified, Oracle APEX will automatically read the format mask of the specified item.

2359.name: BUTTON_SHOW_PROCESSING
2359.helpText: Specify whether the current page is grayed-out and a 'processing' style animation is displayed during page submission. This can be useful to prevent end user action during long running operations, such as the end user attempting to re-click on the search button when the report is slow to refresh.

236.name: VALUE_PLSQL_EXPRESSION_NO_LANG
236.examples:
To return YES when the employee is in department 30 or is a manager:
case when ( :P2_DEPTNO = 30 or :P2_JOB = 'MANAGER' ) then 'YES' else 'NO' end
236.helpText: Enter the PL/SQL expression that produces a value used as the source for this parameter value.

lovValues.helpText:
Column contains values as a delimited list.

APEX,SQL,PL/SQL

Use the APEX_STRING.SPLIT function for processing, as in the following example:

select column_value from apex_string.split ( :ITEM_NAME, ',' );

The Source column contains a JSON array of scalar values. Oracle APEX will raise error messages if the column contains invalid JSON syntax.

["APEX", "SQL", "PL/SQL"]

Use the JSON_TABLE SQL function for processing, as in the following example:

select
    element
from
    json_table ( :ITEM_NAME, '$[*]'
        columns
            element varchar2 path '$'
    );

2361.name: MULTI_VALUE_SEPARATOR_OPTIONAL
2361.examples:
Normal characters:
,
:
Control Characters:
Tab (ASCII: 9) 
\t
Linefeed (ASCII: 10) 
\n
Other Characters:
Use a Unicode encoding value of the form '\xxxx' where 'xxxx' is the hexadecimal value of a character in UCS-2 encoding format.
Start of Heading (ASCII: 1) 
\0001
"@"-Symbol (ASCII: 64) 
\0040
2361.helpText: Identifies the character which separates values from each other. Note that the " (double-quote) and \ (backslash) characters are not supported as a Value Separator, also not in the \xxxx format.

2362.name: MULTI_VALUE_SEPARATOR_ALWAYS
2362.examples:
Normal characters:
,
:
Control Characters:
Tab (ASCII: 9) 
\t
Linefeed (ASCII: 10) 
\n
Other Characters:
Use a Unicode encoding value of the form '\xxxx' where 'xxxx' is the hexadecimal value of a character in UCS-2 encoding format.
Start of Heading (ASCII: 1) 
\0001
"@"-Symbol (ASCII: 64) 
\0040
2362.helpText: Identifies the character which separates values from each other. Note that the " (double-quote) and \ (backslash) characters are not supported as a Value Separator, also not in the \xxxx format.

2363.name: MULTI_VALUE_TYPE_OPTIONAL
2363.helpText: Determines whether the Source Column contains multiple values, and how these are encoded.

lovValues.helpText:
Column contains values as a delimited list.

APEX,SQL,PL/SQL

Use the APEX_STRING.SPLIT function for processing, as in the following example:

select column_value from apex_string.split ( :ITEM_NAME, ',' );

The Source column contains a JSON array of scalar values. Oracle APEX will raise error messages if the column contains invalid JSON syntax.

["APEX", "SQL", "PL/SQL"]

Use the JSON_TABLE SQL function for processing, as in the following example:

select
    element
from
    json_table ( :ITEM_NAME, '$[*]'
        columns
            element varchar2 path '$'
    );

237.name: VALUE_PLSQL_FUNC_BODY_NO_LANG
237.examples:
To return some data from the EMP table as a stringified JSON:
declare
    l_result json;
begin
    select json_arrayagg (
               json_object (
                   'empno' value empno,
                   'ename' value ename
               )
           )
      into l_result
      from emp;

    return l_result;
end;
237.helpText: Enter the PL/SQL function body which returns a value used as the source for this parameter value.

238.name: MENU_ENTRY_TYPE
238.helpText: Select how the menu entry should be rendered.

lovValues.helpText: A menu entry that executes an action.
Groups multiple other menu entries in a sub-menu. A sub-menu entry can't execute an action.
To group menu entries, a separator can be used to divide menu entries. If there is no previous or next menu entry, the separator will not be shown.

2381.name: VALUE_PARENT_COLUMN
2381.helpText: Select a primary key column from the master interactive grid region; the value of that column will be used as the source for this parameter value.

2390.name: IS_PAGE_PATTERN
2390.helpText: Specify if the page is to be used as a pattern. Page patterns are shown in the create page wizard allowing you to easily copy a pattern when creating a page. Page patterns can be run from the application builder but are not runnable by end users.

2391.name: BUILDER_ICON_CSS_CLASS
2391.helpText: Please provide an icon css class to represent your page pattern in the create page wizard. You can choose a pre-existing icon from the list.

2392.name: PAGE_SUBSCRIBED_FROM
2392.helpText: Use this field to base this page on an existing page in another application in your workspace.

24.name: AUTHORIZATION_SCHEME
24.helpText: Select an authorization scheme to control this component. The authorization must evaluate to TRUE in order for this component to be rendered or executed.

240.name: ACTION_POSITION
240.helpText: Determines where the action is positioned on the Template Component.

241.name: ENTITY_TITLE_SINGULAR
241.helpText:
Define a custom title for the entity displayed by the region. Note: If nothing is defined, the generic term "row" will be used.

The singular and plural titles are used to show more descriptive messages to end users. Instead of a generic "No rows found" a more engaging "No customers found" message is displayed.

242.name: ENTITY_TITLE_PLURAL
242.helpText:
Define a custom title for the entity displayed by the region. Note: If nothing is defined, the generic term "rows" will be used.

The singular and plural titles are used to show more descriptive messages to end users. Instead of a generic "No rows found" a more engaging "No customers found" message is displayed.

2422.name: LAZY_LOADING_ALWAYS
2422.helpText:
Specify whether to load the region independently of the data for the region.

When lazy loading is specified, the page is rendered immediately, showing an empty region, until the data is loaded. Generally, the page is not displayed until all of the page is loaded and ready to be rendered. Therefore, if it takes 5 seconds to load all of the data for a region, without lazy loading, the end user would have to wait 5 seconds before the page started to render.

Note - Lazy Loading should only be utilized on data sets that take significant time to load, as this adds unnecessary processing overhead on the database for regions that load quickly.

243.name: TEMPLATE_COMPONENT_TYPE
243.helpText: Select how the data should be displayed.

lovValues.helpText: A report with pagination controls is rendered based on the rows returned by the region source.
Only one partial is rendered based on the single row the region source returns.
A single partial based on the values from the attributes.

244.name: ENTITIES_PER_PAGE
244.helpText: Enter the number of entities to display per page.

245.name: ALWAYS_EXECUTE
245.helpText:
Specify whether this validation is always executed. If set to On, this validation is always evaluated, irrespective of the Execute Validations setting defined against the button that submitted the page. If set to Off, this validation is only evaluated if the triggering button has an Execute Validations setting of On.

Note: This validation must also comply with the conditions specified before being evaluated.

246.name: ERROR_MESSAGE_DISPLAY_LOCATION
246.helpText: Select where the error message displays for this validation. Validation error messages display on a separate error page, or inline with the existing page. Inline error messages display underneath the Associated Item label and/or in a Notification area, defined as part of the page template.

lovValues.d: Inline with Field and in Notification

247.name: ASSOCIATED_ITEM
247.helpText: Select the item where this validation error message displays. If you select an item and the Error message display location includes "Inline with Field", the error message displays underneath the label of the specified item. If the Error message display location does not include "Inline with Field", this attribute has no impact on the display of the error message.

248.name: ASSOCIATED_COLUMN
248.helpText: Select the column associated with this page processing component.

249.name: EXECUTION_SCOPE
249.helpText: Select the execution scope for this editable region validation. Select For Created and Modified Rows, if you want this validation to be evaluated for new and updated rows in your editable region. If you want your validation to be evaluated for every submitted row, select All Submitted Rows.

25.name: PAGE_AUTHENTICATION
25.helpText:
Specify whether this page is public or requires authentication.
If a page is identified as public, the page can be viewed by any user who accesses the page.
The application's page sentry function may access this page attribute to identify pages that do not require prior authentication to view.
The implementation of the authentication scheme's page sentry function determines whether this attribute has any effect.

250.name: EXECUTE_CONDITION
250.helpText: Select how many times this editable region validation is executed. If you refer to Columns in your condition, you must specify For Each Row in order for the condition to be evaluated for each row of the editable region. Otherwise, set to Once to evaluate the validations one time for the region.

251.name: VALIDATION_REGION
251.helpText: Select the associated region for this validation.

252.name: BUTTON_ACTION
252.helpText: Select the action to be performed when this button is clicked.

lovValues.helpText: Submit the current page with a REQUEST value equal to the Button Name.

lovValues.d: Redirect to Page in this Application
lovValues.helpText: Redirect to a page in the current application, with optional additional attributes for resetting pagination, setting the request value, clearing cache and setting item values, on the target page.

lovValues.d: Redirect to Page in a different Application
lovValues.helpText:
Redirect to a page in a different application, with optional additional attributes for resetting pagination, setting the request value, clearing cache and setting item values, on the target page.

Note: Redirecting to a page in different application relies on deep linking being enabled in the target application. To enable deep linking, go to the application's Security attributes and enable Deep Linking.
Redirect to the target URL you specify.
Does not submit the page or redirect to another page. Instead the button's behavior is defined by a Dynamic Action.
Reset the page by performing a complete page refresh, not a Partial Page Refresh (PPR).
Redirect to the next page.
Redirect to the previous page.

253.name: INITIAL_ENTITIES_COUNT
253.helpText: Enter the number of entities to display initially. If not specified a default of 40 will be used.

254.name: DIALOG_TEMPLATE
254.helpText:
Select a dialog template to define the appearance and layout of this page.

Dialog templates are defined in the application theme. When a dialog page is created, the template is automatically set to Theme Default which will render the page using the default page template defined in the current theme. Making a selection here overrides the default dialog template.

Universal Theme provides the following dialog templates:

Modal Dialog
Useful for most dialog use cases.
Wizard Modal Dialog
Provides a streamlined user interface and is well suited for modal dialog wizards, alerts, notifications, or small forms.
See Also: Universal Theme Sample Application

255.name: OVERWRITE_NAVIGATION_LIST
255.helpText: Specify whether the default User Interface level navigation is overwritten. This can be used to either have no navigation for the current page, or choose alternative navigation for the current page (for example to provide different navigation around a sub-section of your app).

256.name: NAVIGATION_LIST
256.helpText: Select the navigation menu list utilized for navigation on this page.

257.name: NAVIGATION_LIST_TEMPLATE
257.helpText: Select the navigation menu list template utilized with the navigation menu list on this page.

258.name: REGION_ACTION_PARENT_MENU
258.helpText: Select the parent menu in which the menu entry will be displayed.

259.name: ACTION_TEMPLATE
259.helpText: Determines which template is used to render the action.

26.name: DEEP_LINKING
26.helpText:
Select how external URL requests to a page are handled.
Page requests from within this application to this page, are not considered deep linking, and are not governed by this attribute's setting.

lovValues.helpText:
If this page is specified as the target page in a URL, it ultimately redirects to this page.
If the user is not already authenticated and the page is not public, then the user is prompted to login. After successfully logging into the application, the user is redirected to this page.
If the URL does not contain a valid session ID, Oracle APEX starts a new session and redirects the user to the application home page, rather than to this page.

266.name: INCLUDE_SEARCH_BAR
266.helpText:
A search bar is displayed above the report. If you include the search bar, you can also fully customize which functions to display.

The search bar can include the following components:
Search Field
Displays a text field in the search bar used to enter search criteria.
Finder Drop Down
Embedded within the Search Field, displays a drop down list of displayed columns. If a column is selected then the search is only performed against the values in the selected column.
Reports Select List
Displays a list of all available reports for the user, including primary, alternate, public and private reports. This list is only displayed if a report, other than the primary report, is accessible to the user.
Rows Per Page Selector
Displays a select list used to select the number of rows to display per page.
Actions Menu
Displays the Actions menu button, which generally includes a comprehensive set of options. These options enables the end user to customize the report based upon the functions you make available.

267.name: COLUMN_NAME
267.helpText: Enter the column name for this report column.

268.name: COLUMN_TYPE
268.helpText: Enter the data type for the report column.

269.name: IR_COLUMN_GROUP
269.helpText: Select the group for this column. Groups are used to display columns in logical groups in the Single Row View.

27.name: PAGE_ACCESS_PROTECTION
27.helpText: Select what type of session state protection is implemented for this page.

lovValues.helpText: The page may be requested using a URL, with or without session state arguments, and without having to have a checksum.

If Request, Clear Cache, or Name/Value Pair arguments appear in the URL, a checksum must also be provided.
The checksum type must be compatible with the most stringent Session State Protection attribute of all the items passed as arguments.
A URL may be used to request the page, but the URL can not contain Request, Clear Cache, or Name/Value Pair arguments.

The page may not be accessed using a URL.
However, the page may be the target of a Branch to Page branch type, as this does not perform a URL redirect.

271.name: IR_COLUMN_DISPLAY_TYPE
271.helpText:
Select the relevant column display type to define how column values are displayed. The following types are supported:

#NATIVE_PLUGINS#

Depending on your application configuration, you may also have additional plug-ins available here. The following plug-ins are installed within this application's shared components:

#CUSTOM_PLUGINS#

272.name: COLUMN_HEADING
272.helpText: Enter the report column heading text.

273.name: SYNC_FORM_LABEL
273.helpText: Specify this attribute if you want to use the column heading text as the label in the Detail View.

274.name: SINGLE_ROW_VIEW_LABEL
274.helpText: Enter the column label to use in the Single Row View.

275.name: HEADING_ALIGNMENT
275.helpText: Select the heading alignment. Note that your alignment selection must be supported by the selected report template.

276.name: COLUMN_ALIGNMENT
276.helpText: Select the column display alignment. Note that your alignment selection must be supported by the selected report template.

277.name: ALLOW_USERS_TO_HIDE
277.helpText: Specify whether end users can hide this column.

278.name: ALLOW_USERS_TO_SORT
278.helpText: Specify whether end users can sort this column.

279.name: ALLOW_USERS_TO_FILTER
279.helpText: Specify whether end users can filter this column.

28.name: ALLOW_DUPLICATE_PAGE_SUBMISSIONS
28.helpText:
Select whether the end user may submit the same page more than once.
Use this feature to avoid duplicate inserts into the same table.
This can happen when an end user clicks the browser's back button and then submits the page again, or if the end user clicks the browser's reload button.

lovValues.d: No - Prevent page from being re-posted
Yes - Enable page to be re-posted

280.name: ALLOW_USERS_TO_HIGHLIGHT
280.helpText: Specify whether end users can highlight this column.

281.name: ALLOW_USERS_TO_CONTROL_BREAK
281.helpText: Specify whether end users can utilize this column in a control break.

282.name: ALLOW_USERS_TO_AGGREGATE
282.helpText: Specify whether end users can aggregate this column.

283.name: ALLOW_USERS_TO_COMPUTE
283.helpText: Specify whether end users can utilize this column in a computational column they define.

284.name: ALLOW_USERS_TO_CHART
284.helpText: Specify whether end users can use this column within a chart.

285.name: ALLOW_USERS_TO_GROUP_BY
285.helpText: Specify whether end users can group by this column.

286.name: IR_COLUMN_FILTER_TYPE
286.helpText: Select how to derive the filters provided in the report column drop down list.

lovValues.helpText: There is no column filter provided for this report.
STRING and NUMBER columns derive the list of values from distinct column values. DATE columns derive the list of values from predefined date ranges.

lovValues.d: Use Defined List of Values to Filter Exact Match
lovValues.helpText: Derive the list of values from a defined list of values SQL query to create an equal match filter.

lovValues.d: Use Defined List of Values to Filter Word Contains
lovValues.helpText: Derive the list of values from a defined list of values SQL query to create a contains filter.

lovValues.d: Use Named List of Values to Filter Exact Match
lovValues.helpText: Derive the list of values from the named list of values to create an equal filter.

lovValues.d: Use Named List of Values to Filter Word Contains
lovValues.helpText: Derive the list of values from the named list of values to create a contains filter.

287.name: SHOW_AS_DISABLED
287.helpText:
Specify whether to render the button or menu entries as disabled instead of hiding them if the entered row-level condition evaluates to FALSE.

Setting this attribute to On> improves layout stability and guides end-users on which actions are available.

288.name: REPORT_FILTER_DATE_RANGES
288.helpText:
Select the list of values date restrictions.
For date columns, the list of values can display past time, future time, or both in the filter for the report column drop down list.

289.name: HTML_EXPRESSION
289.examples:
Change the background and text colors
<span style="background-color:yellow; color:red;">#EMPLOYEE_STATUS#</span>
Use Heading 2
<h2>#EMPLOYEE_NAME#</h2>
Use a dynamic class from the SQL query
<span class="#COLUMN_CLASS#">#EMPLOYEE_STATUS#</span>

The #COLUMN_CLASS# and #EMPLOYEE_STATUS# substitutions in this example are columns selected in the report SQL query.
Show an image, and a tooltip on hover
<img src="#IMAGE_NAME#" title="#EMPLOYEE_NAME#">
Loop over a comma separated list of values
<ul>{loop "," TAGS/}<li>&APEX$ITEM.</li>{endloop/}</ul>
Use an "if" directive for a column with a quoted identifier
{if Mixed Case Name/}<strong>#"Mixed Case Name"#</strong>{endif/}
289.helpText:
Enter HTML expressions to be shown in this column. Use #COLUMN# syntax to show column values in HTML.

If a column name is a quoted identifier, use #"COLUMN"# syntax.

29.name: ON_DUPLICATE_PAGE_SUBMISSIONS_GO_TO_THIS_URL
29.prompt: On duplicate page submissions go to this URL
29.helpText: Enter a URL target for when an end user attempts to perform a second page submission. Oracle APEX displays an error message and a link to this URL to enable the user to continue.

290.name: LINK_TEXT
290.helpText: Enter the HTML text to be shown as a link. Use an image tag to display images, or pick from the list of default images.

291.name: LINK_ATTRIBUTES
291.examples:
Open the link in a new window
target="_blank"
Show a tooltip on hover
title="Click to edit"
291.helpText: Enter additional column link attributes to be included in the <a href=...> tag, including link target, classes or styles.

292.name: IR_PAGINATION_TYPE
292.helpText:
Select the pagination type for this report. Often only a certain number of rows of a report display on a page. In order to include additional rows, the application end user must to navigate to the next page of the report.

Pagination provides the end user with information about the number of rows and the current position within the result set.

Pagination can be shown above or below the report (or both) and can be positioned on the left or right.

lovValues.d: Row Ranges X to Y of Z

293.name: PAGINATION_DISPLAY_POSITION
293.helpText: Select where the report pagination displays.

294.name: SHOW_NULL_VALUES_AS
294.helpText: Enter the text you want to display for null columns.

295.name: MAXIMUM_ROW_COUNT
295.helpText:
Enter the maximum number of rows which can be processed by the query. If the maximum number of rows to be processed exceeds the limit, then an error message will be displayed instead of data. A custom message can be defined by specifying a message in More Data Found.

This attribute is to safeguard against end users performing actions, such as sorts or aggregations, on all the records in very large tables or views, which might not be performant. Instead, the number of records being processed must first be reduced by adding additional filters.

33.name: BROWSER_CACHE
33.helpText:
If the cache is enabled, the browser can save the contents of your application's pages in its cache, both in memory and on disk. If a user clicks the browser back button, the page typically loads from the cache, not from the server. If the cache is disabled, the browser is instructed to not save page content and requests it anew from the server.

Oracle recommends, from a security perspective, that the cache is disabled, so the browser does not store sensitive data and always requests pages if the URL changes. Otherwise, it may even be possible to go back in the browser history after a log out and see cached content of the former session. Disabling the browser cache prevents subtle back button issues with pages that use partial page refresh, such as interactive reports.

If this attribute is set to Disabled, Oracle APEX sends the HTTP header cache-control: no-store which instructs the Browser to not cache the page contents on disk or in memory. If it is set to Application Default, the value at runtime is taken from the application's Browser Cache attribute.

Note: This feature requires modern browsers that support the HTTP header response variable cache-control.

Users can only query this data, but can not rewind any data changes. How far back in time they can successfully perform a flashback query is determined by when the redo log files were last switched within the Oracle database, as this technology utilizes the RMAN backup.

  • Set Items: Value - enter or select a report column (#ID#), enter an application or page item (&P2_EMPNO.), or enter a static value (2).
  • Clear Cache - enter a comma-delimited list of page numbers (2,3), items (P3_EMPNO,LAST_PAGE), and report settings to be cleared. To reset pagination for a report enter RP. To clear or reset interactive report settings enter CIR or RIR.

Page in a different application

URL

38.name: BUILD_OPTION
38.examples:
1. You are developing an application that will have many installations. Additionally, each installation may choose to enable or disable certain application functionality. With Build Options, you can develop one application and when installed, build options can be configured to include or exclude associated application functionality. You may also use the API to expose this feature within the application. This allows privileged end-users to selectively enable or disable application functionality.

2. You are developing functionality which is not yet complete, so you do not wish to expose to end-users. Using Build Options enables you to disable this functionality from the application when it is built into the test and production environments. The benefit of this approach is that the application can still be deployed without including incomplete functionality.

3. You are removing functionality you think is not needed by the application, but are unsure this is a safe operation. In this case, you can use Build Options to essentially "comment out" specific functionality. If on deployment, the removed functionality was deemed to be necessary, it can be re-instated. If this functionality was deemed to be unnecessary, then it can be safely removed from the application.
38.helpText:
Select a build option for this component.

Build Options can set this component to be Included or Excluded in the runtime application:

Included - Enabled and are part of the application.

Excluded - Disabled and are not a part of the application.

When a screen reader user navigates to different rows of the report, the column, or columns defined as identifying the row will be announced as the row header, as soon as they move to the new row. 41.name: ERROR_HANDLING_FUNCTION
41.helpText:
Enter the name of the PL/SQL function called when an error occurs within the application. You can use this function to act on various error codes including those emanating from the Oracle database, and log such errors in a custom table you define if necessary. The function can include logic to modify the error message and display location, transforming Oracle database errors into user friendly messages. For example, you can capture a unique key violation on DEMO_CUSTOMERS and replace the ORA-00001 message with this text: Customer Name must be unique. Installing the Poll Starter App, from the Gallery, creates the EBA_QPOLL_FW package, which includes the apex_error_handling function. This error handling function includes extensive comments to make it easy for you to utilize as the basis for defining your own function.

The function name entered can reference a package function or stand alone function in the database. For example: 

log_apex_error

When referencing a database PL/SQL package or stand alone function, you can use the #OWNER# substitution string to reference the parsing schema of the current application. For example: 

#OWNER#.log_apex_error

If an error handling function is specified on a page then it is utilized, instead of this application level setting, for that page.

Error Handling Functions must implement the following interface: 

function <name of function> (
    p_error in apex_error.t_error )
    return apex_error.t_error_result

See the API Reference manual for a description of the package apex_error.

411.name: REPORT_TEMPLATE
411.helpText:
Select a report template to define the appearance and layout of this classic report.

Report templates are defined in the application theme. When a classic report is created, the template is automatically set to the default report template defined in the current theme.

Many themes contain classic report templates for displaying data in a table, key value pairs, search results, cards, and so forth. Note that some report templates, such as cards and search results, are "row based" and expect your SQL query to return a particular set of column aliases that are substituted in the template.
Universal Theme provides the following report templates:

Alerts
Displays any number of horizontal alerts or notifications on your page.
Badge List
Displays key value pairs in a dashboard-like user interface.
Cards
Displays report data in cards, or small blocks and is useful for presenting a variety of information. Cards can be heavily customized via Template Options.
Comments
Displays comments and other messages.
Content Row
Displays report data in a set of rows, with support for a selection column, icons, and actions. Suitable for most types of content.
Contextual Info
Displays simple key-value pairs one after the next. It uses the column headers as the labels and displays the associated column value next to each label.
Media List
Displays report content in a media list, with an icon, heading, description, and badge.
Search Results
Displays search-engine style search results.
Standard
This is the default report template for displaying data in a table and can be heavily customized via Template Options.
Timeline
Displays a timeline of actions. It is well suited for home pages, change logs, and other areas where an activity feed of recent actions is needed.
Value Attribute Pairs - Column
Displays key-value pairs for column-based queries. It uses the column header as the label for each item.
Value Attribute Pairs - Row
Displays key-value pairs for row-based queries. It uses the first column for labels, and second column for values.
See Also: Universal Theme Sample Application

Hex notation is defined as #xxyyzz (a # followed by 3 double digit hex numbers), where xx, yy, and zz represent the two character hex values for red, green and blue respectively. RGB codes are defined as RGB(xxx,xxx,xxx), where xxx is a number between 0 and 255 each representing the single 8-bit byte value for red, green, and blue respectively.

Search the internet for 'HTML Color Codes' to find the equivalent hex code or RGB code for the color you wish to utilize.

431.name: CLASSIC_REPORT_PAGINATION_TYPE
431.helpText:
Select the pagination type to utilize in this report. Generally only a subset of the results are currently displayed in the report. Pagination provides the user with information about the number of rows and the current position within the result set. Pagination also defines the style of links or buttons that are used to navigate to the next or previous page.

Pagination can be shown above or below the report (or both) and can be positioned on the left or right.

You can also use a simplified pagination style to improve performance, such as Row Ranges X to Y (with next and previous links). Using pagination types of the form "X to Y of Z", require the Oracle APEX engine to perform two queries to return the results. One query retrieves the current records to be displayed and another query gets the total record count to display in the pagination control. For reports based on exceedingly large data sets or with very CPU intensive queries, such as numerous non-optimal table joins or expensive conditions, this additional query can add some processing time, which can lead to the report taking longer to render.

lovValues.d: Row Ranges X to Y (no pagination)
Row Ranges X to Y of Z (no pagination)
Row Ranges X to Y of Z (with pagination)
Row Ranges 1-15 16-30 in select list (with pagination)

432.name: PARTIAL_PAGE_REFRESH
432.helpText:
Specify whether to use Partial Page Refresh (PPR) to update the report display.

If the end user performs an action, such as a pagination request or selection of a new sort column, the current report rows must be refreshed. Setting this attribute to On, refreshes just the report region. Setting this attribute to Off, refreshes the entire page.

If you select values from the database that already contain HTML tags, then those tags can cause conflicts with the HTML generated for your HTML expressions or URL generated for column links. When exporting such values, the existing HTML tags are included as plain text in the generated CSV file. When this option is enabled, only the actual data portion of your column value is used.

438.name: WHEN_MORE_DATA_FOUND_MESSAGE
438.helpText:
Enter the text message that displays when more report rows exist. Use this approach as an alternative to pagination, especially if a report generally only has a discrete record set. If the report query returns additional rows, this message can be used to alert the end user to the anomaly, rather than simply displaying slightly different pagination controls. Your text message can readily incorporate a "Call to action" so end users are given guidance on how to respond to this unusual query result and can include page or URL links.

The following pagination substitution strings can be utilized in your message:

#ROWS_FETCHED#
The number of rows displayed (page size)
#TOTAL_ROWS#
The "Z" in "rows X - Y of Z"
#FIRST_ROW_FETCHED#
The "X" in "rows X - Y of Z"
#LAST_ROW_FETCHED#
The "Y" in "rows X - Y of Z"
#ROW_RANGES"
Shows: Row(s) 1-15 16-30 30-32
#ROW_RANGES_IN_SELECT_LIST
Same as row ranges but in a select list
#INTERNET_PAGINATION#
Page Sets: 1 2 3 4 5 6

44.name: MEDIA_TYPE
44.helpText:
Enter the Internet media type. An Internet media type is a two part identifier for file formats on the Internet. A media type is composed of at least two parts: a type, a subtype, and one or more optional parameters. This media type is used in the Content-Type HTTP header when rendering the page.

The page-level Media type overrides the application-level media type. If both the page-level and application-level values for media type are NULL, the media type text/html is used.

File URLs you enter here replace the #PAGE_CSS# substitution string in the page template.

Each file URL can optionally be prefixed with [media ...] for conditional loading. See the examples for details.

Note: You do not need to include opening or closing link tags. Just include the file URL.

5400.name: VALIDATION_TYPE
5400.helpText:
Select the type of equality to be tested for this validation. Depending on your selection, one or more additional attributes are required to fully define this validation.

If the validation passes the equality test, or evaluates to TRUE, then the validation error message does not display. Validation error messages display when the validation fails the equality test, or evaluates to FALSE, or a non-empty text string is returned.

A validation failure does not stop subsequent validations from being evaluated, therefore, each subsequent validation may raise an additional validation error message. If you want to stop subsequent validations from executing then you need to add additional logic into the first failed validation, such as setting a page item to a specific value, and then enhancing the conditional logic on subsequent validations as needed. Subsequent processes and branches are not executed if one or more validations fail evaluation.

736.name: REJOIN_EXISTING_SESSIONS
736.helpText:
Use this attribute to control if Oracle APEX should support application URLs that do not contain session IDs. When rejoin sessions is enabled, Oracle APEX will attempt to use the session cookie to join an existing session, when a URL does not contain a session ID.

A more restrictive instance level setting overrides this page level value.

Note: Enabling rejoin sessions exposes your application to possible security breaches, as it can enable attackers to take over existing end user sessions. To learn more, see the Rejoin Sessions sections in "Managing Application Security" in the App Builder User's Guide.

lovValues.helpText: If the URL does not contain a session ID Oracle APEX creates a new session.

If the URL goes to a public page and does not contain a session ID Oracle APEX attempts to utilize the existing session cookie established for that application.
For applications with both public and authenticated pages, a session ID is defined after the end user authenticates.
Oracle APEX only joins via the cookie when the session is not yet authenticated.

If the URL does not contain a session ID Oracle APEX attempts to utilize the existing session cookie established for that application, providing the following conditions are met:

  • Session State Protection is enabled for the application and the URL includes a valid checksum. For public bookmarks, the most restrictive item level protection must be either Unrestricted or Checksum Required - Application Level.
  • OR, the URL does not contain payload (a request parameter, clear cache or data value pairs).

This setting also requires that Embed In Frames is set to Allow from same origin or to Deny for the application.
