lovValues.helpText: Binds the event handler to the triggering element(s) for the lifetime of the current page, but is no longer bound if a triggering element is updated via Partial Page Refresh (PPR).
Binds the event handler to the triggering element(s) for the lifetime of the current page, irrespective of any triggering elements being recreated via Partial Page Refresh (PPR).
Binds the event handler to the triggering element(s) only once. The dynamic action is not triggered again until after the page has been fully refreshed.

770.name: IS_EDITABLE
770.helpText:
Specify whether end users can edit this Interactive Grid.

Note - When the Interactive Grid is made editable a process is automatically created to process the rows.

771.name: EDIT_OPERATIONS
771.helpText: Check which data manipulation operations are allowed on this interactive grid.

772.name: EDIT_ROW_OPERATIONS_COLUMN
772.helpText:
Select a column where the column value indicates if the row can be updated and/or deleted. The allowable values are:
        <dl>
          <dt>U</dt>
            <dd>Row can be updated</dd>
          <dt>D</dt>
            <dd>Row can be deleted</dd>
          <dt>UD</dt>
            <dd>Row can be updated or deleted</dd>
        </dl>

773.name: ADD_AUTHORIZATION_SCHEME
773.helpText:
Specify an authorization scheme to restrict who can add rows.
In order for an end user to add rows, this authorization scheme must evaluate to TRUE for that user.
If no authorization scheme is provided then any user can add rows in this interactive grid.

774.name: UPDATE_AUTHORIZATION_SCHEME
774.helpText:
Select an authorization scheme to restrict who can update rows.
In order for an end user to update rows, this authorization scheme must evaluate to TRUE for that user.
If no authorization scheme is provided then any user can update rows in this interactive grid.

775.name: DELETE_AUTHORIZATION_SCHEME
775.helpText:
Select an authorization scheme to restrict who can delete rows.
        In order for an end user to delete rows, this authorization scheme must evaluate to TRUE for that user.
        If no authorization scheme is provided then any user can delete rows in this interactive grid.

776.name: LOST_UPDATE_CHECK_TYPE
776.helpText:
Select how to protect data against lost updates. Lost updates occur when two or more people try to update the same data, and the last update overwrites updates made by the first user to save changes. To prevent this from happening, updates can check the existing column value(s) in the database with the value(s) retrieved when the record was originally queried.

For example:

  1. User A queries employee (EMP) records.
  2. User B queries the same employee records.
  3. User B updates employee details for EMPNO = 7839 and applies (commits) the changes to the database.
  4. User A updates employee details for EMPNO = 7839 and is attempting to apply the changes to the database.
If User A successfully updates the same record, changes made by User B will be lost.

When User A is attempting to save the employee record, then the data in the database is different from what User A queried originally. In step 1 above, the column value(s) originally queried by User A can be captured. Then in step 4 above, the value(s) can be compared to the current values in the database. This comparison will raise an error for User A, as the database value(s) were updated by User B in step 3. This prevents a user from overwriting changes made by another user to the same row.

Note - Lost Update Type will only be used if the corresponding process, Interactive Grid - Automatic Row Processing (DML), has Prevent Lost Updates enabled.

lovValues.helpText: A checksum value will be calculated for each row, when initially querying the data. The checksum is calculated by concatenating all of the updateable columns into a string and then generating a unique value. When committing the updated record, this checksum will be compared to the checksum value of the current database record. If they are not the same, an error will be raised.

If your database table includes a column which is incremented every time a record is updated, preferably by a database trigger, then this column can be used instead of calculating checksums. This option should not be used if your interactive grid updates data in multiple tables.

Note - The row version column must be included in the SQL Source for the region.

777.name: ROW_VERSION_COLUMN
777.helpText: Select the column which stores the row version number for the table being updated. This column will be used in the lost update check.

778.name: ADD_ROW_IF_EMPTY
778.helpText:
Specify whether to add a new row if the interactive grid currently has no records returned. The No Data Found message will never be displayed as there will always be at least one record displayed.

Note - If no updates are made to the record that was added it will not be inserted when the region is saved.

779.name: SUBMIT_CHECKED_ROWS
779.helpText:
Specify whether to include checked rows in page processing, generally initiated by a custom button, such as Mark Completed. These checked rows can then be utilized in a custom process to perform the required action.

Note - The selected rows will be processed even if nothing on the row has been updated. Generally, only rows which have been inserted, updated or deleted are processed.

78.name: STATIC_CONTAINER_JQUERY
78.helpText:
Enter the jQuery Selector, of a static container, for use by this dynamic action.

You can improve the performance of dynamic actions that have an event scope of Dynamic. This must be an element on the page that itself does not get recreated, but contains the triggering elements that are recreated using Partial Page Refresh (PPR). This element reference needs to be defined as a jQuery selector.

780.name: LAZY_LOADING
780.helpText:
Specify whether to load the region independently of the data for the region.

When lazy loading is specified, the page is rendered immediately, showing an empty region, until the data is loaded. Generally, the page is not displayed until all of the page is loaded and ready to be rendered. Therefore, if it takes 5 seconds to load all of the data for a region, without lazy loading, the end user would have to wait 5 seconds before the page started to render.

Note - Lazy Loading should only be utilized on data sets that take significant time to load, as this adds unnecessary processing overhead on the database for regions that load quickly.

781.name: REQUIRES_FILTER
781.helpText:
Specify whether to prevent the interactive grid from displaying data, unless at least one filter is defined on one of the report columns. This option is designed to limit the data loaded from a very large data set, by restricting the rows returned based on a filter.

Individual columns can have Column Filter Required enabled, ensuring a filter is required for that column, whereas, this option only requires one filter across any of the columns.

Note - When this option is set and no filters are currently defined, a message will be displayed requesting the users to input a filter.

782.name: FIXED_ROW_HEIGHT
782.helpText:
Specify whether to display the interactive grid with fixed row height.

If set to Yes, ellipses (...) will be displayed at the end of data, for columns that are too narrow to display all of the data. If set to No data will wrap across multiple lines as necessary.

783.name: PAGINATION_TYPE
783.helpText:
Select the pagination type for this report. Often not all report rows are displayed in the report. In order to display additional rows, the end user can use the pagination provided.

Pagination provides the end user with information about the number of rows displayed, and the current position within the result set.

lovValues.helpText: The first rows will be displayed, based on the number specified in Rows per Page. If there are additional rows, controls will be added to the report footer, allowing end users to navigate forwards and backwards between row sets.

Initially enough rows to fill the height of the region are displayed.
        As the end user scrolls additional rows are displayed, getting more data from the server as needed.

784.name: SHOW_TOTAL_ROW_COUNT
784.helpText:
Specify whether to display the total row count in the report footer.

Note - An additional query is performed to obtain the total row count, which may hinder performance, especially on very large data sets.

785.name: SHOW_TOOLBAR
785.helpText: Specify whether a toolbar is displayed above the report. The toolbar may include search, report type, saved reports, actions, change, and reset functionality.

786.name: TOOLBAR_CONTROLS
786.helpText: Check which additional controls are to be displayed in the toolbar.

lovValues.helpText: Displays a drop down list of displayed non-numeric columns. If a column is selected then the search is only performed against the values in the selected column.
Displays a text field in the search bar used to enter search criteria.
Displays the Actions menu button, which generally includes a comprehensive set of options. These options enables the end user to customize the report based upon the functions you make available.
Displays the Reset button. When this button is pressed, any customizations, such as filters, column width, and ordering will be removed, and the report definition will be reloaded from the server.

Displays the Save button. When this button is pressed, only changes made to this Interactive Grid will be saved, without needing to save the whole page.

The save button will only be displayed when the Interactive Grid is editable, and the end user has authorization to add, update or delete.

787.name: ADD_BUTTON_LABEL
787.helpText:
Enter an alternative label for the Add button. The default label is Add Row.

For example, enter Add Employee for an interactive grid where employees are maintained.

788.name: ENABLE_SAVE_PUBLIC_REPORT
788.helpText:
Specify whether end users can save their current report definition as a Public report.

Public reports are displayed in a select list of available reports in the Toolbar, and are displayed to everyone.

Note - This option is only available to authenticated users, and is further restricted if you also populate the Save Public Report Authorization.

789.name: PUBLIC_REPORT_AUTH_SCHEME
789.helpText:
Select an authorization scheme to restrict who can save public report definitions. To enable an end user to save a public report, this authorization scheme must evaluate to TRUE for that user.

Note - If no authorization scheme is provided then public reports may be saved by any user.

79.name: DA_EXECUTION_TYPE
79.helpText:
Choose the type of execution method for the Dynamic Action. This defines if the actions are fired immediately, debounced, or throttled.

If a Client-side Condition is defined, it will be evaluated when the Dynamic Action and its Actions are executed, not when the event fires.

lovValues.helpText: Actions are executed immediately.

Actions are only executed once after a specified time at the end of a single or series of events.

Example 1:

Update a text field if the user has stopped typing for 2 seconds and use the values last entered.

Example 2:

Refresh a region once after a click and ignore all other clicks in the next 5 seconds.

Actions are executed at timed intervals when the action is fired multiple times.

Example 1:

During scrolling, update the current screen position at least every 2 seconds. The action will continue to fire if the user keeps scrolling.

Example 2:

As a user types, update a text field with the values entered at least every 2 seconds. The action will continue to fire as the user keeps typing.

790.name: ENABLE_SUBSCRIPTIONS
790.helpText: Specify whether end users can define subscription settings for this report.

791.name: ENABLE_DOWNLOAD
791.helpText: Specify whether end users can download the report to one of the download formats specified.

792.name: IG_DOWNLOAD_FORMATS
792.helpText: Check which download formats users can utilize to download the currently displayed columns.

793.name: ENABLE_MAIL_DOWNLOAD
793.helpText:
Specify whether end users can send an email, with the report download included as an attachment.

Email is only available to authenticated users, and requires the SMTP to be configured within Oracle APEX Administration Services application by an Instance Administrator.

794.name: ICON_VIEW_CUSTOM
794.helpText:
Enter the custom column HTML for the Icon View.

The following substitution strings are available:

  • &<COLUMN_NAME>. - substitution strings for column names.
  • &<COLUMN_NAME>_LABEL. - substitution strings for column labels.
  • &APEX$ROW_ID. - the record identifier for the row.
  • &APEX$ROW_INDEX. - the record display sequence number.
  • &APEX$ROW_URL. - reference the specified Link Target.
  • &APEX$ROW_STATE_CLASSES. - the record state such as is-inserted or is-deleted.

795.name: ICON_VIEW_ICON_TYPE
795.helpText: Select the column type that holds the icon image source.

796.name: ICON_VIEW_ICON_BLOB_COLUMN
796.helpText: Select the interactive grid column that returns the BLOB for the icon image source.

797.name: ICON_VIEW_ICON_URL_COLUMN
797.helpText: Select the interactive grid column that returns the URL for the icon image source.

798.name: ICON_VIEW_ICON_CSS_COLUMN
798.helpText: Select the interactive grid column that returns the CSS classes for the icon image source.

799.name: ICON_VIEW_ICON_ATTRIBUTES
799.helpText: Enter the icon image attributes used for the HTML IMG tag.

8.name: ALIAS
8.helpText:
Enter an alphanumeric alias for this page. You may use this alias to reference the page instead of the page number. For example, if you were working on page 1 of application 100, you could create an alias called home. You could then access this page from other pages using the following f?p syntax: 
f?p=100:home

80.name: DA_EXECUTION_TIME
80.helpText: Specify the amount of time to delay the execution of actions based on the execution type. Measured in milliseconds where 1 second = 1000 milliseconds.

800.name: IG_ICON_VIEW_LINK_TARGET
800.helpText: Click the Link Target to invoke a modal dialog. You can enter a custom target to be called when the icon is clicked.

801.name: ICON_VIEW_LINK_ATTRIBUTES
801.helpText: Enter HTML attributes that are associated with the display of each Link Target.

803.name: COLUMN_INIT_JAVASCRIPT_CODE
803.examples:
function( options ) {
  options.advancedOption = true;
  return options;
}
803.helpText: Enter a JavaScript function that takes a configuration object for the component, modifies the object, and returns it. This allows advanced customization of the appearance, features, and behavior of the component.

804.name: ALTERNATIVE_LABEL
804.helpText:
Enter the alternative label to use in dialogs and in the Single Row View.
        Use an alternative label when the heading contains extra formatting, such as HTML tags, which do not display properly.

805.name: IG_COLUMN_GROUP
805.helpText:
Select the group for this column. Groups are used to associate columns together in the grid and Single Row View.

Note - Groups are added by expanding the Attributes folder within the Rendering tree, and right-clicking on Column Groups to create a new group.

806.name: IG_USE_GROUP_FOR
806.helpText: Select where the group is used to display this column.

lovValues.helpText: The group will display in both the report heading and in the Single Row view.
The group will only display in the Single Row View.
The group will only display in the report heading.

807.name: ENABLE_FILTER
807.helpText: Specify whether end users can filter this column.

808.name: FILTER_OPERATORS
808.helpText:
Select which filter operators end users can utilize for this column.

Depending on the size of the data set and column indexes, you may choose to disable certain filter operators to avoid performance issues for the end users. Certain operators may cause full table scans instead of using column indexes.

lovValues.helpText:
Filter returns results of column values containing the filter value. Oracle APEX will utilize a column LIKE %filtervalue% in the where clause.

Note - this operator will prevent any column indexes being used, which may result in a full table scan.

Filter returns results of column values starting with the filter value. Oracle APEX will utilize a column LIKE filtervalue% in the where clause.

Note - this operator can utilize available column indexes. {Please review Case Insensitive for exceptions}.

Filter returns results of column values irrespective of differences in the case of the column value and filter value. Oracle APEX will utilize a UPPER(column) operator UPPER(filtervalue) in the where clause.

Note - Generally performing UPPER on both the column and filter value will prevent the use of any column indexes, except for function based column indexes with UPPER(column).

Filter returns results based on the regular expression entered.

Note - using REGEXP operators is complex and generally only used by advanced users. Such operators can result in very bad performance.

809.name: FILTER_TEXT_CASE
809.helpText:
Select which case the text within the column value is stored.

If the column can be specified as always upper case, for example Username, or always lower case, then the performance of retrieving filter results can be improved. If Upper or Lower is selected searches will always perform case sensitive searches.

Note - If Mixed is selected, then end users can specify Case Sensitive in the Search and Filter dialogs.

lovValues.helpText: For when the column value is always stored in upper case. Oracle APEX will utilize a column operator UPPER(filtervalue) in the where clause.
For when the column value is always stored in lower case. Oracle APEX will utilize a column operator LOWER(filtervalue) in the where clause.
For when the column value is stored in mixed case. The setting for the Case Insensitive operator will determine the where clause utilized.

81.name: DA_EXECUTION_IMMEDIATE
81.helpText: Toggle when the selected execution type is invoked. Set to Yes for actions to be executed immediately before the timer starts. Set to No for actions to be executed after the value set in Time.

811.name: FILTER_LOV_TYPE
811.helpText: Select how to derive the list of values for the filter when a user clicks on the column header or in filter dialogs.

lovValues.helpText:
Disable any values being displayed in the filter.
        This option is appropriate on large columns, generally with most values being over 50 characters, or when a list would not be very usable for selecting a specific record.
        Instead the end user can just type in a partial value and then view the results.
Distinct column values are displayed for VARCHAR2 and NUMBER columns. DATE and TIMESTAMP columns utilize the built-in predefined date ranges.
Values are derived from the SQL query definition.
Values are derived from an existing list of values.
Values are derived from a static list of values.

lovValues.d: PL/SQL Function Body returning SQL Query
lovValues.helpText: Values are derived from the PL/SQL function body that returns a SQL Query.
Values are derived from list of values.

812.name: FILTER_EXACT_MATCH
812.helpText:
Specify whether to perform an exact match search when the end user enters text into a column filter. If set to Off, the filter will perform a contains search, rather than an equals search.

For example, for a column called TAGS, this is equivalent to TAGS = '<>'. If Exact Match is set to Off, this is equivalent to TAGS LIKE '%<>%'.

813.name: IG_COLUMN_FILTER_STATIC_VALUES
813.helpText:
Enter a comma delimited list of values for this static list.

Note - the Static Values will always be displayed in the same order they are specified, not alphabetically.

814.name: GRID_ROW_CSS_CLASSES
814.helpText:
Enter CSS classes you want to apply to the layout row that contains this region. You may add multiple classes by separating them with spaces.

This property can be used to provide fine grained control over the responsiveness and layout of the region's layout row as the viewport size is changed. For Universal Theme applications, there are a number of CSS modifiers you may use to extend your page components. Review the Reference section of the Universal Theme Sample Application to learn more.

815.name: COLUMN_SOURCE_TYPE
815.helpText: Select the source type the value of this column is based on.

lovValues.helpText: Set to the column value entered in Database Column, that is retrieved from the region source SQL Query.
Set to the value returned from the SQL Expression entered.
The column value is not retrieved from any source. For example, the APEX$ROW_SELECTOR and APEX$ROW_ACTION columns have no source.

817.name: SOURCE_SQL_EXPRESSION
817.examples:
To concatenate two columns together:
FIRSTNAME || ' ' || LASTNAME
Include an inner select:
(select count(*) from emp e where e.deptno = DEPTID)

The SQL Expression will be combined with the main query.
Make sure that there are no ambiguities, use column aliases.

818.name: DATA_TYPE
818.helpText: Select the data type of the underlying database column.

819.name: IS_QUERY_ONLY
819.helpText:
Specify whether to exclude the column from DML operations.

If set to On, Oracle APEX will not utilize the column when executing Interactive Grid - Automatic Row Processing (DML). For example, you should exclude columns whose definitions include concatenations, inner selects, function calls, or a column in an updateable view which is based on an expression.

All columns which need to be included in any INSERT or UPDATE statements must have this option set to Off.

Note: Columns of type Display Only are also included in the Automatic Row Processing unless this option is turned On.

82.name: DA_ACTION_TYPE
82.helpText:
Specify which action you want to perform. The following actions are supported:

#NATIVE_PLUGINS#

Depending on your application configuration, you may also have additional dynamic action plug-ins available here. These are displayed as <My Plug-in> [Plug-in]. The following plug-ins are installed within this application's shared components:

#CUSTOM_PLUGINS#

820.name: IS_PRIMARY_KEY
820.helpText: Specify whether the column is one of the primary key values for the underlying table(s).

821.name: MASTER_COLUMN
821.helpText:
If this column is a foreign key column for the master interactive grid region, as specified by Master Region in the region settings, select the corresponding primary key column from the master table.

For example, if the master region was DEPT and this interactive grid was EMP, then you would select the DEPTNO column within the EMP interactive grid and then select the DEPTNO column from the list of DEPT columns for Master Column.

822.name: ENABLE_SORT_GROUP
822.helpText:
Specify whether end users can use this column in sorting.

Note - Allowing a sort operation can lead to performance issues, especially on large data sets or where appropriate column indexes are not available.

823.name: DEFAULT_TYPE
823.helpText: Select how the default value of this column is determined.

lovValues.helpText: Set to the value entered in Static value.
Set to the value returned from the session state for the Item selected.
Set to the first value returned from the SQL Query entered.

Set to multiple values returned from the SQL Query. The format of what is returned is determined by the current column's Multiple Values setting. If Multiple Values is set to Delimited Values, the value will be a single concatenated list separated by the defined Separator. If Multiple Values is set to JSON Array, the value will be a JSON Array of the values. If Multiple Values is set to No or the column does not support multiple values, then the value is a single concatenated list separated by a colon.
Set to the value returned from the Expression entered.
Set to the value returned from the Function Body entered.

Set to the value returned from the Sequence entered. This is a "special" default type: It is executed as part of the Interactive Grid DML process and not during page load. Use this type for auto-generated primary key values, when Return Primary Key(s) after Insert cannot be used, for instance when working with views and INSTEAD OF triggers or with database links. The sequence name is case-insensitive; use double quotes to indicate a mixed case sequence name ("mySequence").

824.name: DEFAULT_VALUE_SQL_QUERY
824.helpText: Set to the first value returned from the SQL Query entered.

825.name: DEFAULT_VALUE_SQL_QUERY_COLON
825.helpText: Set to multiple values returned from the SQL Query. The format of what is returned is determined by the current item's Multiple Values setting. If Multiple Values is set to Delimited Values, the value will be a single concatenated list separated by the defined Separator. If Multiple Values is set to JSON Array, the value will be a JSON Array of the values. If Multiple Values is set to No or the item does not support multiple values, then the value is a single concatenated list separated by a colon.

826.name: DEFAULT_VALUE_SEQUENCE
826.helpText: Enter the name of the database sequence which returns the default value for this column.

827.name: DUPLICATE_VALUE
827.helpText: Specify whether the column should be defaulted to the existing column value when duplicating the record.

828.name: EXECUTE_READONLY
828.helpText:
Select when this read only condition is executed.

If you refer to Columns in your read only condition, you must specify For Each Row in order for the condition to be evaluated for each row of the Interactive Grid. Otherwise, set to Once to evaluate the condition only one time for the region.

lovValues.helpText: Evaluate the read only condition independently for each row.
Evaluate the read only condition only once for the whole region.

829.name: JET_CHART_TYPE
829.helpText: Select the chart type. The chart type determines the visualization used to render the chart.

lovValues.helpText: Area charts are useful for comparing trends of cumulative values over time, such as breakdowns of sales trends.
Bar charts are useful for comparing values across categories, or over time.

Box plot charts are useful for analyzing the distribution of data, displaying the minimum, quartiles, median, and maximum values of groups of numerical data. Box plots are also called Box and Whisker diagrams.
Bubble charts define data items using x, y, and z values, making them useful for viewing relationships between 3 dimensions. The third dimension is represented by the size of the bubble.
Combination charts allow bar, line, and area series to be displayed on the same chart. The most common use case is lines with bars or lines with stacked bars.
Status Meter gauges are used to display a metric value in relation to the minimum and maximum possible values for that metric.
Donut charts are a pie chart with a hole in the middle. They are useful for visualizing parts of a whole.
Funnel charts are useful for viewing data for stages of a process, such as the stages of a sales process. The area of a funnel slice is proportional to the value for the corresponding stage.
Gantt charts are useful for displaying project schedules, displaying bars that indicate the start and end date of tasks.
Line charts are useful for visualizing trends in a set of values over time and comparing these values across series.
Line with Area charts are the same as line charts, with the area below each line filled in.
Pie charts are useful for visualizing parts of a whole.
Polar charts have a radial y-axis and a tangential x-axis. Polar charts can be rendered as bar, line, area, combination, scatter, or bubble chart series types.

Pyramid charts are useful for visualizing hierarchical, proportional and foundation-based relationships, process steps, organizational layers or topics interconnections. The area of a pyramid slice is proportional to its value for the corresponding stage.
Radar charts are polar charts with a polygonal grid shape, rather than a circle surround. They are supported for line and area chart series types.
Range charts display maximum and minimum (high / low) values for each entry, using either bars or area.
Scatter charts define data items using x and y values, making them useful for viewing relationships between 2 dimensions.

Stock charts are useful for displaying information about a stock on a time axis. Unique to stock charts is the candlestick Stock Render As property, which allows for displaying open, close, high, low information for the stock price.

83.name: FIRE_WHEN_EVENT_RESULT_IS
83.helpText:
Specify whether this action fires when the triggering element condition is met by selecting True (True Action), or when it is not met by selecting False (False Action).

Note: if there is no condition specified, only True actions fire.

830.name: ORIENTATION
830.helpText: Select the orientation of this chart.

lovValues.helpText: Displays the data items of the chart vertically.  For example, the bars on a Bar chart will display vertically.
Displays the data items of the chart horizontally.  For example, the bars on a Bar chart will display horizontally.

831.name: VALUE_TEXT_TYPE
831.helpText: Specify how the value should be displayed on the chart, either as a number or a percentage of the total value.

lovValues.helpText:
The value will be displayed as a number on the chart.

Note: the Format attribute should only be used to apply custom decimal or currency formatting to the label and value displayed on the chart.

The value will be displayed as a percent between 0% and 100%.

Note: When Format is set to Percent, the values on the chart are multiplied by 100 to format as a percent. If you wish to use the Format attribute, ensure that Label Type is set to number.

832.name: IS_GROUP
832.helpText:
Specify whether the column is used to group the rows.

Note: The used Template Component must support Group Templates and grouping depends on Order by. All group columns must be referenced in order by clause and column value cannot be null.

833.name: STACK
833.helpText: Specify whether the data items are stacked.

834.name: STACK_LABEL
834.helpText: Specify whether the total values of stacked data items should be displayed. Only applies to bar charts.

836.name: ANIMATION_ON_DISPLAY
836.helpText:
Select the type of animation used when initially displaying the chart.

The options Alpha Fade and Zoom do not apply to Dial charts.

lovValues.helpText: Apply the Oracle JET defined default animation settings for the chart.
Fade in the chart when initially displayed. This setting does not apply to Gantt charts.
Zoom in to the chart when initially displayed. This setting does not apply to Gantt charts.
No animation applied to the chart when initially displayed.

837.name: ANIMATION_ON_DATA_CHANGE
837.helpText:
Select whether animation is shown when data is changed on the chart. A data change can occur if the chart gets automatically refreshed, if hide and show behavior is performed when clicking on a legend item, or when chart data is programmatically updated via some custom JavaScript code or a Dynamic Action.

The options Slide to Left and Slide to Right do not apply to Dial charts

.

lovValues.helpText: Apply the Oracle JET defined default animation settings for the chart.
The data elements slide to the left when data is changed. This setting does not apply to Gantt charts.
The data elements slide to the right when data is changed. This setting does not apply to Gantt charts.
No animation is applied to the chart when data is changed.

838.name: JET_GAUGE_ORIENTATION
838.helpText: Select the type of Status Meter Gauge chart to render.

839.name: JET_GAUGE_PLOT_AREA
839.helpText: Specify whether the plot area of a Status Meter Gauge chart is to be rendered.

84.name: FIRE_ON_PAGE_LOAD
84.helpText:
Specify if the action fires on initialization.

Initialization has a slightly different meaning depending on how the Dynamic Action is defined. For Dynamic Actions defined to fire on Interactive Grid columns, this specifies if the action fires when the Interactive Grid row is activated for editing. For all other Dynamic Actions, this specifies if the action fires when the page loads.

840.name: JET_DATA_CURSOR
840.helpText:
Select whether the data cursor is enabled on the chart. Data cursor is a useful alternative to tooltips when the data items are difficult to navigate to, especially on touch devices.

If set to Automatic, the data cursor is shown only for line or area charts on touch devices.

Note - The data cursor is not shown when the tooltip is null, and it is not supported on polar charts.

lovValues.helpText: Apply the Oracle JET defined default data cursor display for the chart.
The data cursor is always displayed.
The data cursor is not displayed.

841.name: JET_DATA_CURSOR_BEHAVIOR
841.helpText: Select the behavior of the data cursor on the chart.

lovValues.helpText: Apply the Oracle JET defined default data cursor behavior for the chart.

The data cursor follows the mouse/touch movement smoothly, displaying the tooltip whenever the data cursor is hovering over any part of a data element, and not just specific data points. An indicator identifies the currently selected data element.

Note - Set Cursor to Yes for this visualization to work fully.

The data cursor snaps (jumps) to a data element when a mouse/touch movement occurs over the chart, displaying the tooltip whenever the data cursor is hovering over a data element. An indicator identifies the currently selected data element.

Note - Set Cursor to Yes for this visualization to work fully.

842.name: JET_HOVER_BEHAVIOR
842.helpText:
Specify the behavior to be applied when hovering over data items on the chart.

Select On to dim all data items when not currently hovered over, and highlight only the current data item hovered over.

843.name: JET_TIME_AXIS_TYPE
843.helpText: Select the type of time axis to display on the chart. This setting will automatically render the chart data in chronological order, and should not be used if you require your data to be rendered in reverse chronological order.

lovValues.helpText: Apply the Oracle JET defined default time axis setting for the chart, based on the data being rendered.
Apply no time axis type setting to the chart.
Apply a time axis type setting to the chart.
The time values displayed on the chart axis in mixed frequency. Since the time value of the data can vary, stacking is not supported.
The time values displayed on the chart axis will be rendered at a regular interval regardless of any time gaps that may exist in the data.

844.name: JET_ZOOM_AND_SCROLL
844.helpText:
Specify the zoom and scroll behavior of the chart.
        Zoom and scroll allows the end user to use gestures, such as dragging on the plot area, using the mouse wheel, or two-finger pinches, to resize the values displayed and navigate within the chart to display different chart values.

lovValues.helpText: Zoom and scroll are disabled for the chart.
The change to the data display will wait until the zoom/scroll action is done.
The change to the data display will wait until the scroll action is done.
Live behavior means that the chart will be updated continuously as it is being manipulated. For large data sets or slow client environments, it is recommended to select Delayed.
Live Scroll Only behavior means that the chart will be updated continuously as it is being scrolled. For large data sets or slow client environments, consider selecting Delayed Scroll Only.

845.name: PIE_OTHER_THRESHOLD
845.helpText:
Enter the fraction of the whole pie chart, below which the slices are aggregated into an "Other" slice. Valid values range from 0 (default) to 1

For example, a value of 0.15 would cause all slices which are less than 15% of the pie to be aggregated into the "Other" slice.

846.name: VALUE_MIN
846.helpText: Specify a minimum value for the chart.

847.name: VALUE_FORMAT_TYPE
847.helpText: Select a numeric, date and/or time type of formatting to be applied to the value on the chart. For date and/or time formatting, ensure the chart attribute Time Axis Type is set to one of the following values, depending on your chart data: Enabled, Mixed Frequency, or Skip Gaps. The date and/or time formatting options are only applicable to the x axis of a chart.

lovValues.helpText: When a date is formatted as short, the formatted date will contain year, numeric-month (MM/M), day. For example, 1/6/16.

When a date is formatted as medium, the formatted date will contain year, abbreviated-month (MMM), day. For example, Jan 6, 2016.
        For some languages, abbreviated months are not used; in that case, the medium format will contain the numeric month (MM/M).
When a date is formatted as long, the formatted date will contain year, long-month, day. For example, January 6, 2016.

When a date is formatted as full, the formatted date will contain long-weekday (EEEE), year (y), long-month (MMMM), day (d). For example, Wednesday, January 6, 2016.
        For some languages, long months are not used; for example, in Japanese the numeric month is used in patterns.

When a time is formatted as short, the formatted time will contain hour, minute. For example, 7:30 AM.
        The hour format depends on whether the application language uses 12-hour time or not.

When a time is formatted as medium, the formatted time will contain hour, minute, second. For example, 7:30:21 AM.
        The hour format depends on whether the application language uses 12-hour time or not.

When a time is formatted as long, the formatted time will contain hour, minute, second, and zone (z). For example, 7:30:21 AM.
        The hour format depends on whether the application language uses 12-hour time or not.

When a time is formatted as full, the formatted time will contain hour (h/H), minute (mm), second (ss), and zone (zzzz). For example, 7 h 30 min 21 s.
        The hour format depends on whether the application language uses 12-hour time or not.

When a date-time is formatted as short, the formatted date-time will contain year, numeric-month (MM/M), day, hour, minute. For example, 1/6/16 7:30 AM.
        The hour format depends on whether the application language uses 12-hour time or not.

When a date-time is formatted as medium, the formatted date-time will contain year, abbreviated-month (MMM), day, hour, minute, second, and zone (z). For example, Jan 6, 2016 7:30:21 AM.
        The hour format depends on whether the application language uses 12-hour time or not.

When a date-time is formatted as long, the formatted date-time will contain year, long-month, day, hour, minute, second, and zone (z). For example, Jan 6, 2016 7:30:21 AM.
        The hour format depends on whether the application language uses 12-hour time or not.

When a date-time is formatted as full, the formatted date-time will contain long-weekday (EEEE), year (y), long-month (MMMM), day (d), hour (h/H), minute (mm), second (ss), and zone (zzzz). For example, Wednesday, January 6, 2016 7 h 30 min 21 s.
        The hour format depends on whether the application language uses 12-hour time or not.

When a number is formatted as a decimal, the decimal character is replaced with the most appropriate symbol for the locale. In English this is a decimal point ("."), while in many locales it is a decimal comma (",").
When a number is formatted as currency, the Currency property is required to be set to specify the currency that will be used when formatting the number.
When a number is formatted as a percent, the values on the chart are multiplied by 100 to format as a percent.

848.name: VALUE_CURRENCY
848.helpText: Enter the currency that will be used when formatting the value on the chart. The value should be a ISO 4217 alphabetic currency code. If the format is set to currency, and no currency is defined in the Currency property, the currency will be automatically derived from the application language when the chart is rendered.

849.name: VALUE_NUMERIC_PATTERN
849.examples:
Numeric Pattern to represent temperatures in fahrenheit, for example 15°F:
#°F
Numeric pattern to represent numbers in specific format, for example, 12,30,00:
##,##,##
Numeric pattern to represent numbers in millimeters:
# mm
Date pattern to represent date as Month Year, for example, Jul 2016:
MMM yyyy
Date pattern to represent date as Month, for example, July:
MMMM
849.helpText:
Enter an optional localized numeric or date pattern, where the characters used in the pattern conform to Unicode CLDR for date time formats.
        When present, this will override the Format selected.

85.name: AFFECTED_TYPE
85.helpText: Select how to define the page components to be affected when this action is executed.

lovValues.helpText: The action affects the one or more page items you enter.
The action affects the button you select.
The action affects the region you select.
The action affects the one or more columns you enter.
The action affects the page element identified by the DOM Object or DOM ID you enter.
The action affects the page element(s) returned using the jQuery selector syntax you enter.
The action affects the page element(s) returned using the JavaScript Expression you enter.
The action affects the page element or component that triggered the dynamic action.

The action affects the page element where the event originated, which could be different to the "Triggering Element" in some cases.

In this advanced configuration, the triggering element specified is generally a container element (such as a region) which handles events raised by all of it's sub-elements (such as page items in that region). This selection type can then be used to act upon the sub-element that triggered the event, rather than the container element. For example, if you have a dynamic action that defines a 'Change' event on a region on your page, the action affects the actual item in the region that has changed.

Utilizing 'Event Source' can be a more efficient way of defining common behaviors that affect many page elements. The ability of container elements to catch events raised by sub-elements is determined by the event type. The following event types support this:

  • After Refresh (apexafterrefresh)
  • Before Refresh (apexbeforerefresh)
  • Change (change)
  • Click (click)
  • Double Click (dblclick)
  • Get Focus (focus)
  • Key Down (keydown)
  • Key Press (keypress)
  • Key Release (keyup)
  • Lose Focus (blur)
  • Mouse Button Press (mousedown)
  • Mouse Button Release (mouseup)
  • Mouse Move (mousemove)

850.name: VALUE_FORMAT_SCALING
850.helpText: Select the scaling behavior of the value on the chart.

851.name: JET_SHOW_TOOLTIP
851.helpText: Specify whether a tooltip should be rendered on the chart.

852.name: SHOW_SERIES_NAME
852.helpText: Specify whether the series name should be displayed in the tooltip rendered on the chart.

853.name: SHOW_GROUP_NAME
853.helpText: Specify whether the group name should be displayed in the tooltip rendered on the chart.

854.name: JET_SHOW_VALUE
854.helpText: Specify whether to display values in the tooltip on your chart. Values are derived from your chart query and display next to your chart data.

855.name: JET_SHOW_GANTT_ROW
855.helpText: Specify whether to display row information in the tooltip on your chart.

856.name: JET_SHOW_GANTT_START
856.helpText: Specify whether to display the start date in the tooltip on your chart.

857.name: LEGEND_RENDERED
857.helpText: Specify whether a legend should be rendered on the chart.

858.name: LEGEND_POSITION
858.helpText: Select the position of a legend on the chart.

859.name: HIDE_AND_SHOW_BEHAVIOR
859.helpText:
Select the hide and show behavior that is performed when clicking on a legend item.
        For example, deselecting a legend item will hide its associated data series on the chart.

lovValues.helpText: The chart will not enable the hide and show behavior.
The chart axes will rescale as the minimum and maximum values of the visible data increase or decrease. This is useful for series with largely varying values.
The chart axes will not rescale. This is useful to keep the user in context.

86.name: AFFECTED_REGION
86.helpText: Select the region to be affected by this action.

860.name: OVERVIEW_RENDERED
860.helpText:
Specify whether an overview scrollbar should be rendered on the chart. Currently this option is only supported for vertical bar, line, area, line with area, stock, and combination charts.

Note - The Zoom and Scroll option must be enabled for the overview scrollbar to be displayed.

861.name: OVERVIEW_HEIGHT
861.helpText: Enter the height of the overview scrollbar, in pixels (for example 50px) or percent (for example 15%), to be rendered on the chart.

862.name: CHART_MAX_WIDTH
862.helpText: Enter the maximum width of the chart in pixels. The maximum width defines a fixed width for your chart region. Alternatively, to enable automatic resizing of the chart width, leave this item empty. The width is then automatically set to 100% of the region.

863.name: JET_ZOOM_DIRECTION
863.helpText: Select the zoom direction of the chart.

lovValues.helpText: Zooms in both x and y axes direction.
Zooms only in the x-axis direction.
Zooms only in the y-axis direction.

864.name: JET_SERIES_TYPE_COMBO
864.helpText: Select the chart series type. You can also create a chart combining different types of series on the same data plot.

865.name: JET_SHOW_LABEL
865.helpText: Specify whether to display the label in the tooltip on your chart.

866.name: JET_SHOW_GANTT_END
866.helpText: Specify whether to display the end date in the tooltip on your chart.

867.name: JET_SHOW_GANTT_PROGRESS
867.helpText: Specify whether to display the progress in the tooltip on your chart.

868.name: JET_SHOW_GANTT_BASELINE
868.helpText: Specify whether to display the baseline information in the tooltip on your chart.

869.name: ITEMS_Z_COLUMN_NAME
869.helpText: Select the column name to be used for defining the z value on this chart.  The z value defines the bubble radius for a bubble chart, the width of a box plot item, and the bar width for a bar or combination chart.

87.name: AFFECTED_BUTTON
87.helpText: Select the button to be affected by this action.

870.name: LINK_TARGET_TYPE
870.helpText: Select the action to be performed when the chart is clicked.

lovValues.d: Redirect to Page in this Application
lovValues.helpText: Redirect to a page in the current application, with optional additional attributes for resetting pagination, setting the request value, clearing cache and setting item values, on the target page.

lovValues.d: Redirect to Page in a different Application
lovValues.helpText:
Redirect to a page in a different application, with optional additional attributes for resetting pagination, setting the request value, clearing cache and setting item values, on the target page.

Note: Redirecting to a page in different application relies on deep linking being enabled in the target application. To enable deep linking, go to the application's Security attributes and enable Deep Linking.
Redirect to the target URL you specify.

lovValues.d: Redirect to URL returned by First Column [Deprecated]
lovValues.helpText: Redirect to the target URL returned by the first column of the SQL query.

871.name: ITEMS_MIN_VALUE
871.helpText: Select the column name to be used for defining the minimum value on this chart.

872.name: JET_INITIAL_ZOOMING
872.helpText: Select the initial zooming of the chart.

lovValues.helpText: Initially zoom to the first data points that can fit in the chart plot area.
Initially zoom to the last data points that can fit in the chart plot area.
To disable initial zooming.

873.name: JET_SORT_ORDER
873.helpText: Select the chart sort order of the data on a multi-series chart, based on either the value or label of the chart.

lovValues.helpText: Set to order the chart based on the values in ascending order (1, 2, 3, ...). This setting should only be used for pie charts, bar/line/area charts with one series, or stacked bar/area charts. Sorting will not apply when using a hierarchical group axis.

Set to order the chart based on the values in descending order (10, 9, 8, ...). This setting should only be used for pie charts, bar/line/area charts with one series, or stacked bar/area charts. Sorting will not apply when using a hierarchical group axis.
Set to order the chart based on the x-axis labels in ascending order. This is the default sort order.
Set to order the chart based on the x-axis labels in descending order.

88.name: AFFECTED_ITEMS
88.helpText:
Enter one or more page items to be affected by this action. For multiple items, separate each item name with a comma.

You can type in the name or pick from the list of available items. If you pick from the list and there is already text entered, then a comma is placed at the end of the existing text, followed by the item name returned from the list.

886.name: SERIES_NAME_COLUMN_NAME
886.helpText: Select the column name to be used for defining your multi-series dynamic query.

888.name: ITEMS_LOW_COLUMN_NAME
888.helpText: Select the column name to be used for defining the low value on this chart.

889.name: ITEMS_HIGH_COLUMN_NAME
889.helpText: Select the column name to be used for defining the high value on this chart.

89.name: AFFECTED_DOM_OBJECT
89.helpText:
Enter either a DOM object (document, window) or the id of a DOM object (myElementID) as the element to be affected by this action.

Note: DOM Object is deprecated and should be replaced by JavaScript Expression or jQuery Selector.

890.name: ITEMS_OPEN_COLUMN_NAME
890.helpText: Select the column name to be used for defining the opening value on this chart.

891.name: ITEMS_CLOSE_COLUMN_NAME
891.helpText: Select the column name to be used for defining the closing value on this chart.

892.name: ITEMS_VOLUME_COLUMN_NAME
892.helpText: Select the column name to be used for defining the volume value on this chart. When values are provided, the volume is displayed on the y2 axis.

893.name: ITEMS_X_COLUMN_NAME
893.helpText: Select the column name to be used for defining the x value on this chart.

894.name: ITEMS_Y_COLUMN_NAME
894.helpText: Select the column name to be used for defining the y value on this chart.

895.name: ITEMS_TARGET_VALUE
895.helpText: Select the column name to be used for defining the target value on this chart. When set, the value attribute defines the filled area within the slice and this represents the value of the whole slice.

896.name: ITEMS_MAX_VALUE
896.helpText: Select the column name to be used for defining the maximum value on this chart.

897.name: GROUP_NAME_COLUMN_NAME
897.helpText: Select the column name to be used for defining a short descriptive custom tooltip on the series name(s) on the chart legend. For a Box Plot chart, the column should not match the selected Value column mapping. Selection of a column that matches the Value column mapping will result in no legend tooltip being rendered on the chart.

898.name: GROUP_SHORT_DESC_COLUMN_NAME
898.helpText: Select the column name to be used for defining a short descriptive custom tooltip on the x axis label(s) of the chart. For a Box Plot chart, the column should not match the selected Value column mapping. Selection of a column that matches the Value column mapping will result in no label tooltip being rendered on the chart.

89890006.name: AI_ENABLED
89890006.helpText: Enable the AI Assistant for this component.

89890007.name: AI_CONFIG
89890007.helpText: Select the AI configuration to use for this component.

89890008.name: AI_REMOTE_SERVER
89890008.helpText: Specify the Generative AI Service to be used by the AI Assistant.

89890009.name: AI_SYSTEM_PROMPT
89890009.examples:
You are an expert in marketing. You will be provided with a product description and seed words, and your task is to generate product names.

You are a professional translator. You will be provided with a sentence in English, and your task is to translate it into French.
89890009.helpText:
Specify the initial instructions or context for the AI service. A well-crafted system prompt guides the AI's behavior and sets the tone for its responses. To create an effective system prompt, start by clearly defining the role or expertise you want the AI to assume. Next, describe the specific task or type of responses you expect from the AI.

Note: If you're unsure how to create an effective system prompt, consult the documentation of your AI service for detailed guidance. Additionally, you can ask a generative AI system for help in crafting a prompt. For instance, you might ask "Help me write a system prompt for an AI assistant whose task is to extract relevant tags or keywords from a provided text."

89890010.name: AI_WELCOME_MESSAGE
89890010.helpText: An optional welcome message shown by the AI Assistant.

899.name: ITEMS_LABEL_COLUMN_NAME
899.helpText: Select the column name to be used for defining the label(s) of the x-axis on the chart. For a Stock chart, the column should be of data type Date/Timestamp, to represent the stock information on a time axis.

9.name: PAGE_GROUP
9.helpText:
Specify the page group to associate with this page.
Page groups do not affect functionality, but help developers manage the pages within an application.

90.name: AFFECTED_JQUERY_SELECTOR
90.examples:
To select a page element with an DOM id of my_id
#my_id
To select all the page elements with a class of my_class
.my_class
To select all the page elements that are inputs
input
90.helpText:
Enter jQuery Selector syntax to return one or more page elements to be affected by this action. The jQuery library offers a very powerful selector syntax which provides a way to easily access one or more elements from a page.

Please see the official documentation available from the jQuery homepage for further information about the selector syntax.

900.name: ITEMS_SHORT_DESC_COLUMN_NAME
900.helpText: Select the column name to be used for defining a short descriptive custom tooltip on the data points of the chart. To render a tooltip on chart data points, ensure the chart tooltip attribute Show is set to On. For a Box Plot chart, the column should not match the selected Value column mapping. Selection of a column that matches the Value column mapping will result in no custom tooltip being rendered on the chart.

901.name: JET_SERIES_COLOR
901.examples:
Examples of major HTML color codes include -
  •   Black   #000000 RGB(0,0,0)
  •   Red   #FF0000 RGB(255,0,0)
  •   Yellow   #FFFF00 RGB(255,255,0)
  •   Lime   #00FF00 RGB(0,255,0)
  •   Green   #008000 RGB(0,128,0)
  •   Aqua   #00FFFF RGB(0,255,255)
  •   Blue   #0000FF RGB(0,255,255)
  •   Navy   #000080 RGB(0,0,128)
  •   White   #FFFFFF RGB(255,255,255)
901.helpText:
Enter the color to be displayed for the data items associated with this chart series. You can utilize &COLUMN_VALUE. substitutions. For a Status Meter Gauge chart, this color will be applied to the indicator, with the exception of when thresholds have been defined, and the Threshold Display attribute is set to On Indicator.

The color is specified using hexadecimal (hex) notation, RGB color codes, or HTML color names. Hex notation is defined as #xxyyzz (a # followed by 3 double digit hex numbers), where xx, yy, and zz represent the two character hex values for red, green and blue respectively. RGB codes are defined as RGB(xxx,xxx,xxx), where xxx is a number between 0 and 255 each representing the single 8-bit byte value for red, green, and blue respectively.

Search the internet for 'HTML Color Codes' to find the equivalent hex code or RGB code for the color you wish to utilize.

902.name: LINE_STYLE
902.helpText: Specify the style of the line to be rendered on the chart.

903.name: LINE_WIDTH
903.helpText: Specify the width of the line to be rendered on the chart.

904.name: LINE_TYPE
904.helpText: Specify the type of line to be rendered on the chart.

905.name: MARKER_RENDERED
905.helpText: Specify whether a marker should be rendered on the data items of the chart.

906.name: MARKER_SHAPE
906.helpText: Select the shape of the marker to be rendered on the data items of the chart. Only auto is supported for range series.

907.name: ASSIGNED_TO_Y2
907.helpText: Specify whether the current series is assigned to the Y2 axis rendered on the chart.

908.name: ITEMS_LABEL_RENDERED
908.helpText: Specify whether the label(s) should be rendered on the chart. This setting applies to the visibility of the metric value on a Dial chart.

909.name: ITEMS_LABEL_POSITION
909.helpText: Select the position of the label(s) to be rendered on the chart.

91.name: EXEC_STOP_EXECUTION_ON_ERROR
91.helpText:
Specify whether processing of all other pending actions is stopped when an error occurs while executing the current action.

Note: The order of execution of specific actions is determined by the sequence specified for each action. To ensure that actions are run in the same order, Oracle recommends that the sequence numbers be unique for all True Actions and all False Actions.

910.name: ITEMS_LABEL_CSS_CLASSES
910.helpText: Enter a CSS style string defining the style of the labels on this chart.

912.name: JET_SHOW_AXIS
912.helpText: Specify whether the axis is rendered on the chart.

913.name: AXIS_MIN
913.helpText: Enter the minimum value of the axis. Defaults to null for automatic calculation based on the data.

914.name: AXIS_MAX
914.helpText: Enter the maximum value of the axis. Defaults to null for automatic calculation based on the data.

915.name: RELOAD_ON_SUBMIT
915.helpText: Select when the page should be reloaded following a page submission.

lovValues.helpText: Always reload the page to display errors and the success message.
Show errors dynamically without reloading page, but reload it after a successful processing.

916.name: PAGE_WARN_ON_UNSAVED_CHANGES
916.helpText:
Specify if the user is warned when trying to navigate away from the page, where the page contains unsaved changes. Page Items and Buttons also offer more granular control over when this check is performed, and what is included in it. For Buttons, you can specify if clicking the button will perform the check. For Page Items, you can specify if changes to the item are included, or ignored by the check (see the Warn on Unsaved Changes attribute for both).

Note: This does not apply to an end user closing a Modal dialog page.

917.name: VALUE_BASELINE_SCALING
917.helpText: Select whether the axis baseline starts at the minimum value of the data or at zero. Only applies to numerical data axes.

918.name: AXIS_STEP
918.helpText: Enter the increment between major tick marks. Defaults to null for automatic calculation based on the data. Only applies to time and numerical axes.

919.name: AXIS_POSITION
919.helpText: Select the position of the label(s) to be rendered on the chart.

92.name: WAIT_FOR_RESULT
92.helpText:
Specify whether all pending actions wait for the result of the current action. Set this attribute to On if pending actions are dependent on the result of this action, or to Off if there is no dependency and they can execute asynchronously, without waiting.

Note: The order of execution of specific actions is determined by the sequence specified for each action. To ensure that actions are run in the same order, Oracle recommends that the sequence numbers be unique for all True Actions and all False Actions.

920.name: MAJOR_TICK_RENDERED
920.helpText: Select whether the major tick marks are rendered.

921.name: MIN_STEP
921.helpText: Enter the minimum increment between major tick marks. This is typically used to prevent fractional axis values for discrete measures.

922.name: MINOR_TICK_RENDERED
922.helpText: Specify whether the minor tick marks are rendered.

923.name: MINOR_STEP
923.helpText: Enter the increment between minor tick marks. Defaults to null for automatic calculation based on the data. Only applies to numerical axes.

924.name: TICK_LABEL_RENDERED
924.helpText: Specify whether the tick labels are rendered.

925.name: TICK_LABEL_ROTATION
925.helpText:
Specify whether the chart will automatically rotate the labels by 90 degrees in order to fit more labels on the axis.
        The rotation will only be applied to categorical labels for a horizontal axis.

926.name: TICK_LABEL_POSITION
926.helpText: Select the position of the tick labels relative to the plot area.

927.name: SPLIT_DUAL_Y
927.helpText: Specify whether the plot area is split into two sections, so that sets of data assigned to the different Y-axes appear in different parts of the plot area. Stock charts do not support No.

928.name: SPLITTER_POSITION
928.helpText: In a split dual-Y chart, specify the fraction of the space that is given to the Y-axis subchart. Valid values are numbers from 0 to 1.

929.name: PIE_SELECTION_EFFECT
929.helpText: Select the effect applied when a pie segment is selected.

93.name: ITEM_TYPE
93.helpText:
Specify how this item is rendered. For more information on specific item types, see About Item Types.

The following item types are supported:

#NATIVE_PLUGINS#

Depending on your application configuration, you may also have additional item type plug-ins available here. These display as <My Plug-in> [Plug-in]. The following plug-ins install into this application's shared components:

#CUSTOM_PLUGINS#

930.name: STOCK_RENDER_AS
930.helpText: Select the series type to be applied to the rendered stock chart.

931.name: REFRESH_INTERVAL
931.helpText: Enter the interval in seconds between chart updates. Very small updates intervals, such as 2 seconds, are discouraged since they may cause serious database performance issues.

935.name: CUSTOM_COLUMN_NAME
935.helpText: Specify the custom column name, which can be used for defining a custom tooltip, or database-based colors to be used for the chart elements. For a Box Plot chart, the column should not match the selected Value column mapping. Selection of a column that matches the Value column mapping will result in no custom column being used for the chart.

939.name: AXIS_SCALING
939.helpText: Select the axis scale. Only applies to numerical axes.

94.name: REGION_TYPE
94.helpText:
Specify how this region is rendered. The following region types are supported:

#NATIVE_PLUGINS#

Depending on your application configuration, you may also have additional region type plug-ins available here. The following plug-ins are installed within this application's shared components:

#CUSTOM_PLUGINS#

940.name: ITEM_WARN_ON_UNSAVED_CHANGES
940.helpText: Specify if the page item is included in the unsaved changes check, which warns the user when they try to navigate away from the page, and where the page contains unsaved changes. The following APEX Pseudo Hints are available:
APEX$USE_OFFSET_PAGINATION
Use the OFFSET m ROWS FETCH n ROWS (SQL2008) syntax, instead of the ROW_NUMBER analytic function, when generating pagination SQL. The executed query will only return rows of interest for the current component page.
APEX$USE_ROWNUM_PAGINATION
Use the ROWNUM pseudo column, instead of the ROW_NUMBER analytic function, when generating pagination SQL. The executed query will only return rows of interest for the current component page.
APEX$USE_NO_PAGINATION
Do not build any pagination SQL. The component always starts fetching at the first row; the current page is shown by skipping rows and stopping after fetching the last row of interest.
APEX$USE_NO_BULK_FETCH
Do not use bulk fetching for this query.
APEX$USE_NO_GROUPING_SETS
Do not use the GROUPING SETS SQL clause for Faceted Search or Smart Filters. Instead, compute counts for each facet or filter using an individual query, and combine these with UNION ALL.
975.helpText:
Enter the Oracle Optimizer hint which is added to the top-level statement when executing the SQL query generated by Oracle APEX. A hint is an instruction to the Optimizer. When writing SQL, you may know information about the data unknown to the Optimizer. Hints enable you to make decisions normally made by the Optimizer, sometimes causing the Optimizer to select a plan that it sees as higher cost.

For example, you might know that a certain index is more selective for certain queries. Based on this information, you might be able to choose a more efficient execution plan than the Optimizer. In such a case, use hints to force the Optimizer to use the optimal execution plan.

1088.accessibilityHelpText:
Help text plays a crucial role in providing additional information and guidance to users, particularly those who may require assistance or clarification while interacting with an interface. By ensuring that help text is accessible and effectively communicates its purpose, you enhance the usability and inclusivity of your application.

Best Practices:
  1. Clear and Concise: Keep help text clear and concise to facilitate easy understanding for all users. Avoid using overly technical language or jargon that may be confusing to some users.
  2. Contextual Guidance: Provide help text that is contextually relevant to the task or element it is associated with. This helps users understand how to complete a specific action or navigate through the interface effectively.
  3. Sensory Characteristics: Ensure instructions provided through help do not rely solely on sensory characteristics of page elements (such as shape, color, size or visual location). For example, instead of saying 'click the button in the top right of the page', better help text would be 'click the button labelled "Next" in the top right of the page' (so the instruction is not reliant on location alone).

13.helpText:
Enter a title that will be displayed in the title bar of the browser window, and announced to screen reader users when they first open the page. The Oracle APEX engine uses the title you specify here in place of the #TITLE# substitution string used in the page template. This title is inserted between the HTML tags <TITLE> and </TITLE>.

A good page title should provide a clear and concise description of the purpose of the page, can include the application name and sub-section of the application for additional context, and should always include the most important, and unique information first. For example, if you have a 'Products' page in an 'Administration' section of a 'Customer Portal' application, the page title could be defined as 'Products | Admin | Customer Portal'.
13.accessibilityHelpText:
Page titles are crucial for helping all users understand the purpose of a page, especially those using assistive technology like screen readers. Since the page title is often the first thing heard by a screen reader user, it's essential to make sure every page title is meaningful and unique.

Best Practices:

  1. Clear and Descriptive: Use specific titles like "Understanding WCAG 2.1" or section titles for easy navigation.
  2. Effective: Consider the following example: For a Form page, include relevant information like the record being edited, such as "Create / Edit Customer: [customer name]." Follow these steps in Page Designer:
    1. Select the page in the Rendering tree.
    2. In the Property Editor, locate the Identification - Title field.
    3. Replace P1_CUSTOMER_NAME with the appropriate page item containing the record identifier.
    4. Enter the title format as Create / Edit Customer: &P1_CUSTOMER_NAME. (include the period).

Implementing descriptive page and regions titles significantly enhances accessibility, enabling seamless navigation and content understanding for users across diverse web environments.

24.helpText:
Select an authorization scheme applied to the page. Authorization schemes are defined at the application-level and can be applied to many elements within the application.

An authorization scheme is evaluated either once for each application session (at session creation), or once for each page view. If the selected authorization scheme evaluates to TRUE, then the page displays and is subject to other defined conditions. If it evaluates to FALSE, then the page does not display and an error message displays.

915.accessibilityHelpText:
For improved accessibility, opt for the "Only for Success" option for several reasons:

Best Practices:
  1. Dynamic Error Display: Display errors dynamically without reloading the page.
  2. Contextual Reload: Reload the page after successful processing to maintain user context.
  3. Avoiding Full Page Reloads: Opting for this approach minimizes full page reloads and prevents unnecessary context changes for the user.

916.accessibilityHelpText: When designing web pages, it's essential to prioritize user experience by implementing features that prevent data loss. By enabling the page warn on unsaved changes functionality, users are notified when attempting to navigate away from a page containing unsaved modifications. This feature not only enhances usability but also ensures data integrity and user satisfaction.

1.accessibilityHelpText:
Ensure clear, descriptive titles for each region to aid user navigation and content understanding without relying on page context.

Best Practices:
  • Clear and Descriptive: The title should provide a clear and concise description of the content or purpose of the region. Avoid vague or ambiguous titles.

129.helpText: Enter the value substituted into region attributes. Region templates that contain the substitution string #REGION_ATTRIBUTES# are substituted with this value.

1604.accessibilityHelpText:
Alternative Text, serves as a crucial element to enhance accessibility for users with visual impairments. It provides a textual description of images within documents or webpages, offering insights into their significance in relation to the content.

Best practices:
  1. Purposeful Description:
    • Alt Text should succinctly convey the significance of the image in relation to the surrounding content.
    • Focus on describing the "why" of the image rather than stating what the image is.
    • Keep Alt Text clear, concise, and descriptive.
    2. Example:

    "Team celebrating with high-fives and smiles after successfully completing a challenging project."

    In this example, the alt text emphasizes the reason behind the image, which is the successful completion of a challenging project and the resulting celebration among team members. This description provides context and insight into the significance of the image for users who cannot see it directly.
  2. Informative Images: Identify images that contribute to the comprehension or context of the webpage. If removing the image would diminish the page's meaning or significance, it requires Alt Text.
  3. Avoid Redundancy: Omit phrases like "image of" as screen readers automatically announce an image as such.

1669.accessibilityHelpText:
Landmarks provide a powerful way to identify the organization and structure of a web page. The structural information conveyed visually to users should be represented programmatically in the markup using landmark roles. The use of landmarks roles support keyboard navigation to the structure of a web page for screen reader users, and can be used as targets for browser extensions for enhanced keyboard navigation.

When using landmarks, all perceivable content (eg all items, buttons, regions, menus, etc. of an APEX app) should be contained in a landmark, in order that content is not missed by the user. When labelling landmarks, you have the option to either use the region title (default), or define a custom Landmark Label on the region.

1670.nullHelpText: Uses the default landmark type defined in the region template.
1670.accessibilityHelpText:
Why landmark types matter:

  • Clarity & Navigation: Each type signifies a specific section's purpose, helping users understand and navigate the page efficiently.
  • Accessibility Tools: Screen readers and other assistive technologies depend on these landmarks to offer context and streamline user interaction.
  • Standardized Structure: Choosing the right landmark type promotes a consistent and intuitive browsing experience for all users.

1671.accessibilityHelpText:
It is important to provide good labels that truly improve user experience. Good labels are defined as follows:

  • Unique on a page, and not too long (preferably 3 words or less).
  • Accurately describe the purpose of the contents of the region, for example 'Edit Employee', or 'Useful Links'.
  • Do not use the landmark role in the label, for example the label for a navigation landmark for an application should just be 'Application', rather than 'Application Navigation', to avoid screen readers announcing 'navigation' twice.

127.accessibilityHelpText:
Placeholder text serves as a helpful guide within input fields. When implemented thoughtfully, it aids users in understanding the expected input without overshadowing accessibility or creating confusion.

Best Practices:

  • Clear and Concise: Keep placeholder text brief yet informative.

942.accessibilityHelpText:
Help text plays a crucial role in providing additional information and guidance to users, particularly those who may require assistance or clarification while interacting with an interface. By ensuring that help text is accessible and effectively communicates its purpose, you enhance the usability and inclusivity of your application.

Best Practices:
  1. Clear and Concise: Keep help text clear and concise to facilitate easy understanding for all users. Avoid using overly technical language or jargon that may be confusing to some users.
  2. Contextual Guidance: Provide help text that is contextually relevant to the task or element it is associated with. This helps users understand how to complete a specific action or navigate through the interface effectively.
  3. Sensory Characteristics: Ensure instructions provided through help do not rely solely on sensory characteristics of page elements (such as shape, color, size or visual location). For example, instead of saying 'click the button in the top right of the page', better help text would be 'click the button labelled "Next" in the top right of the page' (so the instruction is not reliant on location alone).

1601.accessibilityHelpText:
When designing message confirmation dialogs or prompts, it's essential to consider accessibility to ensure all users can easily understand and interact with the confirmation message.

Best Practices:
  1. Clear and Informative Content: Ensure that the confirmation message provides clear and concise information about the action being confirmed. Use straightforward language that is easy to understand for all users.
  2. Accessible Formatting: Format the confirmation message in a way that is accessible to users with various assistive technologies, such as screen readers. Use semantic HTML elements and provide alternative text for any non-text elements like buttons.
  3. Consistent Design: Maintain consistency in the design and placement of message confirmation dialogs across your application or website. Consistency helps users predict the location of the confirmation message and reduces confusion.
  4. User Control: Provide users with the option to review their action before confirming, especially for critical or irreversible actions. This empowers users to make informed decisions and reduces the likelihood of unintentional actions.

By following these accessibility considerations, you can ensure that message confirmation dialogs are inclusive and usable for all users, regardless of their abilities or assistive technology usage.

6.accessibilityHelpText:
Accessible error suggestions foster a more inclusive user experience, aiding users of varying abilities in rectifying input errors efficiently.

Best Practices:
  1. Clear and Descriptive: Error messages should clearly describe the problem or issue encountered by the user in a concise and understandable manner. Avoid using technical jargon or ambiguous language that may confuse users.
  2. Provide Solutions: Offer clear instructions or suggestions on how users can resolve the error.
  3. Error Identification: Clearly identify the field or input element that triggered the error. Provide sufficient context to help users understand which part of the form or application needs attention.
  4. Consistent: Maintain consistency in the format and style of error messages throughout the application or website. Consistent error messaging helps users understand and navigate the interface more effectively.
Examples:
  • Error: "Invalid email address. Please enter a valid email format (e.g., example@example.com)."
  • Error: "Insufficient funds. Please add funds to your account to complete the transaction."

331.accessibilityHelpText:
Alt text communicates the information conveyed by icons to users of assistive technology, ensuring website accessibility.

Best Practices:

  1. Determining Alt Text Need: Evaluate whether the absence of the icon would impact page comprehension. If the page would lose meaning without the icon, add alt text.
  2. Considerations for Text: Assess the presence of adjacent text and its relevance to the icon's purpose.
  3. Recommendations:
    • Including text with icons enhances the clickable/touchable area for links or buttons.
    • Adding alt text to stand-alone icons without visible adjacent text ensures accessibility for all users.
    • Utilize consistent, clear and understandable icons
