272.accessibilityHelpText:
Column headings play a crucial role in organizing and presenting tabular data in a clear and understandable format.

Best Practices:
  1. Descriptive and Meaningful: Use descriptive and meaningful column headings that accurately represent the content of each column. Column headings should succinctly convey the information contained within the respective columns.
  2. Consistency: Maintain consistency in column headings throughout the table. Consistent column headings facilitate navigation and comprehension for users, especially when interacting with complex tables containing multiple columns.

290.accessibilityHelpText:
Accessible link text is essential for users of assistive technologies, such as screen readers, to navigate and understand content effectively.

Best Practices:
  1. Conciseness: Keep link text concise while ensuring it conveys the necessary information. Aim for a balance between brevity and descriptiveness.
  2. Accessibility Attributes: Ensure report column row headers are defined. Defining this attribute improves the navigation experience for screen reader users by providing clear orientation points within the tabular data.
  3. Repeated links: In a typical report, each row often features a repeating link, such as an edit option. In such cases, the most effective link text would be 'Edit', and paired with a clear row header.

By following these best practices for link text, you can create a more inclusive and accessible browsing experience for all users, including those with disabilities.

397.accessibilityHelpText:
It's crucial to define row headers for tabular report data, such as in Classic or Interactive Reports, to enhance usability for users of assistive technologies like screen readers.

Best Practices:
  1. Impact on Usability for Screen Reader Users:
    • When a screen reader user navigates through different rows of the report, the column or columns designated as identifying the row will be announced as the row header upon moving to the new row.
    • Failure to define a row header column makes it significantly more challenging for screen reader users to orient themselves while navigating the report.
  2. Enhancing Orientation and Navigation:
    • Defining this attribute improves the navigation experience for screen reader users by providing clear orientation points within the tabular data.
    • This ensures smoother navigation and comprehension of the report's content for users relying on assistive technologies.
  3. Recommendations:
    • Define, one or more columns that identify the row, that will function as the row header for users of Assistive Technology.
    • This will be announced every time a user moves between rows, so the entire row header should not be too long to become overly verbose.

426.accessibilityHelpText:
The Image Description property serves as a vital component in improving accessibility for users with visual impairments. It enables the provision of text or a reference to a column containing text to describe the image. It is important to define descriptions for images that can be displayed as part of reports, such as in Classic or Interactive Reports, to improve usability for users of assistive technologies, such as screen readers.

Best practices:
  1. Informative Images: Identify images that contribute to the comprehension or context of the webpage. If removing the image would diminish the page's meaning or significance, it requires the image description. If removing the image would not diminish the page's meaning (for example if it was just decorative), then leave the image description blank and it will be ignored by screen readers.
  2. Purposeful Description:
    • Alt Text should succinctly convey the significance of the image in relation to the surrounding content.
    • Focus on describing the "why" of the image rather than stating what the image is.
    • Keep Alt Text clear, concise, and descriptive.
    3. Example:

    "Stylish pink tote bag with faux leather straps, perfect for adding a pop of color to your outfit".

  3. Avoid Redundancy: Omit phrases like "image of" as screen readers automatically announce an image as such.

804.helpText:
Enter the alternative label to use in dialogs and in various column heading placements.
        Use an alternative label when the heading contains extra formatting, such as HTML tags, which do not display properly.

Report regions can be printed using the standard print link, shown below the report region, or using a button. If you want to use a button, remove the link label and create a button on your page, using the URL shown in Print URL as the button target.

This is useful if you are planning to support printing to several different output formats (Word, Excel, PDF, and so on) and want to display a button, link, or image for each option. 97.helpText:
Enter the display sequence for this column. The sequence setting determines where this column is displayed in relation to other columns within the region.

Note: If two columns, within the same region, have the same sequence value then they may be displayed in a different order when the application is exported and imported into another environment, such as a test or production environment. 380.accessibilityHelpText:
Clear titles, and labels are crucial for making visualizations accessible to all users.

Best Practices:
  • Descriptive Title: Use descriptive titles that clearly explain what the visualization depicts and guide readers on what to focus on.

By adhering to these principles, you can enhance the accessibility of your visualizations for all users, including those with visual impairments or color blindness.

588.helpText: Specify the number of decimal places to be applied to the numeric value on the chart.

844.helpText: Specify the zoom and scroll behavior of the chart. Live behavior means that the chart will be updated continuously as it is being manipulated, while Delayed means that the update will wait until the zoom/scroll action is done. While Live zoom and scroll provides the best end user experience, no guarantees are made about the rendering performance or usability for large data sets or slow client environments. If performance is an issue, Delayed zoom and scroll should be used instead.

847.helpText: Specify the type of formatting to be applied to the value on the chart. The formats Decimal,Percent or Currency only apply to numeric values. The Date,Time and DateTime formats will only apply to values of that data type on the chart.

849.helpText: Specify the numeric pattern to be applied to the numeric value on the chart.

857.accessibilityHelpText:
When it comes to accessibility best practices for charts, it's essential to consider how to make the information contained within the chart accessible to all users, including those with disabilities.

Best Practices:
  • Text Equivalents: If the chart legend contains crucial information that is not otherwise available in the chart itself, then it should be included in the chart.

943.examples:
function( options ){
    // Setup a callback function which gets called when data is retrieved, it allows to manipulate the series
    options.dataFilter = function( data ) {
        data.series[ 0 ].color = "#00FF00";
        return data;
    };
    // Set chart initialization options
    options.type = "line";
    return options;
}

1053.accessibilityHelpText:
Enhancing chart accessibility through mindful color selection and compliance with WCAG standards is crucial for ensuring inclusivity in data visualization.

272.accessibilityHelpText:
Column headings play a crucial role in organizing and presenting tabular data in a clear and understandable format.

Best Practices:
  1. Descriptive and Meaningful: Use descriptive and meaningful column headings that accurately represent the content of each column. Column headings should succinctly convey the information contained within the respective columns.
  2. Consistency: Maintain consistency in column headings throughout the table. Consistent column headings facilitate navigation and comprehension for users, especially when interacting with complex tables containing multiple columns.

290.accessibilityHelpText:
Accessible link text is essential for users of assistive technologies, such as screen readers, to navigate and understand content effectively.

Best Practices:
  1. Conciseness: Keep link text concise while ensuring it conveys the necessary information. Aim for a balance between brevity and descriptiveness.
  2. Accessibility Attributes: Ensure report column row headers are defined. Defining this attribute improves the navigation experience for screen reader users by providing clear orientation points within the tabular data.
  3. Repeated links: In a typical report, each row often features a repeating link, such as an edit option. In such cases, the most effective link text would be 'Edit', and paired with a clear row header.

By following these best practices for link text, you can create a more inclusive and accessible browsing experience for all users, including those with disabilities.

397.accessibilityHelpText:
It's crucial to define row headers for tabular report data, such as in Classic or Interactive Reports, to enhance usability for users of assistive technologies like screen readers.

Best Practices:
  1. Impact on Usability for Screen Reader Users:
    • When a screen reader user navigates through different rows of the report, the column or columns designated as identifying the row will be announced as the row header upon moving to the new row.
    • Failure to define a row header column makes it significantly more challenging for screen reader users to orient themselves while navigating the report.
  2. Enhancing Orientation and Navigation:
    • Defining this attribute improves the navigation experience for screen reader users by providing clear orientation points within the tabular data.
    • This ensures smoother navigation and comprehension of the report's content for users relying on assistive technologies.
  3. Recommendations:
    • Define, one or more columns that identify the row, that will function as the row header for users of Assistive Technology.
    • This will be announced every time a user moves between rows, so the entire row header should not be too long to become overly verbose.

1157.accessibilityHelpText:
The icon description serves as a vital accessibility feature by providing contextual information about an icon when it receives focus or is hovered over. This feature enhances user understanding and interaction with the interface.

Best Practices:
  1. Clear and Concise: Icon descriptions should be clear and succinct, providing users with a brief but informative understanding of the icon's function or purpose.
  2. Descriptive Language: Use descriptive language that accurately conveys the meaning or action associated with the icon. Avoid ambiguous or vague descriptions that may confuse users.
  3. Determining Alt Text Need: Evaluate whether the absence of the icon would impact page comprehension. If the page would lose meaning without the icon, add alt text.

1171.accessibilityHelpText:
The media description serves as a vital accessibility feature by providing contextual information about a media when it receives focus or is hovered over. This feature enhances user understanding and interaction with the interface.

Best Practices:
  1. Clear and Concise: Media description should be clear and succinct, providing users with a brief but informative understanding of the media's function or purpose.
  2. Descriptive Language: Use descriptive language that accurately conveys the meaning or action associated with the media. Avoid ambiguous or vague descriptions that may confuse users.
  3. Determining Alt Text Need: Evaluate whether the absence of the media would impact page comprehension. If the page would lose meaning without the media, add the media description.

780.helpText:
Specify whether to load the region independently of the data for the region.

When lazy loading is specified, the page is rendered immediately, showing an empty region, until the data is loaded. Generally, the page is not displayed until all of the page is loaded and ready to be rendered. Therefore, if it takes 5 seconds to load all of the data for a region, without lazy loading, the end user would have to wait 5 seconds before the page started to render.

Note - Lazy Loading should only be utilized on data sets that take significant time to load, as this adds unnecessary processing overhead on the database for regions that load quickly.

1539.accessibilityHelpText:
The stroke color of a map serves to ensure that individuals with moderately low vision can effectively distinguish boundaries between adjoining segments of colors in a map.

Best Practices:

  1. Color Selection Considerations:
    • When selecting colors for maps with multiple colors, it's crucial to consider the contrast ratio between adjoining colors.
    • Ensure that the contrast ratio between adjoining colors is at least 3:1 to facilitate clear differentiation.
  2. Testing and Adjustment Procedures:
    • Utilize accessibility testing tools or manual checks to ensure compliance with the minimum contrast ratio requirement.
    • If the contrast ratio falls below 3:1 for any adjoining colors, implement corrective measures to enhance visibility.
    • Consider adding borders with contrasting colors to visually separate adjoining segments and improve clarity.
  3. Considerations for Color Blindness:
    • Take into account the prevalence of color blindness among users and design with consideration for their needs.
    • Avoid relying solely on color to convey information; incorporate other visual cues, such as patterns or textures, to supplement color distinctions.
    • Ensure that color choices accommodate common types of color blindness, such as red-green deficiency, by selecting colors that remain distinguishable in various color vision scenarios.

1541.accessibilityHelpText:
Best Practices:
  • Check Color Contrast Ratio: Ensure there is sufficient contrast between the background color and stroke color to facilitate clear differentiation of the highlighted area on the map. Aim for a ratio of at least 3:1 to ensure readability for individuals with varying levels of vision impairment as well as the borders or stroke color outlining various features. Adequate contrast is crucial for users to easily perceive and discern these visual elements, enhancing the overall legibility and usability of the map interface.

1557.accessibilityHelpText:
Ensure that the color of a Point Clustering fill meets certain criteria to enhance visibility and usability for all users.

Best Practices:
  1. Contrast Ratio: The Point Clustering fill must have a contrast ratio of at least (3:1) in comparison to its background. This ensures that users with visual impairments can discern the clustered points effectively.
  2. Differentiation from Standard Fill Color: The Point Clustering fill color should also be distinguishable from the standard fill color. This distinction is crucial for users to easily differentiate between clustered points and standard data points, facilitating improved data comprehension and interaction.

By adhering to these guidelines, we strive to create a more inclusive and accessible experience for all users, regardless of their visual abilities.

5110.name: NATIVE_CSS_CALENDAR

5110.helpText: Display date based entries on a variety of calendar views. With the inclusion of an end date, the calendar can display duration based events. Calendars can also update records directly if "Drag and Drop" is enabled.

attributes.helpText:
Enter the maximum number of events displayed for each day within the Month view.

If there are more than the specified number of events on a specific day, that day will include More .... Clicking on this item will display a pop-up window with all of the events for that specific day.

attributes.examples:
Styling the calendar based on project status

select ID,
       START_DATE,
       END_DATE,
       TASK_NAME,
       case STATUS
           when 'Open'    then 'apex-cal-green'
           when 'Pending' then 'apex-cal-yellow'
           when 'Closed'  then 'apex-cal-red'
           when 'On-Hold' then 'apex-cal-black'
       end as css_class,
       ASSIGNED_TO as supplemental_info
  from PROJECTS
attributes.helpText:
Select the column which holds the CSS Class to style the events displayed on this calendar.
There are a number of default classes available:

  • apex-cal-cyan
  • apex-cal-blue
  • apex-cal-bluesky
  • apex-cal-darkblue
  • apex-cal-green

Note: The multiple line events setting is only used within Month view. For Weekly and Daily views the duration of the event determines the height of the event displayed.

Displays time using the 12 hour clock including a.m. (from the Latin ante meridiem, meaning "before midday") and p.m. (post meridiem, "after midday"), such as 8:00 a.m. and 4:00 p.m.

The actual display format for a.m./p.m., such as capitalization and periods, is derived from the Timestamp Format.
Displays time using the 24 hour clock, such as 08:00 and 16:00.

attributes.helpText: Select the time format used to display the time portion of an event for this calendar.

Select the column which holds the primary key value for calendar events. If the table has a multi-part primary key, then select ROWID.

The value of this column is returned in the APEX$PK_VALUE substitution variable. Utilize this variable in the Drag and Drop Code attribute to identify the record to be updated, following the drag and drop operation on the calendar.
Enter a target page to be called when the user clicks an existing entry.

Enter a target page to be called when the user clicks an empty cell, or outside of an existing calendar entry.

You need to use the special calendar substitution variables 

&APEX$NEW_START_DATE.
and 
&APEX$NEW_END_DATE.
to pass the selected dates from the calendar to the target page.

Specify whether drag and drop operations are permitted on this calendar.

Note: If drag and drop is enabled, then any end users who have rights to view this calendar, also have rights to update calendar entries.

attributes.examples:
Example with Start Date only (for non-duration based events)
begin
    update emp
       set hiredate = to_date(:APEX$NEW_START_DATE, 'YYYYMMDDHH24MISS')
     where empno = :APEX$PK_VALUE;
end;
Example with Start and End dates. (for duration based events)
begin
    update projects
       set start_date = to_date(:APEX$NEW_START_DATE, 'YYYYMMDDHH24MISS'),
           end_date = to_date(:APEX$NEW_END_DATE, 'YYYYMMDDHH24MISS')
     where id = :APEX$PK_VALUE;
end;
attributes.helpText:
Enter the PL/SQL code to update the underlying tables or updateable views when a calendar entry is updated using drag and drop.

If this calendar shows duration-based events (by selecting a column for End Date), then the PL/SQL code also needs to update this value. If the whole event is dragged, then the End Date maintains the current duration. If the end of the event is dragged, the duration of the event is updated. In such cases the start date will be unchanged, but the end date is updated to reflect the revised duration.

The calendar substitution variables include:

APEX$NEW_START_DATE
Returns the revised start date. The date format is 'YYYYMMDDHH24MISS' even if the Show Time for this calendar is No.
APEX$NEW_END_DATE
Returns the revised end date for duration based events. The date format is 'YYYYMMDDHH24MISS' even if the Show Time for this calendar is No.
APEX$PK_VALUE
Returns the value of the column specified in the Primary Key Column.

Select which additional calendar views to display. The month view is always displayed.

Note: the Weekly and Daily views are not available if Show Time is specified as No.

Choose which export links are provided at the bottom of the calendar.

Note: This exports all of the calendar entries currently displayed, not a single calendar entry.
Select which calendar views to display. At least one of Day, Week or Month must be selected. If not, the calendar will automatically display the month view.

Select whether the time portion of the date should be displayed.

The Week and Day views will only be displayed when Show Time is set to Yes. If the start date or end date columns do not include time components they will be shown as 12:00 am.

function ( pOptions) {

    pOptions.dayHeaderFormat  = { weekday: 'short', month: 'numeric', day: 'numeric' }; // week view column headings
    pOptions.slotDuration     = "00:15:00";                                             // custom slot duration
    pOptions.weekNumbers      = true;                                                   // show week numbers
    pOptions.weekText         = "CW";                                    
    return pOptions;
}

attributes.accessibilityHelpText:
Accessible link text is essential for users of assistive technologies, such as screen readers, to navigate and understand content effectively.

Best Practices:
  1. Descriptive Text: Use descriptive and meaningful text that clearly indicates the purpose or destination of the link. Avoid generic terms like "click here" or "read more."
  2. Conciseness: Keep link text concise while ensuring it conveys the necessary information. Aim for a balance between brevity and descriptiveness.
Example Link Text:
  • Generic: "Click here for more information"
  • Descriptive: "Read the latest blog post"
  • Contextual: "Learn about accessibility best practices"

By following these best practices for link text, you can create a more inclusive and accessible browsing experience for all users, including those with disabilities.

attributes.accessibilityHelpText:
It's crucial to define row headers for tabular report data, such as in Classic or Interactive Reports, to enhance usability for users of assistive technologies like screen readers.

Best Practices:
  1. Impact on Usability for Screen Reader Users:
    • When a screen reader user navigates through different rows of the report, the column or columns designated as identifying the row will be announced as the row header upon moving to the new row.
    • Failure to define a row header column makes it significantly more challenging for screen reader users to orient themselves while navigating the report.
  2. Enhancing Orientation and Navigation:
    • Defining this attribute improves the navigation experience for screen reader users by providing clear orientation points within the tabular data.
    • This ensures smoother navigation and comprehension of the report's content for users relying on assistive technologies.
  3. Recommendations:
    • Define, one or more columns that identify the row, that will function as the row header for users of Assistive Technology.
    • This will be announced every time a user moves between rows, so the entire row header should not be too long to become overly verbose.

Enter the color used for the foreground of this graph. The color is specified using hexadecimal (hex) notation, RGB color codes, or HTML color names.

Hex notation is defined as #xxyyzz (a # followed by 3 double digit hex numbers), where xx, yy, and zz represent the two character hex values for red, green and blue respectively. RGB codes are defined as RGB(xxx,xxx,xxx), where xxx is a number between 0 and 255 each representing the single 8-bit byte value for red, green, and blue respectively.

Search the internet for 'HTML Color Codes' to find the equivalent hex code or RGB code for the color you wish to utilize.
attributes.accessibilityHelpText:
Enhancing graph accessibility through mindful color selection and compliance with WCAG standards is crucial for ensuring inclusivity in data visualization.

Best Practices:
  • Check Color Contrast Ratio: Utilize contrast checking tools to evaluate the color contrast ratio between foreground and background colors. Aim for a ratio of at least 3:1 against adjacent colors to ensure readability for individuals with varying levels of vision impairment.

attributes.helpText: Enter the width in pixels for this bar chart.

lovValues.helpText: Add alternating row stripes on each row.
Add horizontal lines between each row.

attributes.helpText: Check additional report layout options.

Displays the column as a percentage graph. The value retrieved must be between 0 and 100.

5110.name: NATIVE_JSTREE
5110.title: Tree
5110.helpText: Display data in a hierarchical structure, based on parent-child relationships between records.

attributes.helpText:
A CSS class used to specify the type of icons used for all nodes. This class is used in CSS rules to specify properties for all icons of that type. The icon type along with the value of the icon column of the region source determines the icon CSS classes used for each node.

Typical values are:

  • a-Icon This allows using a small number of built-in APEX icons such as icon-circle or icon-tree-folder.
  • fa This allows using Font APEX or Font Awesome icons. The Universal Theme makes one of these icon libraries available.

If no value is given there is no icon type. The icon type CSS class, if needed, can be included in the icon column. For example the icon column value could be "fa fa-user". For a tree with no icons set the Icon Type, and Default Icon attributes to empty and in the SQL Query source the icon column should be null. Custom or third party themes may have their own font or CSS sprite icon library and use a different icon type/prefix class that you can specify here.

attributes.examples: If the Icon Type is fa for Font APEX you can use values such as: fa-user-circle-o, fa-file-o, or fa-arrow-circle-right. See the Universal Theme app for a list of all the icons.
attributes.helpText: The default icon to use when the SQL Query icon column is null. The value is a CSS class name that specifies what icon will be seen. The possible values depend on the Icon Type.

Select the action required to activate node links on your tree. A tree may be used primarily for selection/display or navigation. If used for both selection and navigation it is recommended to set this to Double Click so that a single click will just select the node.

Select the page or application item that you wish to hold the selected node value. You can type in the name or pick from the list of available items.

This item is used to save tree state, by holding the value of the last selected node. The value of the selected node can be saved to the selected item via the node link attribute, or via a page process. When the page is reloaded, the tree is opened to the selected node value.

lovValues.helpText: No tooltip will be displayed.
Use a static tooltip value with the following data source column substitutions: #VALUE#, #TITLE#, #LINK# and #TOOLTIP#
Provide an HTML Expression to use as tooltip. Substitutions are being performed.
Use the value of the Tooltip Column.

attributes.helpText: Select whether tooltips are displayed, and the source for the tooltip. If a tooltip is defined, it is displayed when the end user focuses or hovers over a tree node label.
Enter the text displayed when an end user hovers over a tree element.

An optional unique identifier for the tree.

It is better to give the region a Static ID and use the apex.region("static-id").widget() API to access the tree element.
Select the data source column containing the value for the node label. The value cannot contain markup.

lovValues.helpText: The hierarchy is computed using the SQL START WITH CONNECT BY clause. Providing a Parent Key Column is required. Use this option only if your SQL query does not already contain a START WITH CONNECT BY clause.

All hierarchy information is already contained in the data. Mapping the Node Level and Node Status columns is required for this option. The Node Level must contain the hierarchy level as a numeric value; the Node Status must contain 0 for a leaf node and 1 for a non-leaf node.

attributes.helpText: Indicate whether Oracle APEX should compute the tree hierarchy from the data or whether the data already contains all hierarchy information.
Select the data source column containing the value for the hierarchy level of the node. Required when the Hierarchy attribute is set to Not Computed.
Select the data source column containing the value for the icon CSS class to be applied to the node.
Select the data source column containing the ID for a node. This is required when the hierarchy is being computed by Oracle APEX. Typically, a primary key column is chosen here.
Select the data source column containing the value for the parent key of a node. Required when Oracle APEX computes the hierarchy.

Select the data source column containing the value for the node status. Required when the Hierarchy attribute is set to Not Computed. The column must contain 0 for leaf nodes and 1 for nodes with children.

lovValues.helpText: Use an item value to start the tree.
Use the value returned by a SQL query to start the tree.
Use a static value to start the tree.
Use SQL NULL to start the tree.

attributes.helpText: This attribute determines how the root of the tree is computed. Nodes, for which the Parent Key column contains the value defined here will be considered as root nodes. Multiple roots are possible.
Choose the item containing the value to start the tree with.
Specify the SQL Query to determine the value to start the tree with. The SQL Query is always being executed in the local database and must return exactly one column.
Static value to start the tree with.
Specify the link to be executed when a node is clicked.
Select the data source column containing the value for the node tooltip.
Select the data source column containing the value for the link to be executed when a node is clicked.
Select the data source column to use for ordering children within a parent node.
Select the data source column containing the value for the node "value". This value is not displayed but added to the tree adapter node id property that can be accessed using JavaScript.

INIT_JAVASCRIPT_CODE.examples:
function( options ) {
    options.multiple = true;
    return options;
}
INIT_JAVASCRIPT_CODE.helpText:
Enter a JavaScript function that takes an options object for the Tree, modifies the object, and returns it. This allows advanced customization of the Tree during initialization of the treeView widget. See the treeView widget JavaScript API documentation for the available options.

Additional options defined by the tree region:

  • makeNodeAdapter Used to define a custom nodeAdapter. It is a function that takes the same arguments as makeDefaultNodeAdapter and must return a treeNodeAdapter interface.
  • initialSelectedNodeId The value of a node to select. This is set according to the Selected Node Page Item attribute.
  • nodeHasTooltip This is set according to the Tooltip attribute. It is true if the node has a tooltip and false otherwise.
  • regionStaticId This is the element id used for this region.

SOURCE_LOCATION.examples:
The following SQL queries return columns specific to Tree region attributes:

When the Hierarchy attribute is set to Computed with SQL
 select ename, empno, mgr from emp

Specify EMPNO for Node ID Column, MGR as Parent Key Column attributes

When the Hierarchy attribute is set to Not Computed
 select case when connect_by_isleaf = 1 then 0 when level = 1 then 1 else -1 end as status,
        level,
        ename as title,
        'icon-tree-folder' as icon,
        empno as value,
        ename as tooltip,
        null  as link
   from emp
  start with mgr is null
connect by prior empno = mgr
  order siblings by ename

Specify STATUS for Node Status Column, LEVEL for Hierarchy Level Column attributes.

attributes.helpText: Whether to use a custom template for search results, instead of the display templates specified within the Search Configuration.

attributes.examples:
Example: Template to render the default search result layout.

<div class="a-ResultsItem &RESULT_CSS_CLASSES!ATTR.">
  {if ?ICON_VALUE/}
    {case ICON_TYPE/}
      {when INITIALS/}
        <div class="a-ResultItem-initials u-color-var">&ICON_VALUE.</div>
      {when URL/}
        <div class="a-ResultItem-image"><img src="&ICON_VALUE!ATTR." alt="&TITLE!ATTR." role="presentation" /></div>
      {when CLASS/}
        <div class="a-ResultItem-icon u-color-var"><span class="fa &ICON_VALUE!ATTR." aria-hidden="true"></span></div>
    {endcase/}
  {endif/}
  <div class="a-ResultsItem-content">
    <div class="a-ResultsItem-header">
      {if ?LINK/}
        <span class="a-ResultsItem-title"><a href="&LINK!ATTR.">&TITLE.</a></span>
      {else/}
        <span class="a-ResultsItem-title">&TITLE.</span>
      {endif/}
      {if ?BADGE/}<span class="a-ResultsItem-badge">&BADGE.</span>{endif/}
    </div>
    {if ?SUBTITLE/}<div class="a-ResultsItem-subTitle">&SUBTITLE.</div>{endif/}
    {if ?DESCRIPTION/}<div class="a-ResultsItem-description">&DESCRIPTION.</div>{endif/}
    {if ?HAS_CUSTOM_ATTRS/}
      <div class="a-ResultsItem-attributes">
        {if ?CUSTOM_01/}<span class="a-ResultsItem-attribute">&CUSTOM_01.</span>{endif/}
        {if ?CUSTOM_02/}<span class="a-ResultsItem-attribute">&CUSTOM_02.</span>{endif/}
        {if ?CUSTOM_03/}<span class="a-ResultsItem-attribute">&CUSTOM_03.</span>{endif/}
      </div>
    {endif/}
    {if ?LAST_MODIFIED/}<div class="a-ResultsItem-misc">&LAST_MODIFIED.</div>{endif/}
  </div>
</div>
attributes.helpText:
Enter HTML Expression to display a search result row. Use &COLUMN. syntax to show search result column values in HTML. Supports template directives. The following substitutions are available:

TITLE

SUBTITLE

PRIMARY_KEY_1
Primary Key column.
PRIMARY_KEY_2
Second Primary Key column.
DESCRIPTION
Description column.

LAST_MODIFIED

Custom #1 column.

Custom #2 column.
CUSTOM_03
Custom #3 column.
SCORE
Score column. For Oracle TEXT Search Configurations, this will be the score returned by Oracle TEXT; other configurations allow to map a query column.
ICON_TYPE
Represents the icon type: Can be CLASS, URL or INITIALS.
ICON_VALUE
The actual icon value, depending on the value of ICON_TYPE
RESULT_CSS_CLASSES
The CSS classes to be applied to each row, based on the Result CSS Classes Search Configuration attribute.
LINK
The link being specified in the search configuration.
CONFIG_ID
Internal ID of the search configuration.
CONFIG_LABEL
Label of the search configuration.
Reference the page item for end users to type their searches in.

When enabled, the search is executed as you type in the search field. Otherwise the search is not executed until the user presses Enter or a button.
Specify the minimum number of characters required in the search term before the search will be executed. This can be useful to reduce the amount of searching done when queries are expensive.

Specify whether to load the region independently of the data for the region.

When lazy loading is enabled, the page renders immediately, showing an empty region until the data loads. Generally, the page does not display until the entire page loads and is ready to be rendered. For example, if it takes 5 seconds to load all of the data for a region, without lazy loading, the end user would have to wait 5 seconds before the page started to render.

Note - Lazy Loading should only be utilized on data sets that take significant time to load, as this adds unnecessary processing overhead on the database for regions that load quickly.

lovValues.helpText: Embed remote content as an iframe.

Enter additional HTML element attributes for the iframe tag.

5120.name: NATIVE_AUTO_COMPLETE

5120.helpText: Displays a text field that displays a list of possible values, based on the text already entered by the end user, inline with the text item. The list is further refined as the end user types in more text.

attributes.helpText:
Select how the search against the entered value is performed. When using Fetch On Type this setting can have an impact on query performance.

Note: Selecting Contains & Case Sensitive or Contains & Ignore Case prevents the use of column indexes.

Specify whether matching values are retrieved from the database as the user types on the autocomplete item. Fetch On Type retrieves matching records from the database each time the user types a character. Otherwise, all of the list values are loaded on page load.

Oracle recommends using Fetch On Type when you have a large select list, as loading a large number of records may impact the time to initially load the page.

Enter the maximum number of items to display in the select box.

This value can help avoid performance problems by returning too many rows, and also prevent a very large return set when only a few letters have been entered.
Specify the minimum number of characters that must be entered before a search is executed.
Specify whether search results are cached in the browser, when Fetch on Search is enabled.

LOV.examples:
Display and store same value in page item
select ename
  from emp
 order by 1

5120.helpText: Displays multiple values as check boxes, enabling the end user to select multiple values. A list of values is required for items displayed as check boxes. The values corresponding to the checked boxes are stored in a single colon-delimited string.

attributes.helpText: Enter the number of layout columns used to display the check boxes. For example, a value of 2 would display two columns of check boxes. By default, all values display in one column.

List of values based on SQL query

5120.name: NATIVE_COLOR_PICKER
5120.title: Color Picker
5120.helpText: Allows users to choose or enter a color. Colors can be selected from a color spectrum.

lovValues.helpText: Hex color value. No alpha value is allowed. For example #2244ee
Red, Green, Blue in rgb function notation. Example rgb(34,68,238)

Red, Green, Blue, with optional Alpha (transparency) in rgb/rgba function notation.
If the color has no alpha (alpha equals 1), an rgb format is used.
If the color has an alpha, an rgba format is used.
Example rgba(34,68,238,0.5)
Hue, Saturation, Lightness in hsl function notation. Example hsl(230,86,53)

Hue, Saturation, Lightness with optional alpha (transparency) in hsl/hsla function notation. 
If the color has no alpha (alpha equals 1), an hsl format is used.
If the color has an alpha, an hsla format is used.
Example hsla(230,86,53,0.5)
Any valid CSS color format including color names or a CSS variable.

attributes.helpText: Specify the format of the color value returned by this item. Even if the color is entered in a different valid format it will be presented, returned, and sent to the server in this format.

lovValues.helpText: Shows just the color spectrum controls and color presets if any are defined.
Shows additional fields to view or enter colors as Hex, HSL, or RGB values with optional Alpha value depending on Return Value As. Also shows the Initial and Current colors.

attributes.helpText:
Select the amount of information shown in the color picker.

Note this does not apply when Display As is Native Color Picker.

lovValues.helpText: A color can be entered in the text field or chosen from the popup color picker.
A color picker is shown inline.
A button opens a popup color picker.
A native browser color input. The UI is dependent on the browser.

attributes.helpText: Select how the color picker is displayed.
Select whether the color picker should show a set of predefined colors and if so are they from the theme or custom.

List of preset colors to be displayed in the color picker's dialog.
Separate colors using a semicolon.

Allows comparing the color of this item with a the color from another item or a static value and displaying the contrast ratio between them in the color picker UI.  
This can help the user choose colors with enough contrast to be accessible to everyone.
attributes.accessibilityHelpText:
In the color picker UI, you can compare the color of a selected item with that of another item or a static value. This feature displays the contrast ratio between the two colors, aiding users in choosing colors that ensure accessibility for all individuals.

Contrast ratio refers to the difference in luminance or color between two elements in a design, typically the foreground (e.g., text or icons) and the background. A higher contrast ratio enhances readability and visibility, particularly for users with visual impairments or color vision deficiencies. The World Wide Web Consortium (W3C) recommends a minimum contrast ratio of 4.5:1 for normal text and 3:1 for large text (18pt or 14pt bold).

Best practices:
  1. Contrast Ratio: Choose colors with a sufficient contrast ratio to ensure readability and visibility for all users. A higher contrast ratio between text and background colors is especially important for users with low vision or color blindness.
  2. Contrast checker: Utilize contrast checking tools to evaluate the color contrast ratio between foreground and background colors. Aim for a ratio of at least 4.5:1 for text and interactive elements to ensure readability for individuals with varying levels of vision impairment.

attributes.helpText: Item to be used for contrast comparison.
Color to be used for contrast comparison.
Whether to use the defaults defined for this component in Shared Components, Component Settings or custom settings.

5120.name: NATIVE_COMBOBOX
5120.title: Combobox
5120.helpText:
Displays a text item with a list of values icon. When the end user clicks the icon, a popup window appears with a suggestion dropdown of values. It supports filtering and freetext input. If multiple values can be selected they are displayed as chips.

Combobox is best suited for small lists where end users should be able to add own text. For selections without freetext input Select List, Select One and Select Many are better suited. For large result sets have a look at Popup LOV.

attributes.helpText:
The specified item holds manual entered entries that are not found on the LOV data-set. Use this configuration if you are planning to further process the Combobox value, and you need to know if a value exists on the data-set or not.

It is required when the list of values has display and return columns configured. This would preferably be a hidden item, with the attribute Value Protected equal to false, therefore the value can be processed on the server. If Multiple Values equal true, the Manual Entries Item would have its value separated in the same format as the item itself, using the attribute separator. The item value is updated unidirectionally from the Combobox item to Manual Entries Item, and not the other way around.

The use of this property will affect the session state content, where the Combobox item value will only contain the values that are part of the LOV data-set, to access the Manual Entries, developer has to check the session state content for the Manual Entries Item. This also applies to the JavaScript method apex.items.PX_ITEM_NAME.getValue, where it will return only the the values that are part of the LOV data-set too.

Select how the search against the entered value is performed. When using Fetch On Search this setting can have an impact on query performance.

Note: Selecting Contains prevents the use of column indexes.

Specify whether matching values are retrieved from the database as the user types on the combobox item. Fetch on Search retrieves matching records from the database each time the user types a character. Otherwise, all of the list values are loaded on page load.

Oracle recommends using Fetch on Search when you have a large select list, as loading a large number of records may impact the time to initially load the page.

If attribute Fetch on Search is set to false, consolidation logic will be applied to avoid duplicated values, this is affected by the attribute Case Sensitive too. If Fetch on Search is set to true, no consolidation logic will be applied and LOV source cannot have a display column configured.

Example of data consolidation when LOV has only one column and attribute Case Sensitive is set to false: If the user types "blue", and on the Combobox data-set the option "Blue" exists, the value will be set to "Blue" and not "blue". If the value doesn't exists on the data-set the value would be set to what the user typed.

Example of data consolidation when LOV has return and display column configured and attribute Case Sensitive is set to false: If the user types "blue", the value would be set to the return value of the option. Following the blue example: If the option on the LOV is Display: Blue, Return: 15 and the user types "blue", the value would be 15 and the display value would be set to "Blue". If the value doesn't exists on the data-set, then the Manual Entries Item value would be set to "blue".

Enter the maximum number of options to display in the select box. If not specified, up to 250 options are shown.

This value can help improve performance, by avoiding returning too many rows, and also prevent a very large return set when only a few letters have been entered.
Specify the minimum number of characters that must be entered before a search is executed.
Specify whether search results are cached in the browser, when Fetch on Search is enabled.

Controls if the suggestion dropdown should remain opened after selection. If enabled it will add a checkbox next to each option to indicate the selected status. This option is only applicable for multi-value items.

Alternative Text serves as a crucial element to enhance accessibility for users with visual impairments. It provides a textual description of images within the pages, offering insights into their significance in relation to the content.

Best practices:

select *

declare
    l_file_names apex_t_varchar2;
    l_file       apex_application_temp_files%rowtype;
begin
    l_file_names := apex_string.split (
                        p_str => :page item name,

    for i in 1 .. l_file_names.count loop
        select *
          into l_file
          from apex_application_temp_files
         where name = l_file_names(i);

end;

5120.name: NATIVE_GEOCODED_ADDRESS
5120.title: Geocoded Address
5120.helpText:
This item type provides Geocoding (turning a postal address to a coordinate) functionality.

Geocoding is performed by the browser doing a REST request to the Oracle Elocation Geocoding Service (elocation.oracle.com). Thus the browser must be connected to the internet in order for geocoding to work.

Geocoding input data comes from other page items, which are mapped to address parts like Street, House Number, Postal Code or City. The Geocoder will show a popup window with a list of possible matches. After choosing a match, the item's session state value will be the address coordinate in GeoJSON format. If Sanitize Address is enabled, address part page items will be overwritten with the sanitized values received from the Geocoding service.

For simpler use cases, the Unstructured Address mode allows to map only one text field or text area where end users enter address parts, separated by comma. In this case, the Sanitize Address mode is not available.

attributes.helpText:
Whether address parts are provided to the geocoding service in a structured or unstructured manner.

Structured means that explicit page items are mapped to address parts like Street, Postal Code, City or Region. This leads to more accurate geocoding results, and also allows to feed the corrected addresses back to the page items.

Unstructured means that only one item is used for the whole address; parts are separated by comma. This mode does not allow to feed corrected addresses back to the page item.

lovValues.helpText: Use a static country from a select list.
Get the country from an application or page item. The item must contain the 2-digit ISO code for a country.

Pick the item containing the Sub Area (within a City) part of the address.
Pick the item containing the City part of the address.
Pick the item containing the Postal Code part of the address.
Pick the item containing the Region (State) part of the address.
Enable this switch to feed address data from the geocoding service back to the mapped items.

Pick a page item for the Geocoder to return the Match Vector into. The match vector is a 17-digit string with detailed information about how each address attribute has been matched against the data used for geocoding.

Match Vector digits can have the following values:

  • 0: The input attribute is not null and is matched with a non-null value.

  • 1: The input attribute is null and is matched with a null value.

  • 2: The input attribute is not null and is replaced by a different non-null value.

  • 3: The input attribute is not null and is replaced by a null value.

  • 4: The input attribute is null and is replaced by a non-null value.


Match Vector digits and the address attribute corresponding to each:

  • 3: Address Point (exact address matched in data used for geocoding)

  • 4: Point Of Interest Name

  • 5: House Number

  • 6: Street Prefix

  • 7: Street Name

  • 8: Street Suffix

  • 9: Street Type

  • 10: Secondary Unit

  • 11: City

  • 14: Region

  • 15: Country

  • 16: Postal Code

  • 17: Postal Add-On Code

  • other digits are unused yet.

lovValues.helpText:
Geocoding is triggered automatically before the page is submitted.

If a dependent item value has changed, like for example the value of P1_STREET and geocoding was not executed so far, or a valid address hasn't been selected, we make sure that geocoding is triggered automatically. In this case we interrupt the submission flow of the current page submit and show a popup window with possible matches first. If the user picked a matching result, the page can be re-submitted without any further interruption.
Geocoding must be triggered by adding the Dynamic Action Trigger Geocoding to the page.

Geocoding is triggered based on an event on the DOM element targeted by the selector. If an input field is referenced, Geocoding is triggered on change of the element, if a button is referenced, Geocoding will be triggered on click.

attributes.helpText: Determine when to trigger geocoding. This includes the browser performing the REST request to the geocoding service and showing the popup window with possible matches.

    l_file_names apex_t_varchar2;
    l_file       apex_application_temp_files%rowtype;
begin
    l_file_names := apex_string.split (
                        p_str => :page item name,
                        p_sep => ':' );
    for i in 1 .. l_file_names.count loop

          into l_file
          from apex_application_temp_files
         where name = l_file_names(i);
        -- add code here to store the uploaded file in your own table
    end loop;
end;

RGB codes are defined as RGB(xxx,xxx,xxx), where xxx is a number between 0 and 255 each representing the single 8-bit byte value for red, green, and blue respectively.

attributes.accessibilityHelpText:
When it comes to accessibility, text colors should adhere to certain guidelines to ensure readability and inclusivity for all users, including those with visual impairments. Here are some best practices for choosing text colors:

Best Practises:
  1. High Contrast: Text should have sufficient contrast against the background to ensure readability. The Web Content Accessibility Guidelines (WCAG) recommend a minimum contrast ratio of 4.5:1 for normal text and 3:1 for large text (defined as text that is at least 18pt or 14pt bold).
  2. Avoid Pure Black and Pure White: While black text on a white background may seem like the default choice, pure black (#000000) and pure white (#FFFFFF) can create harsh contrasts that may strain the eyes. Slightly off-black and off-white shades are often easier on the eyes.
  3. Use of Red and Green: Red and green are particularly problematic for individuals with certain types of color blindness. If these colors are used to convey information, ensure that there are alternative ways to differentiate them (e.g., using patterns or labels).
  4. Consistency: Maintain consistency in text colors throughout your website or application to provide a cohesive experience for users. Inconsistencies in color usage can be confusing and detract from accessibility.
  5. Testing: Use accessibility testing tools to evaluate the contrast ratio of text colors against their background. These tools can help identify areas where contrast needs to be adjusted to meet accessibility standards.

RGB codes are defined as RGB(xxx,xxx,xxx), where xxx is a number between 0 and 255 each representing the single 8-bit byte value for red, green, and blue respectively.

attributes.accessibilityHelpText:

Displays an item with a built-in list of values selector. Each option represents a range of values, from a lower to an upper boundary. The facet supports single or multiple selection, and manual entry.

For single selection support, displays multiple values as radio group options, enabling the end user to select a single value. For multiple selection support, displays multiple values as check boxes, enabling the end user to select multiple values. For manual entry support, text fields will render below the facet, allowing the end user to manually enter the range of values they wish to use for filtering the Filtered region.

For filtering and count computation, the lower boundary of a specified range is always treated inclusive, and the upper boundary is exclusive. Example LOV Syntax:

Less than 100
|100
Between 100 and 500 (exclusive)
100|500
500 and more
500|

For DATE or TIMESTAMP values, use the YYYYMMDDHH24MISS canonical format. The Format Mask is only used for representation on the client.

5120.name: NATIVE_RICH_TEXT_EDITOR
5120.title: Rich Text Editor
5120.helpText: Displays a rich text editor with comprehensive text formatting options. End users can enhance the content displayed in a similar fashion to using a word processor, such as Microsoft Word.

attributes.helpText: Set the minimum height in pixels of the editable area.
Set the maximum height in pixels of the editable area. Leaving this attribute empty will let the editor grow infinitely as you type.
Select the number of text formatting options available within the editor.
Choose whether the toolbar items should only take up one line and overflow into a popup menu if wider than the editor's width, or whether to split them into multiple lines.

For advanced usage only.

As a preferred alternative, embedding snippets of custom HTML can also be done via the "HTML Embed" functionality available in the "Full" Toolbar.

Unless necessary, this setting should be left disabled, as it is only meant to provide backwards compatibility with HTML generated by CKEditor4 or HTML hand-crafted by end users.

This setting controls whether the "General HTML Support" ("GHS") and "Source Editing" library plugins will be enabled or not. "Source Editing" offers the ability to manually change the underlying HTML, while General HTML Support allows for HTML features that are not explicitly supported by any other dedicated library plugin. For example, HTML elements like iframe or video, or custom HTML atrributes like id, if added via the "Source Editing" functionality, would normally be stripped away unless this attribute is enabled.

Under the hood, the General HTML Support plugins would be configured as follows: 

htmlSupport: {
    allow: [ {
        name: /.*/,
        attributes: true,
        classes: true,
        styles: true
    } ]
}

For more granular control, it is recommended to leave this setting off, and instead configure it via the Initialization JavaScript Function. For example: 

function( options ) {

    options.editorOptions.extraPlugins.push (
        CKEditor5.sourceEditing.SourceEditing,
        CKEditor5.htmlSupport.GeneralHtmlSupport,
        CKEditor5.htmlSupport.HtmlComment
    );

    options.editorOptions.toolbar.items.push( "sourceEditing" );

    options.editorOptions.htmlSupport = {
        allow: [ {
            name: /.*/,
            attributes: true,
            classes: true,
            styles: true
        } ]
    };

    return options;
}

The actions menu includes options such as Single Row View, Add Row, Delete Row, and Refresh Row, and so forth, depending on the grid attributes and end user authorizations. These menu options allow end users to perform specific actions on the current row in the grid.

The actions menu can be used in both editable and non-editable Interactive Grids, but the menu options will differ depending on this. For non-editable Interactive Grids, the menu will have a subset of options, for example Single Row View and Refresh Row, and not include editable specific actions like Add Row, Delete Row and so on.

When an Interactive Grid is made editable, the APEX$ROW_ACTION column will be automatically added, and set to a type of Actions Menu. For non-editable Interactive Grids, this column must be added manually.

Specify whether search results are cached in the browser, when Fetch on Search is enabled.

5120.name: NATIVE_SELECT_ONE

attributes.helpText: Enter a text message to display when no rows are found.
Controls if the search is case-sensitive.

Select how the search against the entered value is performed. When using Fetch On Search this setting can have an impact on query performance.

Note: Selecting Contains prevents the use of column indexes.

Enter the maximum number of options to display in the select box. If not specified, up to 250 options are shown.

The left list displays the source list of values that have not been selected and the right list shows the currently selected values. End users can select one or more values in a list then use the shuttle controls to move the selected values or all values.

5120.name: NATIVE_SINGLE_CHECKBOX
5120.title: Checkbox
5120.helpText: Displays a single checkbox that the user can check or uncheck. The defined checked or unchecked value is stored in session state when submitted.

attributes.helpText: Whether to use the defaults defined for this component in Shared Components, Component Settings or custom settings.

Enter the value stored in the page item if the user checks the checkbox. The value can be up to 255 characters long.

On a Faceted Search page, if the facet filters a query column based on a List Of Values, this value must match both LOV display and return value. If display and return values differ, then you cannot use this facet type for this column - use the Checkbox Group facet instead.

Enter the value stored in the page item if the user unchecks the checkbox. This attribute can also be left blank if you want to store NULL when unchecked. The value can be up to 255 characters long.

5120.name: NATIVE_STAR_RATING
5120.title: Star Rating
5120.helpText:
Modern Star Rating Item

This item displays a numeric value as a number of stars or other icons. The end user can change the value by selecting the desired number of stars. The value can be adjusted by clicking the number of stars with the mouse or by using the keyboard.

The icon to be displayed, the background and foreground colors can be adjusted either in the component settings or in the individual item settings. To use individual items and colors, set the attribute Use Component Defaults to No.

As icons, you may use any icon from the Icon Font available in your application. For Universal Theme applications, use an icon from the Font APEX library.

attributes.helpText: Choose the default color for active stars.
attributes.accessibilityHelpText:
Enhancing star rating accessibility through mindful color selection and compliance with WCAG standards is crucial for ensuring inclusivity.

Best Practices:
  • Utilize contrast checking tools to evaluate the color contrast ratio between foreground and background colors. Aim for a ratio of at least 3:1 against adjacent colors to ensure readability for individuals with varying levels of vision impairment.

attributes.helpText: Choose the default color for inactive stars.

Legacy item Used to stop the previous HTML table and start a new HTML table. Before Grid Layout was introduced in Oracle APEX Release xx, this item type was used extensively to tailor the display of page items.

Oracle recommends deleting these legacy item types and updating the Start New Grid to Yes for the next page item displayed in that region. This is functionally equivalent to using a Stop and Start Grid Layout item.

5120.name: NATIVE_TEXTAREA

5120.helpText: Displays a multiple-row text area.

attributes.helpText: Select how the item value is trimmed after submitting the page. This setting trims spaces, tabs, and new lines from the text entered.
Specify whether the text area resizing using the mouse is enabled.
Specify whether the height of the text area varies based on the amount of text displayed. Use this option to scale the text area to the amount of data.

5120.name: NATIVE_TEXT_FIELD
5120.title: Text Field
5120.helpText: Displays a text field.

attributes.helpText: Specify whether pressing the Enter key while in this field automatically submits the page.

Specify whether this item is disabled, which prevents end users from changing the value.

A disabled text item still displays with the same HTML formatting, unlike an item type of Display Only, which removes the HTML formatting. Disabled text items are part of page source, which enables their session state to be evaluated. Conversely, display only items are not stored in session state.
Specify whether the current item value should be sent when the page is submitted.

Select the HTML5 text subtype. This enables devices with on-screen keyboards to show an optimized keyboard layout specific to the subtype, for easier data input. The subtype selection is also used to render an appropriate link with the value of the page item, if it is rendered read only. This attribute does not change the text item, or data entry, when using a physical keyboard.

Note: This HTML5 feature only works in modern browsers. Older, non HTML5-compliant, browsers ignore this attribute and render the page item as a normal text field.
Select how the item value is trimmed after submitting the page. This setting trims spaces, tabs, and new lines from the text entered.
Select how the item value text case is transformed.

5120.name: NATIVE_YES_NO
5120.title: Switch
5120.helpText: Displays as a flip toggle switch.

attributes.helpText: Whether to use the defaults defined for this component in Shared Components, Component Settings or custom settings.
Enter the value stored in the item if the user picks the On option. The value can be up to 255 characters long.

Enter the text displayed for the On option. If no text is entered, the system default label is used.

Note: If the Component Setting 'Display Style' is Switch, this attribute is only used as the display value for Interactive Grid columns. It will not be displayed for page items.

Enter the value stored in the item if the user picks the Off option. This attribute can also be left blank if you want to store NULL when the Off option is selected. The value can be up to 255 characters long.

Note: This value is used if the item is populated with a value which does not match either the On Value or Off Value.

Enter the text displayed for the Off option. If no text is entered, the system default label is used.

Note: If the Component Setting 'Display Style' is Switch, this attribute is only used as the display value for Interactive Grid columns. It will not be displayed for page items.

Add the CSS classes articlenumber and highlight to the HTML tag of the affected elements: 
articlenumber highlight

5150.name: NATIVE_ALERT

attributes.helpText: Optionally provide a dialog title.
Specify the style of the dialog.

Specify an optional dialog icon.

attributes.helpText: Optionally provide a dialog title.
Specify the style of the dialog.
Enter optional CSS classes to be applied to the dialog container.
Specify an optional dialog icon.
Enter the label of the Cancel button. If none is provided, the value of text message APEX.DIALOG.CANCEL will be used.

5150.name: NATIVE_DISABLE

You can reference page or application items using bind syntax, providing you include them in Items to Submit.

The column order of the provided SQL Query should be as follows:

  1. File Content - BLOB, CLOB or VARCHAR2 column

Enter the uppercase page items submitted to the server, and therefore, available for use within your SQL Query.

You can type in the item name or pick from the list of available items. If you pick from the list and there is already text entered then a comma is placed at the end of the existing text, followed by the item name returned from the list.

5150.name: NATIVE_ENABLE

5150.name: NATIVE_EXECUTE_PLSQL_CODE
5150.title: Execute Server-side Code
5150.helpText: Executes code on the server.

attributes.helpText: Specify whether the change event is suppressed on the items specified in Page Items to Return. This prevents subsequent Change based Dynamic Actions from firing, for these items.

attributes.examples:
Increases the salary by 3% for those employees which are qualified for a salary raise:
begin
    for l_emp ( select empno
                  from emp
                 where deptno = :P2_DEPTNO )
    loop
        if needs_salary_raise( l_empno.empno ) then
            update emp
               set sal = sal * 1.03
             where empno = l_emp.empno;
        end if;
    end loop;
end;

In this example, you need to enter P2_DEPTNO in Items to Submit.
attributes.helpText:
Specify an execution only PL/SQL anonymous block, that is executed on the server.

You can reference other page or application items from within your application using bind syntax (for example :P1_MY_ITEM). Any items referenced also need to be included in Page Items to Submit.

Enter the uppercase page items submitted to the server, and therefore, available for use within your PL/SQL Code.

You can type in the item name or pick from the list of available items. If you pick from the list and there is already text entered then a comma is placed at the end of the existing text, followed by the item name returned from the list.

attributes.examples:
Increases the salary by 3% for those employees which are qualified for a salary raise:
var rows;
function needsSalaryRaise( empno ) {
  // placeholder for some complicated logic to calculate if employee needs a raise
  return true;
}
rows = apex.conn.execute( "select empno from emp where deptno = :deptno", { deptno: apex.env.P2_DEPTNO } ).rows;
for ( var row of rows ) {
  if ( needsSalaryRaise( row.EMPNO )) {
    apex.conn.execute( "update emp set sal = sal * 1.03 where empno = :empno", { empno: row.EMPNO } );
  }
}

In this example, you need to enter P2_DEPTNO in Items to Submit.
attributes.helpText:
Specify an execution only JavaScript block, that is executed on the server.

You can reference other page or application items from within your application using bind syntax (for example apex.env.P1_MY_ITEM). Any items referenced also need to be included in Page Items to Submit.

attributes.examples:
apex_util.set_session_state('P1_MY_ITEM', 'New Value');

In this example, enter P1_MY_ITEM in this attribute in order for 'New Value' to be displayed in that item on your page.
attributes.helpText:
Enter the uppercase page items set when the call to the server returns, based on their current value in session state. If your PL/SQL Code sets one or more page item values in session state you need to define those items in this attribute.

You can type in the item name or pick from the list of available items. If you pick from the list and there is already text entered then a comma is placed at the end of the existing text, followed by the item name returned from the list.

5150.name: NATIVE_GENERATE_TEXT_AI
5150.title: Generate Text With AI
5150.helpText: Invokes the configured Generative AI Service to generate a one-time response based on user content. This action is ideal for tasks like summarizing or translating text, extracting keywords, or drafting an email.

lovValues.helpText: Do not send any additional data. Only rely on the declared system prompt and RAG sources.
The item whose value is the input to the AI service.
JavaScript expression from which the user input is derived.

attributes.helpText: Select the type of user input to be delivered to the AI service.
Enter the item used to set the user input. You can type in the name or pick from the list of available items.

attributes.examples:
Using a page item value

apex.items.P1_NAME.value + " " + apex.items.P1_DESCRIPTION.value
attributes.helpText:
Enter a JavaScript Expression for the user input.

The code has access to the following dynamic action related attributes:

this.triggeringElement
A reference to the DOM object of the element that triggered the dynamic action.
this.browserEvent
The event object that triggered the event. Note: On load this is equal to 'load'.
this.data
Optional additional data that can be passed from the event handler.

lovValues.helpText: Capture the response directly into an item value.
Process the response based on more complex logic using JavaScript Code.

attributes.helpText: Select how the AI generated response should be returned.
Select an item as the destination for the response value that the AI service returns.

attributes.examples:
Assign the response value to a page item

apex.items.P1_RESPONSE.value = this.data.response;

Call the custom myFunctionToProcessResponse JavaScript function to process the response value in the application.

const response = this.data.response;
myFunctionToProcessResponse( response );
attributes.helpText: Enter the JavaScript Code to manage the processing of the response value returned by the AI service. Use this.data.response to access the message content, which is provided as a string.
Specify whether the change event is suppressed on the items specified in Use Response - Item. This prevents subsequent Change based Dynamic Actions from firing, for the item.

5150.name: NATIVE_GEOCODING_TRIGGER
5150.title: Trigger Geocoding
5150.helpText: Manually trigger the geocoding search of an Geocoded Address item.

5150.name: NATIVE_GET_CURRENT_POSITION
5150.title: Get Current Position
5150.helpText: Triggers the device to return its current position. The device will ask permission to first time users.

lovValues.helpText: Returns the GeoJSON as a string to a page item.
Returns the latitude and longitude to two different page items.
Get the full Geolocation Position object to use in a JavaScript function.

attributes.helpText: Choose between returning the GeoJSON to a page item, Latitude and Longitude to a page item, or full object to a JavaScript function.
Enter the page item to return the GeoJSON string to.
Enter the page item to return the latitude to.
Enter the page item to return the longitude to.

attributes.examples:
function( position, event ) {

}
attributes.helpText: Enter a JavaScript function that takes a GeolocationPosition object as the first parameter and the event as the second parameter.

Choose if high accuracy geolocation should be enabled. When enabled, the device will provide a more accurate position but this can result in a slower response time or increased power consumption. If disabled, the device can take the liberty to save resources by responding more quickly and/or using less power. Default: disabled.

5150.name: NATIVE_HIDE

This code has access to the following dynamic action related attributes:

this.triggeringElement
A reference to the DOM object of the element that triggered the dynamic action.

A jQuery object containing all the affected elements.
this.action
The action object containing details such as the action name and additional attribute values.
this.browserEvent
The event object of event that triggered the event. Note: On load this equals 'load'.
this.data
Optional additional data that can be passed from the event handler.
attributes.helpText: Enter any custom JavaScript that is specific to the page or dynamic action.

5150.name: NATIVE_OPEN_AI_ASSISTANT
5150.title: Show AI Assistant
5150.helpText: Shows the AI Assistant, an AI-powered chat service, displayed either as a dialog or inline.

lovValues.helpText: Will present the assistant in a modal dialog.
Will integrate the assistant directly into the page layout.

attributes.helpText: Select how the AI Assistant should appear on your page.

Enter a title for the modal dialog.

The default title can be changed application-wide by creating a text message named APEX.AI.DIALOG_TITLE.

The attribute supports template directives.

attributes.examples:
To select a page element with a DOM ID of my_id
#my_id
To select a page element with a class of my_class
.my_class
attributes.helpText:
Enter jQuery Selector syntax to return a page element present on your current page. This Container Selector will be used to locate the element where the AI Assistant widget will be embedded.

If the selector returns multiple DOM elements only the first one is used.

Select the type of initial prompt to be delivered to the AI Assistant. The initial prompt represents a message as if it were coming from the user. This can be either a specific item value or a value derived from a JavaScript expression. Select the appropriate option based on the source of the initial input to the assistant.
Enter a page item used to set the initial prompt. You can type in the name or pick from the list of available items.

Enter the text to be displayed as the initial prompt message. Note that this displayed text can be different from the complete content provided by the item. This allows for a more user-friendly or context-specific message to be showcased while still leveraging the full item value for processing.

The attribute supports template directives.

attributes.examples:
Using a page item value

apex.items.P1_NAME.value + " " + apex.items.P1_DESCRIPTION.value

Using the values from page items to construct an object that contains both the full and displayed content

{
    fullContent: "Product Name: " + apex.items.P1_NAME.value + "\n Product Description: " + apex.items.P1_DESCRIPTION.value, // Message sent to AI service
    content: "Product Information", // Optional message displayed if different from fullContent
    type: "text", // Optional type to render content as: text (default), markdown or html
    commit: false // Optional flag to immediately send the message to the AI service. Defaults to 'false'
}
attributes.helpText:
Enter a JavaScript Expression that will evaluate to the initial prompt. The expression can return either a string or a JavaScript object.

The code has access to the following dynamic action related attributes:

this.triggeringElement
A reference to the DOM object of the element that triggered the dynamic action.
this.browserEvent
The event object that triggered the event. Note: On load this is equal to 'load'.
this.data
Optional additional data that can be passed from the event handler.

Select how the AI Assistant should return responses. The term 'response' refers to the message content of an individual chat message. You have the option to capture this response directly into a page item value or to process it based on more complex logic using JavaScript Code.
Select a page item as the destination for the response value that the AI Assistant returns.

attributes.examples:
Assign the response value to a page item

apex.items.P1_RESPONSE.value = this.data.response;

const response = this.data.response;
myFunctionToProcessResponse( response );

Specify the label for the message action button, which is used to send the response to a designated target. The default label is 'Use this'. Customize this label to better suit the action's purpose or context.

Only show the 'Use this' quick action button on messages which contain the phrase 'recipe' and return the whole message in such cases.

this.fullContent.toLowerCase().includes( "recipe" ) ? this.fullContent : ""
attributes.helpText:
Enter a JavaScript Expression to search for certain criteria within the message, like finding a specific piece of text. This expression should return the text to be used in the response. Additionally, the result of this expression determines if a quick action button is displayed on the message. If the expression returns a value, the button will be made visible.

Use 'this' to access the message content object.

Enter a message to serve as a chat-wide quick action. A quick action is a pre-defined phrase that, once clicked, will be sent as a user message.

The attribute supports template directives.

Enter a message to serve as a chat-wide quick action. A quick action is a pre-defined phrase that, once clicked, will be sent as a user message.

The attribute supports template directives.

attributes.examples:
Summarize the provided text.

Translate this text into German.
attributes.helpText:
Enter a prompt that is used in conjunction with the 'Initial Prompt' to display an immediate AI-generated response for the end user.

The attribute supports template directives.

INIT_JAVASCRIPT_CODE.examples:
function( options ) {
    options.displayAs = "DIALOG";
    options.initialPrompt.message = "My initial display message";
    options.response.buttonLabel = "Use this text";

    options.useChatContext = ( chat, chatView ) => {
        console.log( "useChatContext", chat, chatView );
    };

    options.view.title = "My dialog title";
    options.view.quickActions.push( {
        title: "My new Quick Action",
        message: "Description of new Quick Action"
    } );

    return options;
}
INIT_JAVASCRIPT_CODE.helpText: Enter a JavaScript function that takes a configuration object for the AI Assistant, modifies the object, and returns it. This allows advanced customization of the assistant appearance, features, and behavior.
