8050.helpText:
Displays a text field with a calendar icon. End users can either enter the date directly into the text item, or click on the calendar icon to select a date, and optionally a time, from the calendar popup.

Time is only displayed in the calendar popup if the Format Mask for this item includes time components.

attributes.helpText:
Enter the minimum date that can be input or selected.

The date value can be an absolute value in 'YYYY-MM-DDTHH24:MI:SS' or 'YYYYMMDDHH24MI' format or a relative value with respect to today's date, such as +7d, or a dynamic value using substitution syntax, providing the substitution returns the correct date format or relative value.

Relative date values include:

y
+ / - years from today's date
m
+ / - months from today's date
w
+ / - weeks from today's date
d
+ / - days from today's date

Enter the maximum date that can be input or selected.

The date value can be an absolute value in 'YYYY-MM-DDTHH24:MI:SS' or 'YYYYMMDDHH24MI' format or a relative value with respect to today's date, such as +7d, or a dynamic value using substitution syntax, providing the substitution returns the correct date format or relative value.

Relative date values include:

y

m
+ / - months from today's date
w

d

The value can be an absolute value in 'YYYYMMDDHH24MI' format or a relative value with respect to today's date, such as +7d, or a dynamic value using substitution syntax, providing the substitution returns the correct date format or relative value.

Relative date values include:

y

d

attributes.helpText: Select when the date picker pop-up calendar displays.

Specify whether the leading dates from the previous month and the trailing dates for the next month are displayed. The leading and trailing dates fully populate the first and last lines of the calendar. For example, if the first day of the week is Sunday, and the first of the current month displayed falls on a Wednesday, then the Sunday, Monday, and Tuesday show the last three days of the previous month.

attributes.examples:
<dl>
  <dt>2000:2010</dt>
    <dd>Uses absolute years to restrict permitted years to be between 2000 and 2010, inclusive.</dd>
  <dt>-05:+05</dt>
    <dd>Uses relative dates to limit permitted years to +/- five years from the current year.</dd>
  <dt>+01:+03</dt>
    <dd>Uses relative dates to limit permitted years to next year for a further two years.</dd>
</dl>

Enter how many months to show in the calendar pop-up.

You can enter an integer value or a two-dimensional array using [row,column], to define the number of rows and columns to display

Note: Months after the Highlighted Date are displayed.
Select whether select lists are provided within the calendar pop-up for Month and/or Year.

8050.name: NATIVE_DISPLAY_IMAGE
8050.title: Display Image
8050.helpText: Displays an image stored in a database BLOB columns, or based on an image URL.

lovValues.d: Image URL stored in Page Item Value
lovValues.helpText: The image URL is read from the value stored in session state for the page item specified.

lovValues.d: BLOB Column specified in Item Source
lovValues.helpText: Reads the image from the BLOB column specified in the Item Source attribute.

lovValues.d: BLOB Column returned by SQL statement
lovValues.helpText: Displays the image based on the BLOB column which is returned by the SQL statement specified.

attributes.helpText: Select where to retrieve the image from.
Enter the uppercase page or application item name that holds the filename column value associated with the BLOB column.

Enter the uppercase page or application item name that holds the date column value when the associated BLOB was last updated.

This value is used for browser caching and to identify if the image has been changed since the last request from the browser. If the image is not updated then the image is retrieved from the browser cache, if available.
Enter text which is read by screen readers when an end user navigates to this image.
attributes.accessibilityHelpText:
Alternative Text serves as a crucial element to enhance accessibility for users with visual impairments. It provides a textual description of images within the pages, offering insights into their significance in relation to the content.

Best practices:

  1. Purposeful Description:
    • Alt Text should succinctly convey the significance of the image in relation to the surrounding content.
    • Focus on describing the "why" of the image rather than stating what the image is.
    • Keep Alt Text clear, concise, and descriptive.
  2. Avoidance of Redundant Phrases:
    • Instruction to avoid redundant phrases such as "image of" in Alt Text.

8050.name: NATIVE_GEOCODED_ADDRESS
8050.title: Geocoded Address
8050.helpText:
This item type provides Geocoding (turning a postal address to a coordinate) functionality.

Geocoding is performed by the browser doing a REST request to the Oracle Elocation Geocoding Service (elocation.oracle.com). Thus the browser must be connected to the internet in order for geocoding to work.

Geocoding input data comes from other page items, which are mapped to address parts like Street, House Number, Postal Code or City. The Geocoder will show a popup window with a list of possible matches. After choosing a match, the item's session state value will be the address coordinate in GeoJSON format. If Sanitize Address is enabled, address part page items will be overwritten with the sanitized values received from the Geocoding service.

For simpler use cases, the Unstructured Address mode allows to map only one text field or text area where end users enter address parts, separated by comma. In this case, the Sanitize Address mode is not available.

attributes.helpText:
Whether address parts are provided to the geocoding service in a structured or unstructured manner.

Structured means that explicit page items are mapped to address parts like Street, Postal Code, City or Region. This leads to more accurate geocoding results, and also allows to feed the corrected addresses back to the page items.

Unstructured means that only one item is used for the whole address; parts are separated by comma. This mode does not allow to feed corrected addresses back to the page item.

lovValues.helpText: Use a static country from a select list.
Get the country from an application or page item. The item must contain the 2-digit ISO code for a country.

Pick the item containing the Sub Area (within a City) part of the address.
Pick the item containing the City part of the address.
Pick the item containing the Postal Code part of the address.
Pick the item containing the Region (State) part of the address.
Enable this switch to feed address data from the geocoding service back to the mapped items.

Pick a page item for the Geocoder to return the Match Vector into. The match vector is a 17-digit string with detailed information about how each address attribute has been matched against the data used for geocoding.

Match Vector digits can have the following values:

  • 0: The input attribute is not null and is matched with a non-null value.

  • 1: The input attribute is null and is matched with a null value.

  • 2: The input attribute is not null and is replaced by a different non-null value.

  • 3: The input attribute is not null and is replaced by a null value.

  • 4: The input attribute is null and is replaced by a non-null value.


Match Vector digits and the address attribute corresponding to each:

  • 3: Address Point (exact address matched in data used for geocoding)

  • 4: Point Of Interest Name

  • 5: House Number

  • 6: Street Prefix

  • 7: Street Name

  • 8: Street Suffix

  • 9: Street Type

  • 10: Secondary Unit

  • 11: City

  • 14: Region

  • 15: Country

  • 16: Postal Code

  • 17: Postal Add-On Code

  • other digits are unused yet.

lovValues.helpText:
Geocoding is triggered automatically before the page is submitted.

If a dependent item value has changed, like for example the value of P1_STREET and geocoding was not executed so far, or a valid address hasn't been selected, we make sure that geocoding is triggered automatically. In this case we interrupt the submission flow of the current page submit and show a popup window with possible matches first. If the user picked a matching result, the page can be re-submitted without any further interruption.
Geocoding must be triggered by adding the Dynamic Action Trigger Geocoding to the page.

Geocoding is triggered based on an event on the DOM element targeted by the selector. If an input field is referenced, Geocoding is triggered on change of the element, if a button is referenced, Geocoding will be triggered on click.

attributes.helpText: Determine when to trigger geocoding. This includes the browser performing the REST request to the geocoding service and showing the popup window with possible matches.

attributes.accessibilityHelpText:
When it comes to accessibility, text colors should adhere to certain guidelines to ensure readability and inclusivity for all users, including those with visual impairments. Here are some best practices for choosing text colors:

Best Practises:
  1. High Contrast: Text should have sufficient contrast against the background to ensure readability. The Web Content Accessibility Guidelines (WCAG) recommend a minimum contrast ratio of 4.5:1 for normal text and 3:1 for large text (defined as text that is at least 18pt or 14pt bold).
  2. Avoid Pure Black and Pure White: While black text on a white background may seem like the default choice, pure black (#000000) and pure white (#FFFFFF) can create harsh contrasts that may strain the eyes. Slightly off-black and off-white shades are often easier on the eyes.
  3. Use of Red and Green: Red and green are particularly problematic for individuals with certain types of color blindness. If these colors are used to convey information, ensure that there are alternative ways to differentiate them (e.g., using patterns or labels).
  4. Consistency: Maintain consistency in text colors throughout your website or application to provide a cohesive experience for users. Inconsistencies in color usage can be confusing and detract from accessibility.
  5. Testing: Use accessibility testing tools to evaluate the contrast ratio of text colors against their background. These tools can help identify areas where contrast needs to be adjusted to meet accessibility standards.

attributes.helpText:
Enter the color used for the background of this graph. The color is specified using hexadecimal (hex) notation, RGB color codes, or HTML color names.

Hex notation is defined as #xxyyzz (a # followed by 3 double digit hex numbers), where xx, yy, and zz represent the two character hex values for red, green and blue respectively. RGB codes are defined as RGB(xxx,xxx,xxx), where xxx is a number between 0 and 255 each representing the single 8-bit byte value for red, green, and blue respectively.

Search the internet for 'HTML Color Codes' to find the equivalent hex code or RGB code for the color you wish to utilize.

8050.title: Popup LOV
8050.helpText:
Displays a text item with a popup list of values icon. When the end user clicks the icon, a popup window appears with a search field, and a list of supported values.

Popup LOV is best suited for large lists since end users can enter search criteria to reduce the available values displayed. For relatively small lists Select List is often better suited.

If No the user can only select values from the popup list of values. This is like a Select List. 8050.name: NATIVE_RANGE
8050.title: Range
8050.helpText:
Displays an item with a built-in list of values selector. Each option represents a range of values, from a lower to an upper boundary. The facet supports single or multiple selection, and manual entry.

For single selection support, displays multiple values as radio group options, enabling the end user to select a single value. For multiple selection support, displays multiple values as check boxes, enabling the end user to select multiple values. For manual entry support, text fields will render below the facet, allowing the end user to manually enter the range of values they wish to use for filtering the Filtered region.

For filtering and count computation, the lower boundary of a specified range is always treated inclusive, and the upper boundary is exclusive. Example LOV Syntax:

Less than 100
|100
Between 100 and 500 (exclusive)
100|500
500 and more
500|

For DATE or TIMESTAMP values, use the YYYYMMDDHH24MISS canonical format. The Format Mask is only used for representation on the client.

attributes.helpText: Specify whether the Range facet supports manual entry. When set to On, text fields will render below the facet, allowing the end user to manually enter the range of values they wish to use for filtering the Filtered region.

8050.name: NATIVE_RICH_TEXT_EDITOR
8050.title: Rich Text Editor
8050.helpText: Displays a rich text editor with comprehensive text formatting options. End users can enhance the content displayed in a similar fashion to using a word processor, such as Microsoft Word.

attributes.helpText: Set the minimum height in pixels of the editable area.
Set the maximum height in pixels of the editable area. Leaving this attribute empty will let the editor grow infinitely as you type.
Select the number of text formatting options available within the editor.
Choose whether the toolbar items should only take up one line and overflow into a popup menu if wider than the editor's width, or whether to split them into multiple lines.

For advanced usage only.

As a preferred alternative, embedding snippets of custom HTML can also be done via the "HTML Embed" functionality available in the "Full" Toolbar.

Unless necessary, this setting should be left disabled, as it is only meant to provide backwards compatibility with HTML generated by CKEditor4 or HTML hand-crafted by end users.

This setting controls whether the "General HTML Support" ("GHS") and "Source Editing" library plugins will be enabled or not. "Source Editing" offers the ability to manually change the underlying HTML, while General HTML Support allows for HTML features that are not explicitly supported by any other dedicated library plugin. For example, HTML elements like iframe or video, or custom HTML atrributes like id, if added via the "Source Editing" functionality, would normally be stripped away unless this attribute is enabled.

Under the hood, the General HTML Support plugins would be configured as follows: 

htmlSupport: {
    allow: [ {
        name: /.*/,
        attributes: true,
        classes: true,
        styles: true
    } ]
}

For more granular control, it is recommended to leave this setting off, and instead configure it via the Initialization JavaScript Function. For example: 

function( options ) {

    options.editorOptions.extraPlugins.push (
        CKEditor5.sourceEditing.SourceEditing,
        CKEditor5.htmlSupport.GeneralHtmlSupport,
        CKEditor5.htmlSupport.HtmlComment
    );

    options.editorOptions.toolbar.items.push( "sourceEditing" );

    options.editorOptions.htmlSupport = {
        allow: [ {
            name: /.*/,
            attributes: true,
            classes: true,
            styles: true
        } ]
    };

    return options;
}

lovValues.helpText: Use HTML for the source and output of this rich text editor. HTML is more flexible and offers more formatting options than Markdown, but is less secure and must be trusted or sanitized when displayed.

Use Markdown format for the source and output of this rich text editor. Markdown is more restrictive than HTML in terms of features, but is more secure as it must first pass through a parser before being displayed.

attributes.helpText: Specify the output format of the content entered in the rich text editor.

    // apply a custom toolbar

    return options;
}

8050.name: NATIVE_ROW_ACTION
8050.title: Actions Menu
8050.helpText:
Displays the actions icon (hamburger) on each row of an Interactive Grid. The actions menu includes options such as Single Row View, Add Row, Delete Row, and Refresh Row, and so forth, depending on the grid attributes and end user authorizations. These menu options allow end users to perform specific actions on the current row in the grid.

The actions menu can be used in both editable and non-editable Interactive Grids, but the menu options will differ depending on this. For non-editable Interactive Grids, the menu will have a subset of options, for example Single Row View and Refresh Row, and not include editable specific actions like Add Row, Delete Row and so on.

When an Interactive Grid is made editable, the APEX$ROW_ACTION column will be automatically added, and set to a type of Actions Menu. For non-editable Interactive Grids, this column must be added manually.

The icon to be displayed, the background and foreground colors can be adjusted either in the component settings or in the individual item settings. To use individual items and colors, set the attribute Use Component Defaults to No.

Allows comparing the color of this item with a the color from another item or a static value and displaying the contrast ratio between them in the color picker UI.

attributes.accessibilityHelpText:
In the color picker UI, you can compare the color of a selected item with that of another item or a static value. This feature displays the contrast ratio between the two colors, aiding users in choosing colors that ensure accessibility for all individuals.

Contrast ratio refers to the difference in luminance or color between two elements in a design, typically the foreground (e.g., text or icons) and the background. A higher contrast ratio enhances readability and visibility, particularly for users with visual impairments or color vision deficiencies. The World Wide Web Consortium (W3C) recommends a minimum contrast ratio of 4.5:1 for normal text and 3:1 for large text (18pt or 14pt bold).

Best practices:
  1. Contrast Ratio: Choose colors with a sufficient contrast ratio to ensure readability and visibility for all users. A higher contrast ratio between text and background colors is especially important for users with low vision or color blindness.
  2. Contrast checker: Utilize contrast checking tools to evaluate the color contrast ratio between foreground and background colors. Aim for a ratio of at least 4.5:1 for text and interactive elements to ensure readability for individuals with varying levels of vision impairment.

8052.name: NATIVE_COMBOBOX
8052.title: Combobox
8052.helpText:
Displays a text item with a list of values icon. When the end user clicks the icon, a popup window appears with a suggestion dropdown of values. It supports filtering and freetext input. If multiple values can be selected they are displayed as chips.

Combobox is best suited for small lists where end users should be able to add own text. For selections without freetext input Select List, Select One and Select Many are better suited. For large result sets have a look at Popup LOV.

attributes.helpText:
The specified item holds manual entered entries that are not found on the LOV data-set. Use this configuration if you are planning to further process the Combobox value, and you need to know if a value exists on the data-set or not.

It is required when the list of values has display and return columns configured. This would preferably be a hidden item, with the attribute Value Protected equal to false, therefore the value can be processed on the server. If Multiple Values equal true, the Manual Entries Item would have its value separated in the same format as the item itself, using the attribute separator. The item value is updated unidirectionally from the Combobox item to Manual Entries Item, and not the other way around.

The use of this property will affect the session state content, where the Combobox item value will only contain the values that are part of the LOV data-set, to access the Manual Entries, developer has to check the session state content for the Manual Entries Item. This also applies to the JavaScript method apex.items.PX_ITEM_NAME.getValue, where it will return only the the values that are part of the LOV data-set too.

Select how the search against the entered value is performed. When using Fetch On Search this setting can have an impact on query performance.

Note: Selecting Contains prevents the use of column indexes.

Specify whether matching values are retrieved from the database as the user types on the combobox item. Fetch on Search retrieves matching records from the database each time the user types a character. Otherwise, all of the list values are loaded on page load.

Oracle recommends using Fetch on Search when you have a large select list, as loading a large number of records may impact the time to initially load the page.

If attribute Fetch on Search is set to false, consolidation logic will be applied to avoid duplicated values, this is affected by the attribute Case Sensitive too. If Fetch on Search is set to true, no consolidation logic will be applied and LOV source cannot have a display column configured.

Example of data consolidation when LOV has only one column and attribute Case Sensitive is set to false: If the user types "blue", and on the Combobox data-set the option "Blue" exists, the value will be set to "Blue" and not "blue". If the value doesn't exists on the data-set the value would be set to what the user typed.

Example of data consolidation when LOV has return and display column configured and attribute Case Sensitive is set to false: If the user types "blue", the value would be set to the return value of the option. Following the blue example: If the option on the LOV is Display: Blue, Return: 15 and the user types "blue", the value would be 15 and the display value would be set to "Blue". If the value doesn't exists on the data-set, then the Manual Entries Item value would be set to "blue".

Enter the maximum number of options to display in the select box. If not specified, up to 250 options are shown.

Stores the uploaded file(s) in a temporary location that you can access with the view APEX_APPLICATION_TEMP_FILES. Oracle APEX will automatically delete the file(s) at the end of the session or at the end of the upload request, depending on what you choose for Purge File At.

To access a file if Allow Multiple Files is set to No:

select *
  from apex_application_temp_files
 where name = :page item name;

To access files if Allow Multiple Files is set to Yes:

declare
    l_file_names apex_t_varchar2;
    l_file       apex_application_temp_files%rowtype;
begin
    l_file_names := apex_string.split (
                        p_str => :page item name,
                        p_sep => ':' );
    for i in 1 .. l_file_names.count loop
        select *
          into l_file
          from apex_application_temp_files
         where name = l_file_names(i);
        -- add code here to store the uploaded file in your own table
    end loop;
end;

8052.name: NATIVE_GEOCODED_ADDRESS
8052.title: Geocoded Address
8052.helpText:
This item type provides Geocoding (turning a postal address to a coordinate) functionality.

Geocoding is performed by the browser doing a REST request to the Oracle Elocation Geocoding Service (elocation.oracle.com). Thus the browser must be connected to the internet in order for geocoding to work.

Geocoding input data comes from other page items, which are mapped to address parts like Street, House Number, Postal Code or City. The Geocoder will show a popup window with a list of possible matches. After choosing a match, the item's session state value will be the address coordinate in GeoJSON format. If Sanitize Address is enabled, address part page items will be overwritten with the sanitized values received from the Geocoding service.

For simpler use cases, the Unstructured Address mode allows to map only one text field or text area where end users enter address parts, separated by comma. In this case, the Sanitize Address mode is not available.

attributes.helpText:
Whether address parts are provided to the geocoding service in a structured or unstructured manner.

Structured means that explicit page items are mapped to address parts like Street, Postal Code, City or Region. This leads to more accurate geocoding results, and also allows to feed the corrected addresses back to the page items.

Unstructured means that only one item is used for the whole address; parts are separated by comma. This mode does not allow to feed corrected addresses back to the page item.

lovValues.helpText: Use a static country from a select list.
Get the country from an application or page item. The item must contain the 2-digit ISO code for a country.

attributes.helpText: Choose whether to use a static country for geocoding, or whether to derive the country from an item.

attributes.examples:
• US: United States
  • UK: United Kingdom
  • DE: Germany
  • AT: Austria
attributes.helpText: Pick a page or application item to get the country for geocoding from. The item must contain the 2-digit ISO code for a country.
Pick the country to use for geocoding.
Pick the item containing unstructured address parts, separated by comma.
Pick the item containing the Street part of the address.
Pick the item containing the House Number part of the address.
Pick the item containing the Sub Area (within a City) part of the address.
Pick the item containing the City part of the address.
Pick the item containing the Postal Code part of the address.
Pick the item containing the Region (State) part of the address.
Enable this switch to feed address data from the geocoding service back to the mapped items.

Pick a page item for the Geocoder to return the Match Vector into. The match vector is a 17-digit string with detailed information about how each address attribute has been matched against the data used for geocoding.

Match Vector digits can have the following values:

  • 0: The input attribute is not null and is matched with a non-null value.

  • 1: The input attribute is null and is matched with a null value.

  • 2: The input attribute is not null and is replaced by a different non-null value.

  • 3: The input attribute is not null and is replaced by a null value.

  • 4: The input attribute is null and is replaced by a non-null value.


Match Vector digits and the address attribute corresponding to each:

  • 3: Address Point (exact address matched in data used for geocoding)

  • 4: Point Of Interest Name

  • 5: House Number

  • 6: Street Prefix

  • 7: Street Name

  • 8: Street Suffix

  • 9: Street Type

  • 10: Secondary Unit

  • 11: City

  • 14: Region

  • 15: Country

  • 16: Postal Code

  • 17: Postal Add-On Code

  • other digits are unused yet.

lovValues.helpText:
Geocoding is triggered automatically before the page is submitted.

If a dependent item value has changed, like for example the value of P1_STREET and geocoding was not executed so far, or a valid address hasn't been selected, we make sure that geocoding is triggered automatically. In this case we interrupt the submission flow of the current page submit and show a popup window with possible matches first. If the user picked a matching result, the page can be re-submitted without any further interruption.
Geocoding must be triggered by adding the Dynamic Action Trigger Geocoding to the page.

Geocoding is triggered based on an event on the DOM element targeted by the selector. If an input field is referenced, Geocoding is triggered on change of the element, if a button is referenced, Geocoding will be triggered on click.

attributes.helpText: Determine when to trigger geocoding. This includes the browser performing the REST request to the geocoding service and showing the popup window with possible matches.

attributes.examples:
Execute process when items P1_STREET and P1_ZIP_CODE changes, jQuery selector:

#P1_STREET,#P1_ZIP_CODE
attributes.helpText: Provide the jQuery selector referencing the element which triggers geocoding. Buttons will trigger geocoding on click, other elements will trigger on change.

lovValues.helpText: Stores the uploaded file in the table used by the Automatic Row Processing (DML) process and the column specified in the item source attribute. The column has to be of data type BLOB. If the file gets downloaded, the table name of the Automatic Row Fetch process is used.

Stores the uploaded file(s) in a temporary location that you can access with the view APEX_APPLICATION_TEMP_FILES. Oracle APEX will automatically delete the file(s) at the end of the session or at the end of the upload request, depending on what you choose for Purge File At.

To access a file if Allow Multiple Files is set to No:

select *
  from apex_application_temp_files
 where name = :page item name;

To access files if Allow Multiple Files is set to Yes:

declare
    l_file_names apex_t_varchar2;
    l_file       apex_application_temp_files%rowtype;
begin
    l_file_names := apex_string.split (
                        p_str => :page item name,
                        p_sep => ':' );
    for i in 1 .. l_file_names.count loop
        select *
          into l_file
          from apex_application_temp_files
         where name = l_file_names(i);
        -- add code here to store the uploaded file in your own table
    end loop;
end;

attributes.accessibilityHelpText:
When it comes to accessibility, text colors should adhere to certain guidelines to ensure readability and inclusivity for all users, including those with visual impairments. Here are some best practices for choosing text colors:

Best Practises:
  1. High Contrast: Text should have sufficient contrast against the background to ensure readability. The Web Content Accessibility Guidelines (WCAG) recommend a minimum contrast ratio of 4.5:1 for normal text and 3:1 for large text (defined as text that is at least 18pt or 14pt bold).
  2. Avoid Pure Black and Pure White: While black text on a white background may seem like the default choice, pure black (#000000) and pure white (#FFFFFF) can create harsh contrasts that may strain the eyes. Slightly off-black and off-white shades are often easier on the eyes.
  3. Use of Red and Green: Red and green are particularly problematic for individuals with certain types of color blindness. If these colors are used to convey information, ensure that there are alternative ways to differentiate them (e.g., using patterns or labels).
  4. Consistency: Maintain consistency in text colors throughout your website or application to provide a cohesive experience for users. Inconsistencies in color usage can be confusing and detract from accessibility.
  5. Testing: Use accessibility testing tools to evaluate the contrast ratio of text colors against their background. These tools can help identify areas where contrast needs to be adjusted to meet accessibility standards.

attributes.helpText:
Enter the color used for the background of this graph. The color is specified using hexadecimal (hex) notation, RGB color codes, or HTML color names.

Hex notation is defined as #xxyyzz (a # followed by 3 double digit hex numbers), where xx, yy, and zz represent the two character hex values for red, green and blue respectively. RGB codes are defined as RGB(xxx,xxx,xxx), where xxx is a number between 0 and 255 each representing the single 8-bit byte value for red, green, and blue respectively.

Search the internet for 'HTML Color Codes' to find the equivalent hex code or RGB code for the color you wish to utilize.
attributes.accessibilityHelpText:
Enhancing graph accessibility through mindful color selection and compliance with WCAG standards is crucial for ensuring inclusivity in data visualization.

Best Practices:
  • Check Color Contrast Ratio: Utilize contrast checking tools to evaluate the color contrast ratio between foreground and background colors. Aim for a ratio of at least 3:1 against adjacent colors to ensure readability for individuals with varying levels of vision impairment.

attributes.helpText:

8052.name: NATIVE_RANGE
8052.title: Range
8052.helpText:
Displays an item with a built-in list of values selector. Each option represents a range of values, from a lower to an upper boundary. The facet supports single or multiple selection, and manual entry.

For single selection support, displays multiple values as radio group options, enabling the end user to select a single value. For multiple selection support, displays multiple values as check boxes, enabling the end user to select multiple values. For manual entry support, text fields will render below the facet, allowing the end user to manually enter the range of values they wish to use for filtering the Filtered region.

For filtering and count computation, the lower boundary of a specified range is always treated inclusive, and the upper boundary is exclusive. Example LOV Syntax:

Less than 100
|100
Between 100 and 500 (exclusive)
100|500
500 and more
500|

For DATE or TIMESTAMP values, use the YYYYMMDDHH24MISS canonical format. The Format Mask is only used for representation on the client.

8052.name: NATIVE_RICH_TEXT_EDITOR
8052.title: Rich Text Editor
8052.helpText: Displays a rich text editor with comprehensive text formatting options. End users can enhance the content displayed in a similar fashion to using a word processor, such as Microsoft Word.

attributes.helpText: Set the minimum height in pixels of the editable area.
Set the maximum height in pixels of the editable area. Leaving this attribute empty will let the editor grow infinitely as you type.
Select the number of text formatting options available within the editor.
Choose whether the toolbar items should only take up one line and overflow into a popup menu if wider than the editor's width, or whether to split them into multiple lines.

For advanced usage only.

As a preferred alternative, embedding snippets of custom HTML can also be done via the "HTML Embed" functionality available in the "Full" Toolbar.

Unless necessary, this setting should be left disabled, as it is only meant to provide backwards compatibility with HTML generated by CKEditor4 or HTML hand-crafted by end users.

This setting controls whether the "General HTML Support" ("GHS") and "Source Editing" library plugins will be enabled or not. "Source Editing" offers the ability to manually change the underlying HTML, while General HTML Support allows for HTML features that are not explicitly supported by any other dedicated library plugin. For example, HTML elements like iframe or video, or custom HTML atrributes like id, if added via the "Source Editing" functionality, would normally be stripped away unless this attribute is enabled.

Under the hood, the General HTML Support plugins would be configured as follows: 

htmlSupport: {
    allow: [ {
        name: /.*/,
        attributes: true,
        classes: true,
        styles: true
    } ]
}

For more granular control, it is recommended to leave this setting off, and instead configure it via the Initialization JavaScript Function. For example: 

function( options ) {

    options.editorOptions.extraPlugins.push (
        CKEditor5.sourceEditing.SourceEditing,
        CKEditor5.htmlSupport.GeneralHtmlSupport,
        CKEditor5.htmlSupport.HtmlComment
    );

    options.editorOptions.toolbar.items.push( "sourceEditing" );

    options.editorOptions.htmlSupport = {
        allow: [ {
            name: /.*/,
            attributes: true,
            classes: true,
            styles: true
        } ]
    };

    return options;
}

lovValues.helpText: Use HTML for the source and output of this rich text editor. HTML is more flexible and offers more formatting options than Markdown, but is less secure and must be trusted or sanitized when displayed.

Use Markdown format for the source and output of this rich text editor. Markdown is more restrictive than HTML in terms of features, but is more secure as it must first pass through a parser before being displayed.

attributes.helpText: Specify the output format of the content entered in the rich text editor.
Specify whether the value shown in the grid view is rich text, or plain text without any Markdown or HTML notation.

    options.editorOptions.removePlugins.push( "Autoformat" );
    // apply a custom toolbar
    options.editorOptions.toolbar = [ "heading", "bulletedList", "numberedList", "fontSize", "undo", "redo" ];
    return options;
}

8052.name: NATIVE_ROW_ACTION
8052.title: Actions Menu
8052.helpText:
Displays the actions icon (hamburger) on each row of an Interactive Grid. The actions menu includes options such as Single Row View, Add Row, Delete Row, and Refresh Row, and so forth, depending on the grid attributes and end user authorizations. These menu options allow end users to perform specific actions on the current row in the grid.

The actions menu can be used in both editable and non-editable Interactive Grids, but the menu options will differ depending on this. For non-editable Interactive Grids, the menu will have a subset of options, for example Single Row View and Refresh Row, and not include editable specific actions like Add Row, Delete Row and so on.

When an Interactive Grid is made editable, the APEX$ROW_ACTION column will be automatically added, and set to a type of Actions Menu. For non-editable Interactive Grids, this column must be added manually.

8052.name: NATIVE_ROW_SELECTOR
8052.title: Row Selector
8052.helpText:
Displays a check box on each row of an Interactive Grid, allowing selection of specific row(s) for row manipulation.

By default the APEX$ROW_SELECTOR column is set to a type of Row Selector. This column is automatically added when the Interactive Grid is made editable.

attributes.helpText: Allow multiple rows to be selected.

8052.name: NATIVE_SEARCH
8052.title: Search
8052.helpText: Displays a text field, enabling the end user to search the list entries of the facets in the Faceted Search region. A Faceted Search region supports one Search facet, which will always be at the top of the list of Facets, regardless of its sequence.

attributes.helpText: Specify whether the search field of Smart Filters is initially collapsed.

8052.name: NATIVE_SELECT_LIST
8052.title: Select List
8052.helpText:
Displays an item with a built-in list of values selector. When the end user clicks the item, the list of supported values displays directly inline with the current item.

Select List is best suited for relatively small, discrete lists. End-Users can very quickly select a value from the list without needing to change focus to a popup dialog. For large lists Popup LOV is often better suited.

lovValues.helpText: No immediate action is taken when the value is changed.
The page is submitted with the page REQUEST set to the page item name.
The browser is redirected to the current page and session state for the current item is set to the selected value.
The browser is redirected to the page contained in the selected value. The return values in the list must include valid page numbers or page aliases.
The browser is redirected to the URL contained in the selected value. The return values in the list must include valid URLs.

attributes.helpText: Select what action is taken when a list value is selected.
Specify whether validations are performed when the page is submitted, based on the page action setting of Submit Page.

8052.name: NATIVE_STAR_RATING
8052.title: Star Rating
8052.helpText:
Modern Star Rating Item

This item displays a numeric value as a number of stars or other icons. The end user can change the value by selecting the desired number of stars. The value can be adjusted by clicking the number of stars with the mouse or by using the keyboard.

The icon to be displayed, the background and foreground colors can be adjusted either in the component settings or in the individual item settings. To use individual items and colors, set the attribute Use Component Defaults to No.

As icons, you may use any icon from the Icon Font available in your application. For Universal Theme applications, use an icon from the Font APEX library.

attributes.helpText: Choose the default color for active stars.
attributes.accessibilityHelpText:
Enhancing star rating accessibility through mindful color selection and compliance with WCAG standards is crucial for ensuring inclusivity.

Best Practices:
  • Utilize contrast checking tools to evaluate the color contrast ratio between foreground and background colors. Aim for a ratio of at least 3:1 against adjacent colors to ensure readability for individuals with varying levels of vision impairment.

Legacy item Used to stop the previous HTML table and start a new HTML table. Before Grid Layout was introduced in Oracle APEX Release xx, this item type was used extensively to tailor the display of page items.

Oracle recommends deleting these legacy item types and updating the Start New Grid to Yes for the next page item displayed in that region. This is functionally equivalent to using a Stop and Start Grid Layout item.

8052.name: NATIVE_TEXTAREA
8052.title: Textarea
8052.helpText: Displays a multiple-row text area.

attributes.helpText: Select how the item value is trimmed after submitting the page. This setting trims spaces, tabs, and new lines from the text entered.

8052.name: NATIVE_TEXT_FIELD
8052.title: Text Field
8052.helpText: Displays a text field.

attributes.helpText: Specify whether pressing the Enter key while in this field automatically submits the page.

Specify whether this item is disabled, which prevents end users from changing the value.

A disabled text item still displays with the same HTML formatting, unlike an item type of Display Only, which removes the HTML formatting. Disabled text items are part of page source, which enables their session state to be evaluated. Conversely, display only items are not stored in session state.
Specify whether the current item value should be sent when the page is submitted.

Select the HTML5 text subtype. This enables devices with on-screen keyboards to show an optimized keyboard layout specific to the subtype, for easier data input. The subtype selection is also used to render an appropriate link with the value of the page item, if it is rendered read only. This attribute does not change the text item, or data entry, when using a physical keyboard.

Note: This HTML5 feature only works in modern browsers. Older, non HTML5-compliant, browsers ignore this attribute and render the page item as a normal text field.
Select how the item value is trimmed after submitting the page. This setting trims spaces, tabs, and new lines from the text entered.
Select how the item value text case is transformed.

attributes.helpText: Whether to use the defaults defined for this component in Shared Components, Component Settings or custom settings.

8830.helpText: Process to close the current modal or non-modal dialog page.

attributes.helpText: Specify whether success messages from processes should be displayed automatically.

Enter the name of one or more page items to be returned by the dialog. For multiple items separate each item name with a comma.

You can access the returned item values by defining a Dynamic Action to fire on the Dialog Closed event on the element that opens the dialog, with an action of Set Value and a Set Type of Dialog Return Item.

8830.name: NATIVE_CREATE_TASK
8830.title: Human Task - Create
8830.helpText: Process creates a human task using an existing task definition from the application.

attributes.helpText: The page item pointing to the Primary Key of the system of records for which this task is defined.

The Task Definition contains the settings of a human task. It includes the Task Subject, Priority, Due Date, Participants, Parameters and Actions defined for a Human Task. The Subject and Priority attributes can be overridden when creating an instance of human task based on the task definition.

Specify if an initiator can approve or reject the task.

Choose on to allow task initiators to approve or reject the task.

Choose off to prohibit the initiator from completing the task.
The ID of the user initiating the task. When not specified, this value defaults to the current logged in user.
The Task Subject which summarizes the purpose of the task. This field can be used to override the subject of the task specified at the task definition level.

The priority of the task. 1 - Urgent - 2 - High, 3 -Medium (also the default) and 4 -Low and 5 - Lowest Priority. This field, when provided, overrides the priority defined at the task definition level.

An (optional) attribute to store the Workflow Variable item to which the outcome of this task will be saved when the task is Approved or Rejected. This is applicable only when the task is being used as a Workflow Activity.

An (optional) attribute to store the Workflow Variable item to which the actual owner of this task will be saved when the task is Completed. This is applicable only when the task is being used as a Workflow Activity.
An optional Page Item representing the Due Date of the Task. When specified, this value overrides the Due Date provided in the Task Definition this Task is based on.

attributes.prompt: Page item containing XLSX Sheet Name

A select list or popup LOV item to display available worksheets in the uploaded XLSX file would use the following List Of Values SQL Query (PX_FILE is the file browse item used to upload the XLSX file).

Note that the SHEET_FILE_NAME attribute must be used as the LOV return column.

       s.sheet_file_name    return
  from apex_application_temp_files f,
       table( apex_data_parser.get_xlsx_worksheets( p_content => f.blob_content ) ) s

Choose On to download all files returned by your SQL Query as a ZIP archive.

Choose Off to download a single file returned by your SQL Query.
Enter a filename for the downloaded ZIP archive.

lovValues.helpText: Saves the file to disk.
Displays the file instead of the current page.

8830.name: NATIVE_EXECUTION_CHAIN
8830.title: Execution Chain
8830.helpText: Execute a sequence of page processes, either in the foreground or in the background.

attributes.helpText:
Pick a page item containing a Context Value to be passed to the background execution. The context value is available in the APEX_APPL_PAGE_BG_PROC_STATUS view, as well as in the record returned from APEX_BACKGROUND_PROCESS.GET_EXECUTION.

When the Serialize switch is enabled, the context value will be used as the mutex for serialization, which means that executions with the same context value have to wait for each other, while executions with different context values can run in parallel.

lovValues.helpText: The execution will wait until previous executions have finished.
If an execution with the same context value is already running, an error is raised.

attributes.helpText: Specify the behavior when a background execution is added, while another execution with the same or a NULL context value is already running.

Enable this switch if the background process should be submitted for execution immediately, outside of the current transaction. If the current transaction is rolled back, the submitted execution remains in the queue. When disabled, the background process submission will be part of the current transaction.
Specify whether to execute this chain in the background.

Specify whether to serialize executions of this execution chain. When set to On, all executions (from all APEX sessions) with the same Context Value will be serialized, to avoid concurrent executions in the background. An execution with a NULL context value will block executions regardless of the context value, and a new execution with a NULL context value will only run, if no other execution of this process is running.

Use this setting when processes of this chain are likely to work on the same resources, for instance, performing DML on the same row in a table.
Choose a page item to return the execution ID into. Based on the execution ID, the current status of the background execution can be fetched.

lovValues.helpText: Neither move nor copy temporary files to the working session for background execution. Choose this option if the background processes will not work with uploaded files.
Move temporary files to the working session for background execution. Choose this option if access to temporary files is only needed by one background execution chain.
Copy temporary files to the working session for background execution. Choose this option if you have multiple background execution chains, and all of them require access to the temporary files.

attributes.helpText:
To execute this chain in the background, Oracle APEX clones the current APEX session; and all background executions will work with the session clone.

Determine how to deal with temporary files, uploaded through a File Browse page item.
Specify a list of page items to move or copy to the session clone for this background execution. If nothing is selected, all temporary files are affected.

If an execution limit is specified, Oracle APEX will raise an error message, if an application user requests more than the specified limit of background executions within the current session. For instance, if a value of 3 is specified, end users see an error message when attempting to submit the fourth background execution. This is useful to prevent users from submitting large amounts of background executions to the server.

8830.name: NATIVE_FORM_DML
8830.title: Form - Automatic Row Processing (DML)
8830.helpText: Process to insert, update, or delete a form region row(s).

lovValues.helpText:
Inserts, updates, and deletes utilize the region source SQL Query .

Note - Ensure columns that are not insertable or updatable have Query Only set to Yes, to exclude them from processing.

Inserts, updates, and deletes utilize a different table or view to the one defined in the region source SQL Query. For example, the SQL Query retrieves data from a table-join or non-undateable view and the DML processing needs to be performed against a single base table or updatable view.

Note - Ensure columns that are not insertable or updatable have Query Only set to Yes, to exclude them from processing.

Processing is based on custom PL/SQL code. This option allows you to execute any PL/SQL code to implement any data manipulation in the underlying database.

This option should be utilized when using database packages, such as table APIs or calls to RESTful Web Services, to implement business logic.

Note - The PL/SQL code will be called for each row that has been inserted, updated or deleted.

attributes.helpText: Select which row processing technique is performed to save data changes made to the Form Region.
Select the table owner (schema) name.
Enter the case-sensitive table or view name. You can type in the name or pick from the list.

attributes.examples:
begin
    case :APEX$ROW_STATUS
    when 'C' then

Specify whether processing should ensure that updates are not lost when multiple users update the same database record.

Lost updates occur when two or more people try to update the same data, and the last update overwrites updates made by the first user to save changes. To prevent this from happening, updates can check the existing column value(s) in the database with the value(s) retrieved when the row was originally queried.

For example:

  1. User A queries employee (EMP) records.
  2. User B queries the same employee records.
  3. User B updates employee details for EMPNO = 7839 and applies (commits) the changes to the database.
  4. User A Updates employee details for EMPNO = 7839 and is attempting to apply the changes to the database.
If User A successfully updates the same row, changes made by User B will be lost. When User A is attempting to save the employee row, then the data in the database is different from what User A queried originally. In step 1 above, the column value(s) originally queried by User A can be captured. Then in Step 4 above, the value(s) can be compared to the current values in the database. This comparison will raise an error for User A, as the database value(s) were updated by User B in Step 3. This prevents a user from overwriting changes made by another user to the same row.

Note

  • How the lost updates are detected is specified in the Attributes for the Form region, based on the setting for Lost Update Type.
  • Lost Update Detection is not available for Form Regions using a REST Data Source and a Target Type of Table/View or PL/SQL Code.

This option exists for backwards compatibility only. New applications should always leave this setting empty. The option "Set Memory Cache on Display" is deprecated and is not utilized in processes generated with this release of Oracle APEX.

When an Automated Row Fetch process selects a row, the corresponding page items are set to the fetched column values. The DML Fetch Mode setting determines when that happens. The default mode updates the in-memory session state immediately when the row is fetched. The mode 'Set Memory Cache on Display' updates this session state only when (and if) the item is rendered. If you need to reference the fetched value of the item using bind variable or v('ITEM_NAME') syntax between the time of the row fetch and the time of the item rendering, you must use the default fetch mode. When you create a new Automatic Row Fetch process, its fetch mode is set to this default mode. Unless your page's logic depends on the 'On Display' behavior, we suggest that you update this process to use default behavior, to give you maximum flexibility to reference fetched column values during page rendering.

Select the column that identifies the version of the row, this column does not need to be present on the page. Leave this attribute blank to use the built-in checksum.

Opportunistic locking uses lost update detection to ensure data integrity in applications where data can be accessed concurrently. Oracle APEX can use a built in checksum to perform lost update detection and determine the version of the row. The checksum is a hash function of all the column values for the specific table row. It is retrieved when the record is queried from the database, and then compared against the hash of the current record in the database as part of Automatic Row Processing. If the two values are the same then the update proceeds, otherwise an error is raised by Automatic Row Processing.

This attribute enables you to specify a single column which holds the row version, as an alternative to using the built-in checksum processing. This column should be updated whenever a record in the database is updated. Oracle recommends implementing a 'Before Update' database trigger on the table to increment or otherwise update the row version column. NUMBER columns are presumed to contain a sequence number for the row. However, DATE and TIMESTAMP columns can also be used. The advantage of using a single column is that the Oracle APEX engine does not need to perform the hash of the complete row, instead it can just compare a single column value.

8830.helpText:
This process type provides Geocoding (turning a postal address to a coordinate) functionality.

Geocoding is performed by calling SDO_GCDR.ELOC_GEOCODE, which does a REST request to the Oracle Elocation Geocoding Service (elocation.oracle.com). For further information on this function, see the Oracle Spatial Developer's Guide.

Geocoding input data comes from page items, which are mapped to address parts like Street, House Number, Postal Code or City. The process populates a coordinate and match vector page item with the results of the first matched address. In addition, all matches can be loaded into a collection for further processing. If Sanitize Address is enabled, address part page items will be overwritten with the sanitized values of the first matched address.

Note - This process type is only supported on Oracle Autonomous Database.

lovValues.helpText: Use a static country from a select list.
Get the country from an application or page item. The item must contain the 2-digit ISO code for a country.

Pick the country to use for geocoding.

attributes.examples:
• US: United States
  • UK: United Kingdom
  • DE: Germany
  • AT: Austria
attributes.helpText: Pick a page or application item to get the country for geocoding from. The item must contain the 2-digit ISO code for a country.

Whether address parts are provided to the geocoding service in a structured or unstructured manner.

Structured means that explicit page items are mapped to address parts like Street, Postal Code, City or Region. This leads to more accurate geocoding results, and also allows to feed the corrected addresses back to the page items.

Unstructured means that only one item is used for the whole address; parts are separated by comma. This mode does not allow to feed corrected addresses back to the page item.

Enable this switch to feed address data from the geocoding service back to the mapped items. If the geocoder returns multiple matching addresses, the first match will be fed back to the configured page items.

Configure a Collection Name to fetch all matched addresses into a collection, for further processing.
Pick the item containing the Street part of the address.
Pick the item containing the House Number part of the address.
Pick the item containing the Postal Code part of the address.
Pick the item containing the City part of the address.
Pick the item containing the Sub Area (within a City) part of the address. This attribute is not passed to the geocoder, but can be received back for address enrichment.
Pick the item containing the Region (State) part of the address.
Pick a page item to store the coordinate of the first Geocoder match, in GeoJSON format.

Pick a page item to store the Match Vector of the first Geocoder match. The match vector is a 17-digit string with detailed information about how each address attribute has been matched against the data used for geocoding.

Match Vector digits can have the following values:

  • 0: The input attribute is not null and is matched with a non-null value.

  • 1: The input attribute is null and is matched with a null value.

  • 2: The input attribute is not null and is replaced by a different non-null value.

  • 3: The input attribute is not null and is replaced by a null value.

  • 4: The input attribute is null and is replaced by a non-null value.


Match Vector digits and the address attribute corresponding to each:

  • 3: Address Point (exact address matched in data used for geocoding)

  • 4: Point Of Interest Name

  • 5: House Number

  • 6: Street Prefix

  • 7: Street Name

  • 8: Street Suffix

  • 9: Street Type

  • 10: Secondary Unit

  • 11: City

  • 14: Region

  • 15: Country

  • 16: Postal Code

  • 17: Postal Add-On Code

  • other digits are unused yet.

If the name of a collection is provided, then all geocoding results are fetched into this collection. The mapping of geocoding result attributes to collection member attributes is as follows:

  • C001: Street
  • C002: House Number
  • C003: Postal Code
  • C004: City
  • C005: City sub area
  • C006: Region (State)
  • C007: Country
  • C011: Match Vector
  • N001: Longitude
  • N002: Latitude
  • D001: Timestamp of Geocoding

Use the following query to fetch geocoding results from the collection:

select c001 as street,
       c002 as house_number,
       c003 as postal_code,
       c004 as city,
       c005 as city_sub_area,
       c006 as region,
       c007 as country,
       c011 as match_vector,
       n001 as longitude,
       n002 as latitude,
       d001 as geocode_date
  from apex_collections
 where collection_name = '{collection name}'

If the collection does not exist, it will be created before the first member is added. Existing collections will not be cleared; this must be done using a separate page process which runs before this geocoding process.
Pick the item containing unstructured address parts, separated by comma.

8830.title: Send E-Mail
8830.helpText: Process sends an email and optionally one or more attachments from the application.

attributes.helpText: Choose an email template to use.
Template placeholder names along with the values, to be substituted.

If a language code is specified, the process will look up the template from an application translation for this language. If no translation exists, the process uses the primary language of the application. Substitution syntax is supported.

Language code hierarchy is supported. If a value of "fr-ca" (French - Canada) is specified, but only a translation for "fr" (french) exists, this translation is being used.

lovValues.helpText: Use HTML escaping. The !RAW modifier prevents escaping for a substitution.
Do not escape substitution values.

attributes.helpText: Whether to escape substitution values in the HTML body.
Enter the email recipients by specifying one or more email addresses. For multiple email addresses, use a comma-separated list. Use substitution syntax if you want to use a dynamic value.
Enter the carbon copy email recipients by specifying one or more email addresses. For multiple email addresses, use a comma-separated list. Use substitution syntax if you want to use a dynamic value.

Enter the blind carbon copy email recipients by specifying one or more email addresses. For multiple email addresses, use a comma-separated list. Use substitution syntax if you want to use a dynamic value.
Enter the subject of the e-mail. Use substitution syntax, such as &P6_PRODUCT_NAME., if you want to include a dynamic value.

Enter the text of the e-mail. The plain text version is used if the recipient's e-mail client does not support rich text display. Use substitution syntax, such as &P6_PRODUCT_NAME., if you want to include dynamic content in your text.

Note: The SMTP/MIME specification dictates that no single line shall exceed 1000 characters. To comply with this restriction, you must add a carriage return or line feed characters to break your text into chunks of 1000 characters or less. Failing to do so will result in erroneous email messages, including partial messages or messages with extraneous exclamation points.
Enter the email address replies should be sent to. If not specified the e-mail address entered in From will be used. Use substitution syntax if you want to use a dynamic value.

Enter text that yields a multi-part HTML message, including both plain text and HTML content. The settings and capabilities of the recipient's email client will determine what displays. Although most modern email clients can read an HTML formatted email, remember that some users disable this functionality to address security issues. Use substitution syntax, such as &P6_PRODUCT_NAME., if you want to include dynamic content in the text.

When referencing images using the <img /> tag, remember that the images must be accessible to the recipient's email client in order for them to see the image. For example, suppose you reference an image on your network called hello.gif as follows:

<img src="http://example.com/hello.gif" alt="Hello" />

In this example, the image is not attached to the email, but is referenced by the email. For the recipient to see it, they must be able to access the image using a Web browser. If the image is inside a firewall and the recipient is outside of the firewall, the image will not display. For this reason, avoid using images. If you must include images, be sure to include the ALT attribute to provide a textual description in the event the image is not accessible.

Note: The SMTP/MIME specification dictates that no single line shall exceed 1000 characters. To comply with this restriction, you must add a carriage return or line feed characters to break your text into chunks of 1000 characters or less. Failing to do so will result in erroneous email messages, including partial messages or messages with extraneous exclamation points.

attributes.examples:
The SQL statement must be in the following format:

select blob_column,
       file_name,
       mime_type,
       content_id
  from table

The columns mime_type and content_id are optional. If content_id is present then the file will be attached inline and the value of content_id will be used for the attachment's CID.

If the content_id column contains the value 'my_inline_content' then that image may be embedded within the email using the following HTML:

<div>
  <h1>Some Embedded Content</h1>
  <p>
    <img src="cid:my_inline_content" alt="Inline Image" >
  </p>
</div>
attributes.helpText:
Enter a SQL statement which returns one or more BLOBs that are attached as files to the e-mail.

If the content_id column contains a null value then the associated files will be regular attachments. Files such as documents or zip archives are generally attached in this way.

If the value of the content_id is non-null then the associated file will be marked as being attached inline. The value of the content_id column will be used as the CID (Content ID) of the attachment. This CID value can be used in the HTML code of the email in order to embed images directly within the email content. Note that some email clients may not automatically display inline attachments. Also note that email standards dictate various requirements for the format of content identifiers. Oracle APEX does not enforce compliance with these standards.

Enter the email address to display as the sender of the email. This email address must be a valid address. Otherwise, the message will not be sent. Use substitution syntax if you want to use a dynamic value.

Specify whether this email is sent immediately. This will also send all emails currently in the Oracle APEX email queue table. By default, Oracle APEX stores unsent email messages in a table and periodically delivers them for better system performance.

8830.name: NATIVE_WORKFLOW
8830.title: Workflow
8830.helpText:
Process to perform the following operations on a Workflow:
  • Start a new Workflow Instance based on the selected Workflow Definition
  • Terminate, Suspend, Resume or Retry an existing Workflow Instance

lovValues.helpText: Start a new workflow instance based on a workflow definition.
Terminate a running workflow instance
Suspend a running workflow instance
Resume a previously suspended workflow instance
Retry a failed workflow instance

attributes.helpText: The Type of the Workflow Operation being performed by this process.
This Page Item is used to specify the static ID of a Workflow Activity from where to resume the Workflow after it has been suspended.
The Workflow Definition.

Page Item specifying the primary key value of the row in the system of records which acts as the source for this workflow. The source is defined in the Workflow Version inside the Workflow Designer.

When executing the workflow, the Detail Primary Key Item will be used only if the source in the workflow version is specified.

When the source of the workflow version is of type Table or SQL Query, then the value of this detail primary key is available in workflow queries or code using the APEX$WORKFLOW_DETAIL_PK bind variable or substitution string.

The Workflow Id Item identifies a workflow instance uniquely. When the Type is Terminate, Resume, Suspend or Retry, this needs to be passed in as an attribute in order to perform those operations on the workflow instance . When the Type is Start, the Workflow Id Item is an optional Page Item where the id of the newly created workflow instance can be stored.

8830.helpText: Process completes the execution of the workflow in which this process has been added as an activity. lovValues.helpText: This is the natural state of termination of a workflow when all its activities are completed.
This End state represents a forced termination of the workflow.

8830.name: NATIVE_WORKFLOW_START

8830.name: NATIVE_WORKFLOW_SWITCH
8830.title: Switch
8830.helpText: Process supports condition-based evaluation to arrive at a certain outcome. It can be used in a workflow activity to decide the next activity based on certain conditions.

lovValues.helpText: Based on the result of a single condition that returns a boolean (Workflow Variable = value, Row (not) Exists, Expression, Function Call result).
Based on the value of a Workflow Variable, the different branches perform a comparison against that value.
Based on the result of a computation (Workflow Variable, SQL query result, Function Call result), the different branches perform a comparison against that value.
If the conditions in the different branches are more complex, use If Elsif Else to perform AND/OR comparison between the conditions.

attributes.helpText: Select the type of switch.

lovValues.helpText: The result of the case expression should be either 'Y' or 'N' or null.

attributes.helpText: The data type of the result of the CASE expression. The result of the CASE expression from the code editor is always expected to be a varchar2, and the data type is applied only at runtime when the case statement is being executed.
The condition types in a True False Check Switch.
SQL or PLSQL Expression that returns a Boolean Value in a True False Check switch.
PLSQL Function Body that returns a Boolean Value in a True False Check switch.
The Workflow Variable to be compared in Check Workflow Variable or True False Check switches.
The type of the CASE condition.
The Workflow Variable used for the comparison.
SQL Query used to specify the condition in a Case Switch.
Expression used in a Case Switch.
Function Body used to specify the condition in a Case switch.

The Value to be compared against a Workflow Variable in True False Check or Check Workflow Variable switches. If the Workflow Variable has a format mask specified, it is expected that the compare value is also formatted according to the same mask.

8830.name: NATIVE_WORKFLOW_WAIT
8830.title: Wait
8830.helpText: Process pauses the execution of the workflow in which this process has been added as an activity. The Workflow resumes execution when the timeout specified by the process attributes, elapses, or when APEX_WORKFLOW.CONTINUE_ACTIVITY() procedure is called.

attributes.helpText: Enter the timeout value in ISO or SQL Duration format. For example, PT2M implies that the Wait Activity will time out after 2 Minutes. P2W implies that the Wait Activity will time out after 2 Weeks.
